findings.title: FDA probe reads system TCC.db, which is readable without FDA: false 'granted' (PureMac, Pearcleaner)
findings.problem:
Full Disk Access (FDA) detection returns "granted" when FDA is NOT granted, because the probe reads the system-wide TCC database, which on macOS 26.6 (25G72) is readable by any app without FDA.

- PureMac `FullDiskAccessManager.hasFullDiskAccess` tries `/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db` FIRST and returns true on the first readable probe (momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083, PureMac/Services/FullDiskAccessManager.swift:17-28). Onboarding polls this every 1 s (PureMac/Views/OnboardingView.swift:19,61-62,179-183), so it shows "Permission granted" immediately.
- Pearcleaner's debug-info block uses `FileManager.default.isReadableFile(atPath: "/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db")` for its FDA line (alienator88/Pearcleaner@7724df7, Pearcleaner/Logic/Utilities.swift:790), so bug reports say "Full Disk Access: ✓ Granted" when it is not.

Local evidence (verified-locally, macOS 26.6 25G72): an ad-hoc-signed app bundle launched with `open` (so it is its own TCC responsible process) got EPERM on ~/Library/Safari, ~/Library/Mail, ~/Library/Messages, ~/Library/Cookies and the per-user ~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db, but `open()`+`read()` of the system TCC.db succeeded and returned "SQLite format 3". Replicated independently by topic-platform-constraints (T-0010). `sqlite3 -readonly` of the system TCC.db shows `com.puremac.app|kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles|auth_value=0` on this Mac, i.e. PureMac is not granted, yet its probe would report granted.

Consequence: the user is told they are set up, scans then silently skip protected folders (Mail/Safari/Messages caches, ~/.Trash) and totals are wrong with no warning.
findings.after:
macontrol probes only per-user paths that are gated by kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles and exist on every account, and treats EPERM (not ENOENT) as "not granted":

1. `~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db` (per-user DB; always exists; EPERM without FDA on 26.6, verified-locally)
2. fallback `~/Library/Safari` (EPERM without FDA, verified-locally; may be absent on some accounts)

Result is tri-state: granted / denied (EPERM) / unknown (ENOENT or other errno), and "unknown" never shows as granted. The system TCC.db is never used as a signal.
findings.how:
- `func fdaState() -> FDAState` doing `open(path, O_RDONLY)`; `errno == EPERM` -> .denied, success -> .granted, else try next probe, finally .unknown. Cheap enough (one syscall) to poll every 1 s while the onboarding pane is visible.
- Unit test is impossible in CI (TCC), so keep a manual check script: build a throwaway ad-hoc app bundle, launch with `open -W -n`, assert probe says denied; grant FDA, assert granted. Script lives at research/bench/fda-probe/run.sh (T-0011).
- Also call the probe once at launch so the app gets registered in the FDA list (both sources rely on the failed read registering the app; observed rows with auth_value=0 in the system TCC.db for apps that only attempted access).
findings.verified: macontrol probes only per-user paths (~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db, then ~/Library/Safari) with open(); EPERM/EACCES -> denied, missing -> unknown, never granted (MacontrolCore/Permissions/FullDiskAccess.swift). Tests: Tests/MacontrolUITests/FullDiskAccessProbeTests (fake home via TemporaryDirectory): emptyHomeIsUnknownEvenThoughTheSystemTCCDatabaseIsReadable, readablePerUserDatabaseMeansGranted, refusedOpenMeansDenied, fallsBackToSafariWhenTheDatabaseIsMissing; AccessModelTests.unknownIsNeverTreatedAsGranted. Deliberate-bug proof: planting PureMac's system TCC.db open() first made 2 probe tests fail (granted instead of unknown/denied); reverted, green. Branch feat/app-shell e87fd5a.

findings.title: Root helper runs bash -c on double-quoted paths: a $(...) filename executes as root; PID-based caller check (Pearcleaner)
findings.problem:
Pearcleaner's root helper is a general "run this bash string as root" service, and the app builds those strings by wrapping file paths in double quotes. Any leftover whose name contains `$(...)`, a backtick, `"` or `\` either fails to move or runs code as root. The helper also checks who is calling by PID, which Apple DTS calls the weak option.

All citations are alienator88/Pearcleaner@7724df7 (14,715 stars, license NOASSERTION per `gh api repos/alienator88/Pearcleaner`, 2026-09-23):

1. **Arbitrary command API.** `HelperToolProtocol.runCommand(command: String)` (PearcleanerHelper/main.swift:13) executes `/bin/bash -c <command>` (main.swift:48-51). The daemon plist (PearcleanerHelper/com.alienator88.Pearcleaner.PearcleanerHelper.plist) has no `UserName`, so it runs as root. It is registered with `SMAppService.daemon(plistName:)` (Pearcleaner/Logic/HelperToolManager.swift:58).
2. **Shell-string paths.** `deleteFiles` builds `"/bin/mv \"\(file.path)\" \"\(destinationURL.path)\""` (Pearcleaner/Logic/UndoManager.swift:129-131) plus `/bin/mkdir -p "..."` (line 109). It joins them with ` ; ` and sends them through `runSUCommand` (UndoManager.swift:236). `runSUCommand` goes to the helper when it is installed (Pearcleaner/Logic/Utilities.swift:855-857) and otherwise to Authorization Services. No path is escaped. A grep for escap|shellQuote|quoted in UndoManager.swift and Utilities.swift finds nothing.
3. **PID-based caller check.** `isValidClient` uses `connection.processIdentifier` (main.swift:86-88). `CodesignCheck` resolves the PID with `SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes(nil, [kSecGuestAttributePid: pid] ...)` (PearcleanerHelper/CodesignCheck.swift:60-62). A PID can be reused between the check and the message. Apple DTS recommends the audit token, `xpc_connection_set_peer_code_signing_requirement` (macOS 12) or `-[NSXPCConnection setCodeSigningRequirement:]` (macOS 13): https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/681053

**Local reproduction (verified-locally, macOS 26.6, non-root, scratchpad only):** I made a file named `leftover$(touch INJECTED_MARKER).plist` and ran the exact string shape from UndoManager.swift:129-131 through `/bin/bash -c`, as main.swift:50-51 does. The command substitution ran (the marker file was created) and `mv` failed because bash had rewritten the name. Through the helper, that substitution would run as root. Any app or download can create such a filename in ~/Library.
findings.after:
macontrol's privileged helper (an SMAppService LaunchDaemon, macOS 13+) exposes a narrow, typed XPC API and never runs a shell:

- `trash(paths: [String]) -> [Result]` and `remove(paths: [String])` only, with no command strings. Each path is passed as data to `FileManager.trashItem` / `removeItem` (or `rename(2)` / `unlinkat`), so filenames are never parsed by a shell.
- The helper re-validates every path on its side: it resolves symlinks and `..`, rejects anything under the protected-path denylist (SIP `restricted` flag, sealed or read-only volume, /System, /usr, /bin, /sbin, /private/var/db, /Library/Apple, ~/Library/Mobile Documents, and others), and accepts only locations the app's scan produced. The app is not trusted to have filtered them.
- Caller check: `listener delegate -> newConnection.setCodeSigningRequirement("anchor apple generic and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = \"<TEAMID>\" and identifier \"<app bundle id>\"")` (macOS 13 API, present in MacOSX26.5.sdk NSXPCConnection.h:118). No PID lookups.
- The helper is only used for root-owned leftovers (e.g. /Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist, /Library/Application Support/<vendor>, root-owned app bundles). Everything the user owns goes through `FileManager.trashItem` in-process, which also writes Finder's Put Back record (verified-locally, see T-0010 report).
findings.how:
- Protocol: `@objc protocol MacontrolHelper { func trash(_ paths: [String], reply: @escaping ([String: String]) -> Void) }`, returning a map of path to resulting trash URL or error. No `String` command parameter anywhere in the protocol, and a review checklist item enforces that.
- Denylist and allowlist live in one shared Swift file compiled into both targets. The helper's copy is the one that decides.
- Test: a unit test feeds paths containing `$(...)`, backticks, `"`, newlines and `..` to the helper's validator and trash function (in-process, non-root, temp dir) and asserts the files move with their names unchanged and no side effects. A second test asserts that a protected path returns an error.
- Caller validation: `setCodeSigningRequirement` on each new connection. A manual check signs a second binary with a different team and asserts that the connection is invalidated.
findings.verified: macontrol has no privileged helper and Safety never shells out: SafetySinkTests.safetyOnlyTrashesAndRestores fails on Process(, /bin/, posix_spawn, system(, AppleScript/osascript in Sources/Safety (mutation M9 proof on T-0044); SinkAuditTests does the same for every other module. feat/safety-trash (T-0044)

findings.title: PureMac bundles Sparkle but sets no feed/EdDSA key: 'Check for Updates' just opens GitHub Releases
findings.problem:
PureMac links Sparkle 2 but never configures a feed, so there are no in-app updates: "Check for Updates" opens the GitHub Releases page in the browser, and the user has to download, unzip and replace the app by hand (which on a non-quarantined Homebrew install also invalidates the FDA grant, see PureMac's own `resetFullDiskAccess` comment at FullDiskAccessManager.swift:104-107).

- momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083 PureMac/Services/UpdateService.swift:18 creates `SPUStandardUpdaterController(startingUpdater: false, ...)`; :26 only starts it if `SUFeedURL` exists; :30-33 otherwise opens https://github.com/momenbasel/PureMac/releases/latest.
- GitHub code search in the repo finds `SUFeedURL` only in UpdateService.swift and no `SUPublicEDKey` anywhere (project.yml pulls the Sparkle package at :3-4 but sets no feed/key).
- verified-locally: installed /Applications/PureMac.app 2.9.4 (Developer ID, notarized per `spctl -a -vv`) has no `SUFeedURL` and no `SUPublicEDKey` in Info.plist, yet carries a 2.8 MB Sparkle.framework with Downloader.xpc and Installer.xpc.
findings.after: macontrol ships a configured Sparkle 2 updater from the first public build: `SUFeedURL` (HTTPS appcast), `SUPublicEDKey` (EdDSA), `SPUStandardUpdaterController(startingUpdater: true, ...)`, a "Check for Updates…" menu item bound to `canCheckForUpdates`, and automatic background checks with the user's consent (Sparkle asks on second launch by default). Every archive is Developer-ID signed, notarized, stapled, and EdDSA-signed by `generate_appcast`/`sign_update`; Sparkle replaces the bundle in place, so the TCC/FDA grant (keyed to bundle ID + Developer ID designated requirement) survives the update. A release build fails CI if either Info.plist key is missing.
findings.how:
- SPM: https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle (2.10.0, min macOS 12). `generate_keys` once; private key stays in the maintainer keychain / CI secret; public key -> Info.plist `SUPublicEDKey`.
- Release script: archive -> `xcrun notarytool submit --wait` -> `xcrun stapler staple` -> `ditto -c -k --keepParent` zip -> `generate_appcast <dir>` -> upload zip + appcast.xml (GitHub Releases or any static host).
- Guard: a build-phase check `plutil -extract SUFeedURL raw` and `SUPublicEDKey` on the built Info.plist, failing Release builds when absent.
- Not sandboxed (Developer ID build), so no Installer/Downloader XPC setup is needed; if a sandboxed variant is ever made, see https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/sandboxing/.

findings.title: Reclaim sizes count APFS clones at full size: 'frees N GB' is overstated (PureMac, Mole, dust)
findings.where: PureMac StorageExplorer.swift:313-327, FileSize.swift:44-66; Mole cmd/analyze/scanner.go:1255-1266; dust src/platform.rs:25-66
findings.problem:
The "frees N GB" / item-size figures count APFS clones at their full allocated size, so the space a delete will actually return is overstated whenever the selection holds clones (Finder duplicates, `cp -c`, Xcode/simulator runtimes, any app using clonefile()). None of the surveyed tools reads a clone-aware size:

- PureMac space explorer sums `lstat` `st_blocks*512` (momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083, PureMac/Services/StorageExplorer.swift:313-327); app/orphan sizes sum `totalFileAllocatedSize` (PureMac/Logic/Utilities/FileSize.swift:44-66). Hard links are deduped in the explorer (StorageExplorer.swift:266) but clones are not.
- Mole sums `min(st_blocks*512, st_size)` (tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd, cmd/analyze/scanner.go:1255-1266).
- dust sums `blocks * block_size` (bootandy/dust@ae5c770, src/platform.rs:25-66).
- grep for PRIVATESIZE / CLONEID / fileContentIdentifier / mayShareFileContent in all three: no hits.

Local evidence (verified-locally, macOS 26.6 25G72, research/bench/size-accounting/run.sh): 8 MiB file + `cp -c` clone: stat/du/URLResourceValues report 8 MiB each, `du -sk` of the fixture dir = 38 936 KiB while true unique allocation = 23 576 KiB (+65 %). `ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE` = 0 for both clone members, 1 MiB for a partial clone with 1 MiB rewritten. Deleting a 64 MiB clone changed free space by -0.04 / -0.05 / -6.61 MiB (3 runs, noise from parallel writers); deleting the last copy freed +63.94 / +64.04 / +61.06 MiB.

Consequence: user deletes "8 GB" of duplicates and gets ~0 back; trust in every later number drops.
findings.how:
- Scanner calls `getattrlistbulk(dirfd, &al, buf, n, FSOPT_ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED | FSOPT_NOFOLLOW)` with `al.forkattr = ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE | ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONEID | ATTR_CMNEXT_EXT_FLAGS | ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONE_REFCNT` next to `ATTR_FILE_LINKCOUNT | ATTR_FILE_TOTALSIZE | ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE`. Buffer order: common, dir, file, fork. Working parser: research/bench/size-accounting/bulk.c.
- Store private size and clone id in the node record (16 bytes/file). Compute "frees now" lazily for the current selection.
- Acceptance test: run.sh fixture; expect clone pair reclaimable 0 when one member is selected, 8 MiB when both are; hard-link pair 0 / 4 MiB; comp.txt 86 016 B.
- Open: cost of PRIVATESIZE on large trees (asked of T-0004); snapshot trapping unverified (no local snapshot on test Mac).
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043, fix round 1 @ 4131bda): ScanEngine.reclaimable() sums ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE, uses ALLOCSIZE for UF_COMPRESSED, charges a hard-linked inode only when all links are selected and a full clone group (CLONEID, CLONE_REFCNT) only when all members are; the rest is sharedElsewhere. A compressed file that shares all its blocks (EF_SHARES_ALL_BLOCKS, e.g. a Finder Duplicate of a decmpfs file, which reports PRIVATESIZE 0 and CLONE_REFCNT 0) promises nothing. Tests: ReclaimTests.cloneFreesNothingUntilItsWholeGroupIsSelected (one clone frees 0, pair frees 8 MiB), partialCloneFreesOnlyItsRewrittenBytes (1 MiB of 8), hardLinkFreesOnlyWhenEveryLinkIsSelected, compressedFileFreesItsAllocatedSize, cloneOfACompressedFileFreesNothing, sparseFileFreesItsAllocatedBlocks. Known ceiling: a fully selected clone group still shared with a diverged clone outside the selection is overstated (no attribute answers it), so the UI says 'about'. The Clean/Trash confirmations must show freesNow (T-0049).

findings.title: Machine-wide overview misses Data-volume-only space (macOS Install Data 12.1 GB, /private/var) -> unexplained System Data (Mole)
findings.problem:
Machine-wide views leave out GBs that sit on the Data volume outside the usual folders, and that space shows up as unexplained "System Data".

- Mole's overview is Home, ~/Library, /Applications, /Library plus fixed insight paths (tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd, cmd/analyze/main.go:183-213, cmd/analyze/insights.go:26-71). A root walk skips `private`, `System`, `Volumes` and others by name (cmd/analyze/constants.go:211-233, applied at cmd/analyze/scanner.go:348).
- Content at the Data volume root has no firmlink (`/usr/share/firmlinks`, 19 entries on 26.6), so no walk of `/` can reach it.

Local evidence (verified-locally, macOS 26.6 25G72):
- `/System/Volumes/Data/macOS Install Data` = 12.1 GB (`du -sk` 12 106 964 KiB). It holds InstallAssistant.pkg.integrityDataV1, UpdateBundle and SFRUpdateBundle, dated Jul 27. `/macOS Install Data` does not exist.
- Also Data-root-only: .Spotlight-V100, .fseventsd, .DocumentRevisions-V100, .PreviousSystemInformation, MobileSoftwareUpdate.
- Per-user `/var/folders/65/…` = 2.3 GiB; `/private/var/db` ≥ 2.0 GiB (readable part, no root).
- Walking `/` naively double-counts instead: `/Users` and `/System/Volumes/Data/Users` share st_dev 16777229 / st_ino 26305.
findings.after:
The macontrol overview adds up to the container, byte for byte:

- Container = sum of volume used + free: Data, System (sealed, one read-only block), Preboot, Recovery, VM, Update, etc.
- The Data volume is walked once, rooted at `/System/Volumes/Data`. Paths are shown in their user-facing form through the firmlink map, so `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/x` displays as `/Users/x`. Data-root-only folders such as `macOS Install Data`, Spotlight and fseventsd appear as named nodes.
- Data volume used minus scanned bytes becomes an explicit "Not readable without Full Disk Access / admin" bucket. It is never silently merged into another category.
- `macOS Install Data` is shown read-only until the platform-constraints task (T-0010) confirms a safe removal path.
findings.how:
- Volume list: `getattrlist` ATTR_VOL_SPACEUSED/ATTR_VOL_SIZE per mounted APFS volume in the boot container. `diskutil apfs list` shows the target numbers: Data 174.6, System 12.6, Preboot 10.8, Recovery 2.6, VM 1.1 GB, in use 202.0 GB.
- Firmlink map: parse `/usr/share/firmlinks` once, as tab-separated pairs of System path and Data-relative path. If the user scans `/`, skip `/System/Volumes` and treat `SF_FIRMLINK` (0x00800000 in ATTR_CMN_FLAGS from getattrlistbulk, verified) as a Data-volume edge.
- Check: the scan of this Mac must report `macOS Install Data` at about 12.1 GB, and scanned + unreadable must equal the Data volume used within 1 %.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): scan(URL('/')) walks /System/Volumes/Data once; Data-only root folders (macOS Install Data, .Spotlight-V100, ...) land under a real /System/Volumes/Data node instead of vanishing. Test: TreeSinkTests.dataVolumeRootIsPlacedAtUserFacingPaths. Engine side only: the Overview (T-0047) has to scan '/' to show them.

findings.title: Mole sizes files as min(allocated, logical): small-file trees undercount ~5% vs du/Finder
findings.problem:
Mole sizes each file as `min(allocated, logical)`. For ordinary files logical is smaller, so it reports logical size and drops the 4 KiB block rounding. Small-file trees are undercounted, and the numbers disagree with `du` and Finder "on disk", which Mole otherwise tries to match (its cache comment reads "v2: analyze deduplicates hardlinked files to match `du`", cmd/analyze/cache.go:27).

Local evidence (verified-locally, lstat walk, research-only script):
- `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules`: 13 640 files, 9 629 of them under 4 KiB. Mole's rule gives 688.6 MiB, allocated is 723.7 MiB (−4.9 %).
- `~/Library/Caches`: 774.2 vs 788.7 MiB (−1.8 %).
- A 1-byte file counts as 1 B, but it occupies 4 096 B.
findings.after: macontrol uses the allocated size (`ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE`) unconditionally for "on disk". This is already correct for sparse, compressed and dataless files: 16 KiB for a 100 MiB sparse file, 86 KB for a 10.4 MB compressed file, 0 for dataless. Logical size is shown only as a secondary "size" column, the way Finder does it.
findings.how: One field choice in the scanner record, with no branch. The run.sh fixture checks it: tiny.txt must be 4 096 and sparse.bin 16 384.
findings.verified: integrator, main c99e07e: sizes come from ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE, never min(allocated, logical). ScanEngineTests.hardLinkedBytesAreCountedOnce expects a 10 B file to count as 4096 B. The merged engine totals the bench fixture at exactly 2,368,040,960 B, the ground truth, in research/bench run.sh (docs/BENCHMARKS.md, results/fixture-v1-summary.json), and agrees with dua and ncdu to the byte on ~/projects.

findings.title: gdu non-interactive totals are nondeterministic: a WaitGroup race silently drops 27 MB (fixture) to 520 MB (~/projects) per scan (gdu)
findings.problem:
gdu's non-interactive scan (`gdu -n`, used by `-s`, `--top`, plain listing) returns a different, too-small total on identical warm-cache runs, with exit code 0 and nothing in the log.

Measured on the bench fixture (research/bench/make_fixture.sh, 300k files; gdu 5.37.0 from Homebrew, M1, 8 threads), five back-to-back runs of `gdu-go -n -p -s --no-prefix .`:
2,333,245,440 / 2,333,446,144 / 2,359,623,680 / 2,332,413,952 / 2,340,519,936 bytes.
The correct value for what gdu can see is 2,359,623,680 (du, dua and diskus agree on it). Up to 27 MB (1.1%) goes missing, differently each run. Scanning one subtree (`wide/`) alone was stable, so it needs many directories being walked at once. Raising `ulimit -n` did not fix it, and `-m 1` still gave one wrong total out of three.

It also happens on a real tree. In run.sh's real pass over ~/projects (469k entries), gdu's first of 3 runs reported 30,340.5 MB and the next two 30,860.8 MB: 520 MB missing. Other tools' repeated runs moved by at most 0.1 MB in the same pass (research/bench/results/real-summary.json).

The analyzer used by the TUI and by `-o` export (`pkg/analyze/parallel.go`, `report/export.go:54`, `tui/tui.go:153`) was stable: `gdu -n -p -o file` gave 2,359,623,680 on 5 of 5 runs. The bug is specific to `TopDirAnalyzer`, which `stdout/stdout.go:67` uses for every non-interactive listing.
findings.before:
dundee/gdu @ 848a5dd (HEAD 2026-09-21; the installed 5.37.0 shows the bug too):

- `stdout/stdout.go:67` puts `analyze.CreateTopDirAnalyzer()` behind non-interactive mode.
- `pkg/analyze/parallel_top_dir.go:84-87`: each top-level dir runs in a goroutine, tracked through `subDirChan`. Nested dirs at `:191-198` get `a.wait.Add(1)` and a goroutine only while the `concurrencyLimit` channel has room. Otherwise they run inline.
- `:137-144` receives every top-level result, calls `a.wait.Wait()` and then reads `topDir.GetUsage()`.
- `pkg/analyze/wait.go`, the home-made WaitGroup: `Init` locks a mutex. `Done` → `check()` unlocks it when the count reaches 0 (`:45-50`). `Add` (`:19-23`) never locks it again. `Wait` (`:36-43`) just `Lock()`s it.

The inferred cause (from reading the code, not instrumented): the nested-goroutine count can drop to 0 while some top-level walks are still running inline. Later `Add` calls do not re-arm the mutex, so `Wait()` returns right away and the totals are read while goroutines are still adding to them.
findings.after:
macontrol's scan must be complete by construction. A total may only come from a finished tree:
- A directory job is registered before it is dispatched: `DispatchGroup.enter()` before `async`, or a Swift `TaskGroup` whose parent awaits all its child tasks. The root result therefore cannot exist until every descendant has finished.
- Each directory's size is folded bottom-up from its finished children's results. Shared counters are only for the progress UI and are never read as the answer.
- A debug invariant: for every dir, `size == own + sum(children)`. The scan also keeps an `incomplete` flag per dir (EACCES, ENAMETOOLONG, cancelled), shown in the UI instead of a silent short number.
findings.how: Add a determinism test to the macontrol engine test suite. Run `research/bench/make_fixture.sh`, then scan the fixture 20 times at full parallelism (and again with 64 threads to widen the race window). All 20 totals must be byte-identical and equal `ground_truth.json` → `visible_to_non_root.allocated_all`. The harness already flags this: `research/bench/run.sh` repeats each scanner REPEAT times and writes `total_stable_across_runs` to `results/*-summary.json`.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): the walk ends when a pending-folder counter reaches 0 and the total is folded from the finished ScanTree (finalizeTotals), never read from a shared counter. Test: BenchFixtureTests.totalAndEveryFolderAreIdenticalOverTwentyRuns (MACONTROL_BENCH_FIXTURE, run 2026-09-23: 2,368,040,960 B and identical per-folder sizes in 20/20 runs); run.sh reported the same total in 3/3 runs.

findings.title: Full-path walkers silently drop subtrees deeper than PATH_MAX (du, gdu, dua, dust, pdu, diskus; ncdu gets it right)
findings.where: file_cmds du/du.c:165-168; dua-lib macos/mod.rs:325-329; diskus walk.rs:92; pdu fs_tree_builder.rs:105; dust dir_walker.rs:275; gdu parallel_top_dir.go:172
findings.problem:
Five of the seven CLI scanners silently skip any directory whose absolute path is longer than PATH_MAX (1024 bytes on macOS). They under-report the space in it, and `ENAMETOOLONG` shows up as a warning at most. Such paths are legal on APFS and do occur, for example in nested node_modules or build outputs.

The fixture's `pathmax/` chain (120 levels, 8,437,760 bytes allocated, `bottom_8mib.bin` at the bottom) is missing from the totals of du, gdu, dua, dust, pdu and diskus. Each reports 2,359,623,680 bytes against the 2,368,040,960-byte ground truth, which is 8,417,280 bytes short: everything below the 1024-byte boundary. Only ncdu, which walks with directory fds, counts it (2,368.0 MB). Exit codes vary: du, dua and dust exit 1, while gdu, pdu and diskus exit 0.
findings.before:
Every one of them builds a full path string and calls a path-based syscall on it:
- BSD du: `ftsoptions = FTS_PHYSICAL; ftsoptions |= FTS_NOCHDIR` with the comment `// rdar://4924219` (apple-oss-distributions/file_cmds du/du.c:165-168). NOCHDIR means fts stats `fts_accpath`, the full path, so the stat fails with "File name too long".
- dua-cli: `fs::OpenOptions::new().read(true).custom_flags(libc::O_DIRECTORY).open(&path)` on the full path (Byron/dua-cli crates/dua-lib/src/macos/mod.rs:325-329 @ cf59618). It then calls getattrlistbulk on that fd, but the open itself fails.
- diskus: `entry.symlink_metadata()` on a PathBuf (sharkdp/diskus src/walk.rs:92 @ 90196e9).
- pdu: `symlink_metadata(path)` (KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage src/fs_tree_builder.rs:105 @ c30e46f).
- dust: `fs::read_dir(&pending.dir)` (bootandy/dust src/dir_walker.rs:275 @ ae5c770).
- gdu: `os.ReadDir(path)` with `path + pathSep + name` (dundee/gdu pkg/analyze/parallel_top_dir.go:172,183 @ 848a5dd).
ncdu gets it right: `std.c.fstatat(parent.fd, name, ...)` and `dir.fd.openDirZ(name, .{ .no_follow = true ...})` (ncdu src/scan.zig:49-52, 242 @ v2.9.2).
findings.after: The macontrol walker is fd-relative end to end. Each directory is opened with `openat(parentfd, name, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW)`. Its entries are read with `getattrlistbulk(fd, ...)`, falling back to `fstatat(fd, name, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`. A node stores its name and a parent pointer, never a full path. A full path is built only for display, reveal-in-Finder and deletion, and deletion is fd-relative too (`unlinkat`). Depth is limited by open fds, not by string length: keep a bounded pool and reopen via the parent chain if needed. Skipped subtrees are flagged, not silently dropped.
findings.how: The fixture already contains the case. `research/bench/make_fixture.sh` builds `pathmax/` (total path longer than 1024 bytes) with an 8 MiB file at the bottom. Test: the macontrol scan total over `research/bench/fixtures/tree` equals `visible_to_non_root.allocated_all` in `ground_truth.json` exactly, and the `pathmax/` node reports all 8,437,760 allocated bytes (13 files: the 8 MiB file plus 12 markers). The path-based tools lose the 8,417,280 bytes that sit below the PATH_MAX boundary. Run it in CI on an APFS runner.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): every folder is opened with openat(parentFD, name, O_NOFOLLOW) and read with getattrlistbulk; no full path is ever built. Tests: ScanEngineTests.pathLongerThanPathMaxIsCounted (6 x 200-byte names, file counted, path bytes > PATH_MAX) and the bench fixture total equals ground truth including pathmax/ (dua/du/gdu lose 8.4 MB there).

findings.title: Serial walkers are latency-bound even when warm: ncdu defaults to 1 thread (8.3 s vs 1.5 s with -t8), du 5.9 s vs dua 0.7 s
findings.problem:
Single-threaded walkers are latency-bound even on a warm cache, because on an 8 GB Mac the tree does not fit in the vnode cache. `kern.maxvnodes` is 120,350 on the bench M1, while the fixture has about 311k inodes and ~/projects about 469k entries. Each rescan therefore reloads metadata.

Fixture, warm, hyperfine means (research/bench/results/fixture-summary.json):
- ncdu (default, 1 thread): 8.27 s wall for 2.68 s CPU (user+sys)
- ncdu -t8: 1.47 s, 5.6x faster, same total
- BSD du (fts, 1 thread): 5.88 s wall for 1.23 s CPU
- dua (8 threads, getattrlistbulk): 0.70 s

A serial scan leaves the SSD queue mostly empty. Parallelism is what hides the off-CPU wait, not raw CPU.
findings.before:
- ncdu defaults to one scan thread: `pub var threads: usize = 1;` (ncdu src/main.zig:83 @ v2.9.2). Parallel scanning is opt-in via `-t NUM` (main.zig:319-321).
- macOS du walks with a single fts stream (apple-oss-distributions/file_cmds du/du.c:165-168, 330). Apple's fts already batches metadata with `getattrlistbulk` (apple-oss-distributions/Libc gen/fts.c:757 @ 71bbe350ab), so bulk attributes alone do not close the gap. Concurrency does.
findings.after: By default macontrol scans with a bounded pool of directory workers: start with the active CPU count, and tune it with research/bench/run.sh. Each worker reads one directory fd with `getattrlistbulk` and queues subdirectories, LIFO per worker with stealing, so memory stays bounded on wide trees. dua-cli 2.45 also switches a directory from bulk reads to parallel `fstatat` when bulk refills spend more time waiting than executing (Byron/dua-cli CHANGELOG.md 2.45.0, crates/dua-lib/src/macos/mod.rs:320-323). Measure whether macontrol needs that.
findings.how: Add the macontrol engine as a line in research/bench/run.sh TOOLS and run `./run.sh both`. On the M1/8 GB reference it must beat dua (0.70 s on the fixture) or come within 10%, with the same total as ground truth. Record a serial run (1 worker) too, so the parallel speedup is measured on this machine and not assumed.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): fixed pool of blocking threads (1.5 per active core, cap 12, halved on Low Power/thermal) on a LIFO stack. run.sh fixture: mcscan 1.259 s vs dua 1.045 s at load 9.6 (1.20x); 0.69 s vs 0.68 s at load 4. Serial (-j 1) took 8.05 s. Test: ScanEngineTests.workerPolicyIsParallel.

findings.title: Hard links counted once per link: pdu by default (+16%), dust in apparent-size mode (see F-0004 for clones)
findings.problem:
Two scanners count a hard-linked file once per link. That inflates totals and tells the user that deleting one link frees space, which it does not.

Fixture (50 small files with 10 extra links each, and a 120 MiB file with 3 extra links):
- pdu default: 2,738.5 MB disk usage vs 2,359.6 MB for du, dua, diskus and dust over the same visible tree (+378.9 MB, +16%). The apparent size is 7,683.9 MB vs 7,295.1 MB.
- dust `-s` (apparent size): 7,683.9 MB. It dedups inodes only in disk-usage mode.
du, dua, diskus, gdu and ncdu count each (dev, ino) once in both modes.
findings.before:
- pdu: dedup is opt-in. `deduplicate_hardlinks: bool` is behind `-H/--deduplicate-hardlinks` and false by default (KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage src/args.rs:112-114 @ c30e46f).
- dust: `clean_inodes` skips dedup whenever apparent size is requested: `if !walk_data.use_apparent_size && let Some(id) = x.inode_device && !inodes.insert(id) { return None; }` (bootandy/dust src/dir_walker.rs:134-139 @ ae5c770).
findings.after: macontrol counts each (st_dev, st_ino) once in every size mode. The first link reached gets the bytes. Every other link is shown with a "shared: N links" badge and 0 reclaimable bytes. Only deleting the last link reports reclaimable space. Hard-linked files whose other links are outside the scanned root keep their full size but are marked "also linked elsewhere (nlink = N)", because deleting them frees nothing. The same rule later extends to APFS clones, via ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONEID as dua does.
findings.how: Fixture test: the macontrol totals over research/bench/fixtures/tree equal `visible_to_non_root.allocated_all` (disk) and `visible_to_non_root.apparent_files` (apparent, files only) in ground_truth.json. The fixture's hardlinks/ dir holds 503 extra links, and both totals must not change if hardlinks/ is deleted from a copy of the tree.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): hard links are counted once per (dev, ino) in allocated and logical totals (the other links are 0 B + .sharedHardLink). Tests: ScanEngineTests.hardLinkedBytesAreCountedOnce, hardLinkOwnerIsTheSmallestPathInEveryRun; mcscan -A reports 7,303,489,524 B = ground-truth apparent size on the fixture.

findings.title: Uninstaller searches ~/Documents and ~/Desktop by name substring and preselects every hit (PureMac)
findings.where: PureMac Locations.swift:49-50, AppPathFinder.swift:216-283 matchesApp, AppState.swift:252-268 scanForAppFiles
findings.problem:
PureMac's uninstaller searches the user's own document folders and matches file names by substring. It then preselects every hit, so user documents that happen to contain the app's name go to the Trash along with the app.

- `~/Documents` and `~/Desktop` are search roots (momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083, `PureMac/Logic/Scanning/Locations.swift:49-50`).
- In the default `.enhanced` mode the matcher is `normalizedName.contains(normalizedAppName)`, and the same for the path-component and letters-only names (`AppPathFinder.swift:243-255`). The only guard is a minimum token length of 5 (`:199`).
- The walk recurses one level below each root (`AppPathFinder.swift:174-181`), so `~/Documents/<any folder>/<match>` is also found.
- `AppState.scanForAppFiles` sets `selectedFiles = urls`: every discovered path starts ticked (`PureMac/ViewModels/AppState.swift:264`). Clicking Remove trashes them, and anything that hits EACCES/EPERM falls through to a root `rm -rf` (`AppState.swift:316-330`, `CleaningEngine.swift:271-274`).
- There are no unit tests for `AppPathFinder`.

verified-locally: I compiled `StringNormalization.swift`, `Conditions.swift`, `Locations.swift` and `AppPathFinder.swift` with a probe `main.swift` that pointed `appSearch.paths` at a temp `Docs/` and `Desktop/`. For app "Sketchbook" (`com.example.sketchbook`) `findPaths()` returned `Docs/Sketchbook Drawings.psd`, `Docs/Sketchbook Projects/` and `Docs/Work/sketchbook-notes.txt`. It did not return `Docs/Unrelated.txt`.

Real-world shape: uninstalling Figma, Sketch, Keynote or Blender preselects "Figma exports", "Blender renders" and similar user work.
findings.before:
Locations.swift:48-51 (PureMac@bef6083)
    "\(home)/.config",
    "\(home)/Documents",
    "\(home)/Desktop",
    "\(home)/Applications",

AppPathFinder.swift:243-245
    let appNameMatch = normalizedAppName.count >= minLen && (isStrict
        ? normalizedName == normalizedAppName
        : normalizedName.contains(normalizedAppName))

AppState.swift:260-266
    appFileScanner(app, locations) { [weak self] urls in
        ...
        self.discoveredFiles = sorted
        self.selectedFiles = urls
findings.after:
macontrol's leftover finder never searches user content folders (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, Pictures, Movies, Music, iCloud Drive). Leftovers come only from Library-type roots, receipts (`pkgutil --files`), containers found by metadata identifier, and curated per-app paths (the Homebrew cask `zap` dataset, see T-0005).

Each hit carries a confidence tier and the reason it matched:
- **exact:** bundle-ID folder or plist, container `MCMMetadataIdentifier`, receipt BOM, or cask zap path. Preselected.
- **name:** name or bundle-component match inside a Library root. Shown but NOT preselected, with "matched on name 'figma'".
- **weak:** company or team-ID match. Hidden behind "Show more".

Uninstall always goes to the Trash (or quarantine). It never escalates a name-only hit to root.
findings.how:
- Root list: drop `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop` and any user-content root from the uninstaller search set. Add a test that fails if one is added back.
- Matcher returns `(url, tier, reason)` instead of `Bool`. Selection default = `tier == .exact`.
- Fixture test: a temp tree with `Documents/Sketchbook Drawings.psd`, `Library/Application Support/Sketchbook/` and `Library/Preferences/com.example.sketchbook.plist`. Expect only the last two to be found and only the plist and exact folder preselected.
- Reuse the probe approach from research/reports/sources/momenbasel-puremac.md (Known problems #1) as the regression check against the source behaviour.
findings.verified:
macontrol's leftover search reads only Library folders (LeftoverFinder), matches identifiers whole or at a dot and names only by case-insensitive equality; name hits are shown unselected (.exactName). Tests: LeftoverTests.userFoldersAreNeverSearched (Sketchbook in Documents/Desktop/Downloads/Music/Pictures/Movies, iCloud, /Users/Shared, ~/.sketchbook never found), exactNameIsShownUnselectedAndSubstringsNeverMatch, CaskOracleTests (zap paths outside Library never found). Mutations M1, M2, M10 make them fail (feat/uninstaller, Tests/UninstallerTests, T-0046 comment).

UI side (fix-clean-uninstall-ui, T-0049 @ ec8d76a): leftover choices are kept per app and per leftover. Each leftover is seeded from isPreselected only the first time it is offered, so a leftover the user unchecked is never re-checked by switching apps or re-scanning. Test UninstallModelTests.switchingAppsKeepsTheUsersLeftoverChoices fails when show() re-seeds (mutation pass B).

findings.title: Cleanup deletes permanently with no quarantine or journal; root pass is batch rm -rf (PureMac)
findings.problem:
PureMac category cleanup is irreversible and leaves no record of what it removed.

- User-level deletion is `FileManager.removeItem` (momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083, `PureMac/Services/CleaningEngine.swift:159`). There is no Trash, no quarantine and no undo.
- Items that fail with EACCES/EPERM are escalated to `do shell script "/usr/bin/xargs -0 /bin/rm -rf -- < <tmp>" with administrator privileges` (`CleaningEngine.swift:271-274`). This is root `rm -rf`, and no per-path `(dev, inode)` recheck runs between allowlist validation (`:213-237`) and the unlink.
- Nothing durable is written. `Logger` is os_log plus a 1,000-entry in-memory array (`PureMac/Logic/Utilities/Logger.swift:33-58`), and a successful user-level delete is not even logged per path (`CleaningEngine.swift:159-162`).
- Defaults make it bigger: User Cache preselects every `~/Library/Caches/*` child over 1 KB (`ScanEngine.swift:139-162`, `isSelected: true` default at `:987`).

Real cost: in issue #142 (https://github.com/momenbasel/PureMac/issues/142) one cleanup corrupted iCloud File Provider state. The reporter could not tell which category did it "because PureMac does not expose a persistent, user-readable log of the exact paths removed". The maintainer closed it saying "Persistent cleanup history and rollback/quarantine did not ship". The README admits that dashboard and scheduled cleanup "can permanently delete data" (`README.md:108`).

PureMac's own CLI already does better (dry-run and identity-since-scan in `cli/Sources/puremac/Core/Cleaner.swift:25-47`), but the GUI never got it.
findings.before:
CleaningEngine.swift:148-162 (PureMac@bef6083)
    let reResolved = itemURL.resolvingSymlinksInPath().path
    guard reResolved == resolved, !hasUnexpectedSymlink(in: item.path) else { ... }
    try fileManager.removeItem(at: itemURL)
    result.freedSpace += item.size
    result.itemsCleaned += 1
    result.cleanedPaths.insert(item.path)

CleaningEngine.swift:271-274
    let quotedTempPath = shellSingleQuoted(tempFile.path)
    let script = """
    do shell script "/usr/bin/xargs -0 /bin/rm -rf -- < \(quotedTempPath)" with administrator privileges
    """
findings.after:
Every macontrol cleanup is a transaction with a journal:

1. **Plan.** Write the selection (path, dev, inode, size, rule id, reason) to `~/Library/Application Support/macontrol/journal/<ts>.jsonl` before touching anything. This is the dry-run output and the audit record at once.
2. **Execute.**
   - User files and uninstall leftovers go to the Trash (`trashItem`) or a same-volume quarantine dir, renamed with an atomic `renameat` from an `O_NOFOLLOW` parent fd. The dev and inode are rechecked on the opened fd.
   - Only rules marked `regenerable: true` (DerivedData, package-manager caches) may be unlinked directly, and those are still journaled.
3. **Record.** Append the outcome per path (moved, unlinked, skipped plus reason) to the journal.
4. **Undo.** "Restore last cleanup" moves quarantined items back. Quarantine is purged after N days or on demand.

Root-owned items go through a helper with the same journal. They are never a batch `rm -rf`.
findings.how:
- Model the engine on PureMac CLI `Safety.canRemove` plus `Cleaner.remove` (MIT): critical-root refusal, identity check, then measure, then act. Add fd-based `openat`/`renameat`/`unlinkat` with `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`.
- Journal format: JSON lines, one per path, flushed before and after. `macontrol history` shows it in the UI.
- Rule schema field `disposal: trash|quarantine|unlink` with default `quarantine`, so data decides and code does not.
- Tests: kill the process mid-clean and verify the journal lists everything touched. Swap a path for a symlink between plan and execute and verify it is skipped and logged.
findings.verified: No permanent delete anywhere: TrashService only calls FileManager.trashItem and journals each move (JSON Lines, fsync per line) for Undo. Tests: TrashServiceTests.trashesUnderTheItemsOwnNameAndJournalsIt, undoRestoresTheSameBytesAndIdentity; SafetySinkTests.safetyOnlyTrashesAndRestores bans removeItem/unlink/rmdir in Safety. feat/safety-trash (T-0044)

findings.title: Space Explorer rescans the subtree from disk on every drill-down and Back; keeps no tree (PureMac)
findings.problem:
PureMac's Space Explorer throws away everything below the current level and rescans from disk on every navigation.

- `StorageExplorer.scan(at:)` walks the whole subtree of the selected folder but returns only its direct children (`StorageScanResult.entries`, momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083 `PureMac/Services/StorageExplorer.swift:112-201`).
- `open(_:)`, `goBack()` and `rescan()` each call `startScan(at:)` again (`PureMac/Views/Tools/SpaceExplorerView.swift:51-68`). Drilling from `~` into `~/Library` and back walks `~/Library` three times.
- The walk is a single-threaded DFS inside one actor: `contentsOfDirectory` plus a separate `lstat` per entry (`StorageExplorer.swift:213-262,313-327`).
- Hard-link dedupe keeps the `(dev, inode)` of **every** regular file in a `Set` (`:92,266`), not only files with `st_nlink > 1`, so memory grows with the file count.
- Each progress update (every 64 entries) spawns a new `Task { @MainActor }` (`SpaceExplorerView.swift:97-101`).

Result: navigation that should be instant costs a full rescan every time. PureMac's list UI is also the only visualization (no treemap), so this engine cannot back a Radix-style map. Timing not measured here (machine under load). Handed to T-0004 as a hypothesis.

Scope note: F-0009 already covers "serial walkers are latency-bound". This finding is about re-walking on every navigation and keeping no tree, which a parallel walker would still get wrong.
findings.after:
macontrol scans once into a compact, persistent tree and navigates it in memory:
- A parallel `getattrlistbulk` walk (per-directory work items on a bounded pool) fills a flat node array: parent index, name offset, allocated size, flags. Directory sizes roll up bottom-up.
- Drill-down, Back, breadcrumbs and the treemap read that tree without disk I/O. "Rescan this folder" refreshes only that subtree, and FSEvents marks dirty subtrees.
- Hard-link dedupe tracks `(dev, inode)` only when `nlink > 1`.
- Progress is coalesced into one MainActor publisher (for example at 10 Hz), not one Task per update.
findings.how:
- Node store: struct-of-arrays, about 32 B per node plus a name arena. Budget and measure it on a 1M-entry home in T-0004.
- A subtree rescan replaces a node range and re-rolls sizes up the ancestor chain.
- Acceptance: after the first scan, drill-down and Back into any folder shows results in under 16 ms with zero `getattrlistbulk` calls (count syscalls with `fs_usage` or a counter in debug builds). Scanning the same tree twice is a bug.
- Keep PureMac's good parts: skipped and inaccessible counters, a "Partial result" badge, dataless (`SF_DATALESS`) skip.
findings.verified: feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e (T-0048): the Disk Map keeps the scanned ScanTree in memory; drill-down, Back/Forward, Up and breadcrumb only change DiskMapModel.focus, and layouts are computed from the in-memory tree and cached per (tree version, focus, style, size, scale). Test DiskMapModelTests.navigationNeverReadsTheDisk runs drill/back/forward/up and both layouts on a tree whose root path does not exist.

findings.title: Scheduled auto-clean pops an admin password prompt and deletes permanently while unattended (PureMac)
findings.problem:
PureMac's scheduled auto-clean escalates to root and deletes permanently while nobody is watching.

- `SchedulerService` ticks a 60 s in-app `Timer` and calls `onTrigger` when `nextRunDate` has passed (momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083, `PureMac/Services/SchedulerService.swift:42-46,73-84`). That is `AppState.runScheduledScan` (`AppState.swift:194-196`).
- After the scan, if `autoClean` is on and the selection is at least `minimumCleanSize`, it calls `cleanAll()` (`AppState.swift:1144-1146`).
- `cleanAll` sends every EACCES/EPERM item to `cleaningEngine.cleanWithAdminPrivileges` (`AppState.swift:950-958`). That shows a macOS administrator password prompt (NSAppleScript `with administrator privileges`, `CleaningEngine.swift:271-287`) at whatever moment the timer fires, and then runs root `rm -rf`.
- System Junk preselects children of root-owned `/Library/Caches` and `/private/var/log` (`ScanEngine.swift:121-131`, default `isSelected: true`), so the admin branch is reachable in normal use.
- All user-level deletes are permanent `removeItem` (`CleaningEngine.swift:159`).
- The LaunchAgent code that would run this outside the app is dead: `installLaunchAgent` has no callers, and `--scheduled-clean` is never parsed (`SchedulerService.swift:99-148`).

`autoClean` defaults to false (`Models.swift:225`), and README:112 says "Scheduled auto-clean remains unattended once enabled".

Harm:
- An unprompted password dialog trains users to type their password into dialogs they did not start.
- Unattended permanent deletion of live-state caches is exactly the #142 failure.
findings.after:
In macontrol, unattended runs are limited by policy, not by UI state:
- Scheduled runs only touch rules marked `unattended_ok` (regenerable, user-owned caches). They never escalate privileges, never unlink directly (quarantine plus journal only), and skip anything that needs root or FDA they do not have.
- Scheduling uses `NSBackgroundActivityScheduler` (or an SMAppService login item), so it runs when the system is idle and not from a foreground `Timer`.
- Root-owned or destructive items found by a scheduled scan become a notification: "3.2 GB ready to review". The user starts the privileged step.
findings.how:
- `CleanContext { interactive: Bool }` is passed to the engine. The privileged path asserts `interactive == true`.
- Rule schema: `unattended_ok: bool`, default false.
- Test: run a scheduled clean with a root-owned fixture in the selection. Expect zero calls to the privileged helper, the item listed as "needs review", and the journal entry `skipped: needs-interactive`.

findings.title: Live-cache guard only covers reverse-DNS names: ~/Library/Caches/* sweep deletes a running app's dotless cache (Mole #1607, ~200 GB/h write loop)
findings.problem:
Mole's generic `mo clean` sweep takes every top-level entry of `~/Library/Caches` (tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd `lib/clean/user.sh:178`). The check that refuses a cache whose owning app is running (`_mole_should_refuse_live_user_cache_path`, `lib/core/file_ops.sh:843`) only applies when the directory name contains a dot (`_mole_user_cache_scope`, `file_ops.sh:207-211`). A cache directory named without a dot (`GIPPseudonymousID`, `CCTClearcutLogger`, `Homebrew`, `pip`, ...) has no known owner and gets no owner or open-handle check. It is deleted while its app runs.

Consequence, from open issue tw93/Mole#1607 (2026-09-22): Gemini.app was running when `mo clean` removed `~/Library/Caches/GIPPseudonymousID` (4 KB). Its identity store then hit NSFileNoSuchFileError and entered an unthrottled retry loop: about 50 MB/s, more than 1 M log lines and about 200 GB written to the SSD in one hour. This is the same class of failure as #1390 (Fusion 360 live SQLite cache), which Mole fixed only for names in bundle-id form.

This contradicts Mole's own stated rule, "The owner probe is tri-state and denies on both 'running' and 'could not tell'" (`SECURITY_AUDIT.md:57`). For a directory without a dot, "could not tell" is treated as "allowed".
findings.before:
tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd lib/clean/user.sh:178 (generic sweep):

    for user_cache_target in "$HOME/Library/Caches"/*; do
        ...
        user_cache_targets+=("$user_cache_target")

lib/core/file_ops.sh:207-211 (only reverse-DNS names get the live-owner gate):

    # Reverse-DNS style only (com.vendor.app). Named trees such as Homebrew
    # stay outside this gate; they have their own process probes. ...
    [[ "$component" == *.* && "$component" != .* && "$component" != *"|"* ]] || return 1

lib/core/file_ops.sh:849 then returns early ("not live"):

    scope=$(_mole_user_cache_scope "$path") || return 1
findings.after:
In macontrol, every cache target has an owner state with three values: `owned(bundleID)`, `unowned-proven` or `unknown`. It is resolved once per scan:
- A reverse-DNS name maps to its bundle id.
- A name listed in macontrol's rule data maps to its declared owner. For example, the rule for `GIPPseudonymousID` names the owner `com.google.*` / Gemini.
- Anything else is `unknown`.

Automatic cleanup ("Smart clean", preselected rows) only includes targets that are `owned` by an app that is not running, or are explicitly declared ownerless by a rule. `unknown` targets are listed separately, unselected, as "Cache of an unidentified app". The user can tick them, and the delete-time gate still applies.

At the delete sink, the gate refuses any cache target that has a file open by any process, whatever the target's name. It takes one snapshot of the open-file table per delete batch and matches it against the target as a path prefix.
findings.how:
- Owner resolution: reverse-DNS parse, then the `owner` field in our rules file, else `unknown`. Running apps come from `NSWorkspace.shared.runningApplications` (bundle ids), refreshed immediately before the delete batch.
- Open-file snapshot without forking lsof: for each pid in `proc_listallpids`, use `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDLISTFDS)` and then `proc_pidfdinfo(PROC_PIDFDVNODEPATHINFO)` for vnode fds. Collect the paths into a sorted set and refuse a target when any open path has `target + "/"` as its prefix. If any of these calls fails, count the target as "in use" (fail closed).
- Do NOT use `proc_listpidspath` on a directory. It matches only the exact path. Verified 2026-09-23 on macOS 26.6: a process holding `dir/sub/held.db` open is returned for the file path, but 0 pids come back for `dir/sub` and for `dir`. Probe: `research/bench/tw93-mole/listpidspath_probe.c`.
- Other users' and root processes are not visible without privileges. Treat that as a known ceiling, which is acceptable because user caches belong to user processes.
- Check: a unit test with a fixture `~/Library/Caches/FooNoDot/sub/x.db` held open by a child process. Expect it to be kept at the sink and not preselected by smart clean. A second test: a dotless directory with no rule is not preselected.
findings.verified:
fix-cleaner-catalog (T-0045 round 2, commit 31e540b on feat/cleaner-catalog). The owner state has 3 values: declared by the rule (CleanupRule.owners, with [] meaning ownerless), read from a reverse-DNS folder name, or unknown. Unknown gets the caution 'Cache of an unidentified app' and is never preselected, though it stays cleanable. The name check covers declared owners plus the matched name, a reverse-DNS sub-id of a running bundle, and the last part of the name for daemons. Open files come from libproc PROC_PIDLISTFDS, matched by 'target/' prefix. A same-user process whose fds cannot be listed fails closed. Cleaner.recheck(items) takes a fresh process snapshot and fresh newestModification right before the trash; the Clean UI must call it (commented on T-0049). Tests: CleanerScanTests.unidentifiedCacheIsNotPreselectedWhileItsAppRuns (Mole #1607 literally: Gemini running, idle unopened GIPPseudonymousID), recheckCatchesAppsLaunchedAndWritesMadeAfterTheScan, fileHeldOpenByARunningProcessIsSkipped (real libproc), InUseGuardTests.uninspectedProcessFailsClosed and ownerStateDecidesTheCaution. Mutations M1, M2, M3 and M13 are caught.

UI side (fix-clean-uninstall-ui, T-0049 @ ec8d76a): CleanModel.confirmReview calls cleaner.recheck(items) right before TrashService and sends only the items that still pass canClean. Held items stay listed as 'Not moved: <reason>' and come back unchecked. Test CleanModelTests.confirmChecksAgainAndLeavesOutACacheWhoseAppStartedSinceTheScan: an injected process snapshot starts Editor between the scan and the confirm, and its cache is left out of the batch. The test fails when the recheck is removed (mutation pass A).

findings.title: Disk explorer keeps only the top 30 children per folder: the rest cannot be seen, searched or deleted, and rows do not add up to the total (Mole, verified)
findings.problem:
`mo analyze` shows at most 30 children per directory once a scan finishes. The rest cannot be seen, drilled into, filtered, selected or trashed, and the view gives no hint that anything is missing: no "N more items" row. The header total still counts the hidden children, so the rows do not add up to the total.

- `maxEntries = 30` (tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd `cmd/analyze/constants.go:8`). `runLiveScan` cuts the final list to that size (`cmd/analyze/live_scan.go:346-348`), and `finishLiveScan` replaces the row list with the cut list (`cmd/analyze/update.go:210-218`).
- Every subtree cached during a scan also stores only its top 30 (`scanner.go:607`, `scanPathConcurrentWithLimiter(..., maxEntries, ...)`). A later drill-down served from cache shows the same cut list.
- `/` filter works only on the rows that were kept (`update.go:724-736`, `model.go:375`). Searching for a known folder that ranks 31st finds nothing.

Verified locally: `research/bench/tw93-mole/zz_macontrol_probe_test.go` was run inside the clone. A directory with 45 subdirectories showed 45 rows while scanning and 30 after completion. total=8 478 720 B, sum of visible rows=7 495 680 B, 983 040 B hidden.

For a disk visualizer this undercuts the core promise: "drill into any folder" does not work for folders like ~/Library/Application Support or ~/Library/Containers, which have hundreds of children, whenever the item of interest is not in the top 30.
findings.before:
tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd cmd/analyze/live_scan.go:345-348:

    sortDirEntriesBySize(finalEntries)
    if len(finalEntries) > maxEntries {
        finalEntries = finalEntries[:maxEntries]
    }

cmd/analyze/constants.go:8:

    maxEntries    = 30
findings.after:
macontrol's scan model keeps every child of every directory, so the full tree stays in memory as compact nodes. Views decide how much detail to draw, but never what exists:
- The treemap and sunburst merge children below a pixel or percentage threshold into one "N smaller items (X GB)" tile. Clicking it expands the tile into a list of all its members.
- The list view is virtualised (SwiftUI `List`/`Table` with lazy rows) and shows every child, sorted by size.
- Search runs over the whole scanned tree, not just the visible rows.
- Rows always add up to the parent's total. Anything not attributable (unreadable, permission denied) gets its own explicit row.
findings.how:
- Node store: a flat struct-of-arrays arena (parent index, first child, next sibling, size, name offset into a string pool). Keeping all children then costs about 40-60 B per node instead of a heap object each, which is the design T-0006 is benchmarking.
- Aggregation into "smaller items" happens only in the view model (`groupSmall(children, minFraction:)`). The scan model is never truncated.
- Check: a fixture with 45 subdirectories (as in the Mole probe) must show 45 list rows, the treemap must reconcile (sum of tile bytes == parent total), and searching for the name of the 45th-largest subdirectory must find it.
findings.verified: feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e (T-0048): the tree keeps every child; the map merges only children too small to draw into one 'N smaller items' element that carries every member, and the side list shows that group as one row that expands to all members, plus a 'Folder entries' row for the folder's own bytes, so rows add up. Tests: DiskMapGeometryTests.everyChildIsDrawnOrListedInSmallerItems (each drawn block covers exactly the folder's children, both styles), DiskMapModelTests.listRowsAddUpToTheFolder (collapsed and expanded rows sum to the folder).

findings.title: Scan cache checks only the root folder's mtime: deep deletes, including Mole's own clean, show stale sizes as final for up to 7 days (Mole, verified)
findings.where: Mole cmd/analyze/cache.go:585-621 loadCacheFromDisk, :138-157 loadStoredOverviewSize; update.go:75-88 scanCmd; scanner.go:359-363
findings.problem:
`mo analyze` shows sizes cached on disk as if they were fresh, even after big deletions deep in the tree, including deletions made by Mole's own `mo clean`/`mo purge`.

- `loadCacheFromDisk` checks only the mtime of the scanned directory itself (tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd `cmd/analyze/cache.go:585-621`). A directory's mtime changes only when its direct children are added, removed or renamed. Nothing deeper affects it.
- Even when that mtime has changed, the cache is still reused if it is less than 24 h old (`cacheReuseWindow`, `constants.go:25`, `cache.go:608-616`). The TTL is 7 days (`analyzerCacheTTL`, `constants.go:17`).
- `scanCmd` returns a cache hit with `stale=false`, so the UI says "Scanned X" and starts no refresh (`update.go:75-88,399`).
- When Home is scanned, `~/Library` takes its size from a JSON snapshot for up to 7 days with no freshness check at all (`scanner.go:359-363`, `cache.go:138-157`).
- The shell cleaners never invalidate the analyzer cache: `grep -rn analyzer bin lib` finds only the binary launcher.

Verified locally with the probe `research/bench/tw93-mole/zz_macontrol_probe_test.go`: a 12 MiB file in `A/B/` was scanned, the cache saved (as `finishLiveScan` does, `update.go:236-238`), and the file deleted. `scanCmd` then reported 12 582 912 B with `stale=false`.

Users act on these numbers, and a "freed 5 GB but the map didn't change" moment destroys trust. Only a manual `r` fixes it.
findings.after:
macontrol stores each persisted scan with the FSEvents event id current when the scan started (`FSEventsGetCurrentEventId()`, per volume via the device's UUID). On launch or drill-down:
1. It replays FSEvents from that id (`FSEventStreamCreate(..., sinceWhen: savedId, kFSEventStreamCreateFlagFileEvents | kFSEventStreamCreateFlagUseCFTypes)`) over the cached root. Every changed path marks its node and all ancestors dirty.
2. It shows the cached tree immediately, with dirty subtrees visibly marked (for example hatched or "updating…"), and rescans only the dirty subtrees.
3. If history is unavailable (`kFSEventStreamEventFlagMustScanSubDirs`, `HistoryDone` without continuity, or an event id / UUID mismatch after a volume reset), it treats the whole cache as stale and says so. It never presents stale data as final.

While the app is open, a live FSEvents stream keeps the model current. macontrol's own cleaner and uninstaller subtract freed bytes from the in-memory tree directly after a successful delete.
findings.how:
- Store `(volumeUUID, lastEventId, scanStartedAt)` in the cache header. `FSEventsCopyUUIDForDevice(st_dev)` detects a reset event database.
- Dirty propagation is O(depth) per event path through a path-to-node lookup (a hash map keyed by path, or by parent node id plus name).
- Check: scan a fixture, quit, delete `A/B/big.bin` (12 MiB) outside the app, relaunch. `A` and the root must show as dirty at once and drop by 12 MiB after the partial rescan, without a full rescan (assert that the rescan touched only `A/B`). The same test runs after an in-app cleaner delete, with no rescan at all.

findings.title: Trash via Finder AppleScript with the path pasted in: a filename runs code (verified), no Automation grant silently means permanent delete, freed size never checked (Tencent Lemon)
findings.where: lemon-cleaner@7ff8676 LMAppleScriptTool.m:37-68; LMDuplicateScanResultViewController.m:920-921; LMRemoveViewController.m:95; QMDuplicateItemManager.m:186-200; QMLargeOldManager.m:455-462; LMAuthorizationManager.m:69-82
findings.problem:
Lemon's "move to Trash" for the large-file and duplicate cleaners runs a Finder AppleScript that has the file path pasted into its source. A filename can therefore run code, a missing Automation grant silently turns the operation into a permanent delete, and the freed size is counted whether or not anything moved.

All citations are Tencent/lemon-cleaner@7ff8676 (6 328 stars, GPL-3.0 per LICENSE.txt:5, API says NOASSERTION; 2026-09-23):

1. **Path pasted into script source.** `LMAppleScriptTool._removeFileToTrash:` builds `set theFile to POSIX file "%@"` with `stringWithFormat` and the raw path, then runs it with `NSAppleScript executeAndReturnError:` (localPod/LemonFileManager/LemonFileManager/Classes/LMAppleScriptTool.m:49-59). Nothing escapes `"` or `\`.
   **Verified-locally (macOS 26.6, as the user, scratchpad only, no Finder involved):** I created a real file named `pic" & (do shell script "touch MARKER3") & ".jpg` and ran only the `set theFile to POSIX file "<path>"` line built the same way through `osascript`. `MARKER3` was created. In Lemon the same line runs inside `tell application "Finder"`, so a downloaded file with such a name that shows up in the large-file (>50 MB) or duplicate (>=200 KB) results runs shell code when the user deletes it.
2. **Silent downgrade to permanent delete.** Both flows compute `toTrash = [LMAuthorizationManager checkAuthorizationForFinder]` (LemonDuplicateFile/.../LMDuplicateScanResultViewController.m:920-921, LemonBigOldFile/.../LMRemoveViewController.m:95). That check returns NO on any AppleScript error, including a denied Automation prompt (QMCoreFunction/.../LMAuthorizationManager.m:69-82). With `toTrash == NO` the files go through `removeItemAtPath:` with no further prompt (QMDuplicateItemManager.m:193-196, QMLargeOldManager.m:459-462). Open issue #149 reports the same.
3. **Success never checked.** `removeFileToTrash:` is a fire-and-forget `dispatch_async` on a serial queue (LMAppleScriptTool.m:26-30), and it only logs errors (61-67). The caller adds `needRemoveItem.fileSize` to `removeSize` straight after queuing it (QMDuplicateItemManager.m:198-199). The "freed" total is what was requested, not what moved.
4. **Side effect on failure.** The script mutes system audio on its first line and unmutes it on its last line (LMAppleScriptTool.m:50,55). If `delete theFile` raises, the script stops before the unmute line (from reading the code, not run here, because running it would drive Finder on this Mac).

Lemon's own comment explains why it went back to AppleScript: the API it tried lost Finder's "Put Back" (LMAppleScriptTool.m:43-48, and its App Store build uses `NSWorkspace recycleURLs`, 69-74). T-0010 measured that `FileManager.trashItem` does write the Put Back record and `NSWorkspace.recycle` does not (research/reports/topic-platform-constraints.md D3, verified-locally). So the reason for the AppleScript no longer holds.
findings.after:
macontrol has one in-process trash call for everything the user owns, and it is synchronous per item:

- `FileManager.default.trashItem(at: url, resultingItemURL: &out)`. It takes a URL, so no script or shell ever parses a filename. It does not go through Finder or Apple Events, so it needs no Automation permission and nothing has to be muted. It writes the Put Back record (T-0010 D3) and returns the real destination for undo (T-0010 D1).
- If `trashItem` throws, that item is reported as failed with the error and it stays where it is. There is no fallback to permanent deletion. "Delete immediately" is a separate command with its own confirmation dialog that names the item count and total size.
- The freed-space figure is the sum of sizes of items whose `trashItem` returned a URL, so it is never the requested total. Failures are listed next to it.
- The app does not depend on Finder Automation, so it never asks for that permission.
- Journaling and undo follow F-0012. This finding adds three things: no script or shell in the path, no silent downgrade, and a freed total counted from real results.
findings.how:
- `Trasher.trash(_ urls: [URL]) -> [URL: Result<URL, Error>]`. It runs off the main actor, calls `trashItem` per item, and gives progress by count. The UI shows moved and failed counts and the bytes actually freed.
- Code-review rule: `NSAppleScript`, `osascript` and `Process("/bin/sh" or "/bin/bash", ["-c", ...])` may not appear in any deletion or scan path. A grep test in CI fails the build if they do.
- Test: a unit test creates files named `a" & (do shell script "touch X") & ".jpg`, `$(touch Y)`, a name with an embedded newline and a name with a backslash in a temp dir. It trashes them and asserts that each lands in the Trash with its name unchanged and that X and Y do not exist. A second test makes `trashItem` fail (read-only volume or a locked `uchg` file) and asserts that the item is reported failed, still exists, and adds 0 to the freed total.
findings.verified: Trash is in-process FileManager.trashItem(at:resultingItemURL:) with the URL passed as a value, never Finder AppleScript or a path in a command string; a failed trash is reported as .failed, never falls back to deleting. The sink audit refuses every scripting door in all of Sources (NSAppleScript, osascript, OSAScript, NSUserAppleScriptTask, SBApplication) and any use of Process outside Uninstaller/Launchd*. Tests: SafetySinkTests.safetyOnlyTrashesAndRestores (no scripting, no Process, exactly one trashItem call), SinkAuditTests.everyWayToLaunchOrScriptIsFound (positive and negative samples; 7 issues with the old Process( token). feat/safety-trash @ 8fee903 (T-0044)

findings.title: Disk-map walk adds 1-2 NSURL iCloud lookups per entry on top of getattrlistbulk: 12-13x slower in a bench (3.8 s vs 0.3 s, 40.9k entries); SF_DATALESS from the same call is free (Tencent Lemon)
findings.problem:
Lemon's disk map walks the volume with `getattrlistbulk`, which is the right API. Then, on macOS 13 and later, it makes one or two extra `NSURL` resource lookups per entry to detect iCloud files. Each lookup builds a new `NSURL` and asks for `NSURLIsUbiquitousItemKey`, so the metadata a single bulk syscall already returned is fetched again, one entry at a time.

All citations are Tencent/lemon-cleaner@7ff8676 (GPL-3.0, study only):

- `LMFileScanManager` defaults `_skipICloudFiles = YES` (localPod/LemonSpaceAnalyse/LemonSpaceAnalyse/Classes/ScanManager/LMFileScanManager.m:59) and hands it to every task (226).
- For every entry, `LMFileScanTask` calls `shouldSkipICloudFile:` (LMFileScanTask.m:191-196). That calls `qm_isICloudFileAtPath:`, which runs `[NSURL fileURLWithPath:path]` and `getResourceValue:forKey:NSURLIsUbiquitousItemKey` (localPod/QMCoreFunction/.../QMExtension/NSFileManager+iCloudHelper.m:12-31).
- For every regular file it calls `qm_isICloudFileAtPath:` a second time (LMFileScanTask.m:218-225) before reading `ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE`, which is already sitting in the buffer.
- The bulk request asks only for `ATTR_CMN_RETURNED_ATTRS | ATTR_CMN_ERROR | ATTR_CMN_NAME | ATTR_CMN_OBJTYPE` and `ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE` (LMFileScanTask.m:110-114). It does not ask for `ATTR_CMN_FLAGS`, which would give `SF_DATALESS` (SDK `sys/stat.h:359`) from the same call.

**Measured (verified-locally, macOS 26.6, warm cache, 2 runs each, machine under unrelated load):** `research/bench/lemon-ubiquity-lookup/walk.m` walks /System/Library/Frameworks (40 904 entries) in a single thread.
- Bulk only: 0.293 s and 0.340 s.
- Bulk plus `ATTR_CMN_FLAGS`/`SF_DATALESS`: 0.301 s and 0.290 s.
- Bulk plus Lemon's per-entry lookups: 3.806 s and 3.944 s.

That is about 12-13x slower, or roughly 85 µs added per entry. Lemon runs `processorCount` workers (LMFileScanManager.m:56), so its wall-clock ratio will be lower. I did not build Lemon, so that ratio is unmeasured.

Two smaller costs come from the same design. Every node stores its own full-path `NSString` next to its name (LMItem.h:16-17, LMFileScanTask.m:178-179). Sizes are rolled up in a separate recursive pass only after the whole walk finishes (LMSpaceMainViewController.m:367-368), so nothing is drawn until the scan completes.

The same loop also sends a Spotlight query for every directory named `*.app`, `*.bundle` or `*.simruntime` (`NSMetadataItem` + `NSMetadataItemFSSizeKey`, LMFileScanTask.m:238-245, extension set at LMFileScanManager.m:60). If Spotlight answers, the package is treated as a file, and its size is Spotlight's *logical* size while its siblings use `ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE`. Verified-locally: `mdls` gives `kMDItemFSSize = 6006599` for /System/Applications/Calculator.app, while `du -sk` gives 3 524 KiB. That logical size is 1.7x the space the app actually uses on disk.
findings.after:
macontrol's walker makes no per-entry Foundation calls on the hot path. Everything it needs comes from the one `getattrlistbulk` buffer:

- Request `ATTR_CMN_NAME | ATTR_CMN_OBJTYPE | ATTR_CMN_FLAGS | ATTR_CMN_FILEID | ATTR_CMN_DEVID` plus `ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE | ATTR_FILE_LINKCOUNT` (and the clone and private-size attributes that T-0009 picks).
- An entry with `flags & SF_DATALESS` is counted as "in iCloud, 0 B on disk" and never opened, so no download starts. `IOPOL_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES_OFF` is set for the scan threads as a backstop (T-0009 report, item 34).
- Nodes store a name, a parent index and sizes in a compact array, not a full path per node. Paths are rebuilt only for the items on screen.
- Sizes roll up as each directory finishes, so the map can draw partial results during the scan.
findings.how:
- Add a bench mode to the T-0004 harness (`research/bench/`), or reuse `research/bench/lemon-ubiquity-lookup/walk.m` modes 0 and 2. The gate is that the walker with `ATTR_CMN_FLAGS` stays within 10% of bulk-only on the fixture tree.
- Correctness test: make a dataless file and assert the walker reports 0 allocated bytes, flags it as cloud-only, and leaves it dataless afterwards (`stat` still shows `SF_DATALESS`). This Mac has no iCloud Drive folder, so it needs a File Provider test domain or a Mac with iCloud Drive. Until then this is unverified.
- Review rule: no `NSURL`, `FileManager` or `mdls`/`NSMetadataItem` call inside the per-entry loop of the scanner.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): SF_DATALESS comes from ATTR_CMN_FLAGS in the same getattrlistbulk call (no NSURL lookups); dataless files count 0 B, dataless folders are not listed, and each worker thread runs with setiopolicy_np(IOPOL_TYPE_VFS_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES, IOPOL_SCOPE_THREAD, OFF). Test: TreeSinkTests.datalessItemsAreZeroAndNotEntered. Real iCloud eviction was not exercised (needs a File Provider).

findings.title: Treemap tile area is ln(bytes)^12, not bytes: a 1 GB item next to 100 GB gets 8.3% of the map (true 1.0%), and anything under ~87 MB is dropped silently (Tencent Lemon)
findings.problem:
In Lemon's disk map, tile areas are not proportional to size. Each child's area is `ln(bytes)^12`, so small items look far bigger than they are and big items look far smaller. On top of that, the map shows at most 30 children, silently drops anything whose weight is under 2% of the largest, and draws one level at a time.

Citations are Tencent/lemon-cleaner@7ff8676 (GPL-3.0, study only), file localPod/LemonSpaceAnalyse/LemonSpaceAnalyse/Classes/Controller/LMSpaceResultViewController.m:
- `setSpaceVie:` takes at most 30 non-zero children (898-903). It runs them through `changeNumToLog:` (918) and passes the result to `YMTreeMap` (`tessellateInRect:`) as the tile weights (927-928).
- `changeNumToLog:` computes `log(x)` multiplied by itself 12 times. It drops every child whose weighted value is below 0.02 of the first (largest) one (987-1000).
- One `LMSpaceView` (an NSView with icon, name and size labels) is created per tile (930-937; `alloc` at 933, `addSubview` at 937). Clicking a directory tile drills in (LMSpaceView.m:111-117). Right-click offers only "Reveal in Finder" (LMSpaceView.m:63-77). The disk-map module has no delete action: a grep for delete, trash or removeItem in localPod/LemonSpaceAnalyse returns only reveal and UI hits.

What this does to the picture (arithmetic on the formula above, `python3` one-liner in the report):

| Child vs 100 GB sibling | True share | Area Lemon draws, relative to the 100 GB tile |
|---|---|---|
| 50 GB | 0.50 | 0.72 |
| 10 GB | 0.10 | 0.32 |
| 1 GB | 0.01 | 0.09 |
| 100 MB | 0.001 | 0.022 |

In a folder that holds 100 GB and 1 GB, the 1 GB tile takes 8.3% of the map when its true share is 1.0%. Next to a 100 GB item, anything under about 87 MB disappears from the map without any "and N more" tile.

The 30-child cap is the same defect F-0016 records for Mole. This finding is about the areas. The size labels are correct. Only the areas are wrong, but the areas are what the user compares at a glance. The table view next to the map shows true sizes, so the two views disagree.
findings.after:
macontrol's map is truthful and still readable:

- Tile area is proportional to the size metric shown in the label (allocated bytes by default, per T-0009). The layout is a squarified treemap, or a sunburst ring whose angle is proportional to size.
- No weighting function sits between bytes and area: no log, no power, no floor. Readability comes from aggregation, not distortion. Children too small to draw are merged into the clickable "N smaller items, X GB" tile that F-0016 specifies, so nothing vanishes and the tiles add up to the parent.
- More than one level is drawn at once (nested tiles or rings, 2-3 levels deep), so the user sees where space is before drilling in. Drill-down, a breadcrumb, Reveal in Finder, Quick Look and Move to Trash all work on every tile.
- Rendering uses one layer-backed view or a Canvas that draws all tiles and hit-tests by rect, not one NSView per tile, so a deep map stays at 60 fps.
findings.how:
- Layout: a squarified treemap (Bruls, Huizing and van Wijk 2000). It is about 60 lines of Swift. YMTreeMap (MIT, Yahoo, vendored in Lemon's Pods/YMTreeMap) is fine to use or port, but its input must be raw sizes.
- Test: a pure-function test gives the layout sizes [100 GB, 1 GB, 10 x 1 MB] in a 1000x1000 rect. It asserts that each tile's area divided by the total is within 1% of its size share, and that the 10 small items come back as one aggregate tile holding 10 MB.
- UI check: in the running app, compare the map and the list for the same folder. The area ranking and the size ranking must match.
findings.verified: feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e (T-0048): wedge angle and tile area are bytes/parentBytes with no weighting; readability comes from the smaller-items merge. Tests: DiskMapGeometryTests.wedgeAnglesAreProportionalAndSumToTheParentShare (1e-9), treemapAreasAreProportionalToBytes (0.5%). Deliberate-bug proof: planting Lemon's ln(bytes)^12 made the treemap test fail 103 expectations (relative error up to 0.48).

findings.title: Cleanup rules load from a user-writable file that wins on version number; the 'signature' is an unkeyed MD5 that fails open, and failed deletes retry as root (Tencent Lemon)
findings.where: lemon-cleaner@7ff8676 QMXMLParseManager.m:17-41,127-153; QMXMLParse.m:36-92; QMSigFileHandler.m:17-45; McFunCleanFile.m:296-302; CmcFileAction.m:14-18
findings.problem:
Lemon's cleanup rules are data (an XML "knowledge" file), and the loader prefers a copy in a user-writable folder over the one bundled in the signed app. The only integrity check is an unkeyed MD5 prefix, and when that check fails the loader parses the file as plain XML anyway. The rules decide what gets deleted, and a failed user-level delete is retried by the root daemon. So any process running as the user can decide what Lemon deletes as root on the next "clean".

All citations are Tencent/lemon-cleaner@7ff8676 (GPL-3.0, study only):

1. **User-writable override.** The rule path is `~/Library/Application Support/com.tencent.lemon/KnowledgeEn/2` (or `KnowledgeCh/2`, or the LemonLite variants) (LemonClener/LemonClener/libcleaner/QMXMLParseManager.m:17,29-41). `startParaseXML:` uses that file whenever it exists (132-139). `parseXMLWithData:` picks it over the bundled `garbage1_en.xml` whenever its `<garbage version=...>` compares higher (`NSNumericSearch`) (LemonClener/LemonClener/libcleaner/QMXMLParse.m:36-83, comparison at 75-76). No code in this repo writes that path (a grep for `Knowledge` finds only the reader), so the updater that fills it is not in the open-source tree (unverified).
2. **Checksum, not signature, and it fails open.** `QMSigFileHandler initWithContent:` takes the first 16 bytes as an MD5 of the rest and returns `nil` on a mismatch (localPod/QMCoreFunction/.../SigFileHandler/QMSigFileHandler.m:23-34). Anyone can compute an MD5, so it proves nothing about who wrote the file. On `nil` the parser feeds the raw bytes to `NSXMLParser` anyway (QMXMLParse.m:87-92).
3. **Rules reach root.** A rule action with no `clean` attribute defaults to `QMCleanRemove` (QMXMLItem/QMActionItem.m:104). `QMRemoveManager` maps that to `McCleanRemoveRoot` (LemonClener/LemonClener/QMCleanerManager/QMRemoveManager.m:88, default branch). `McFunCleanFile` first tries `removeItemAtPath:` as the user, then sends every failed path to the root daemon (localPod/QMCoreFunction/.../FuncOpera/McFunCleanFile.m:296-302 and the array branch after it). The daemon deletes with no denylist. Its only check is that the *first* path in the batch is not `/` (Tools/LemonDaemon/LemonDaemon/FileAction/CmcFileAction.m:14-18).
4. **No path limit in the rule format.** Paths are `type="abs"` with any absolute value, a depth `level` and regex `filename` filters (garbage1_en.xml:114-162, for example `/Library/Caches`, `/private/var/log/`, `/private/var/db/diagnostics`). Nothing in the parser confines them to known cache roots.

The bundled rules are careful: 86 filters, 73 of them excludes, several commented with the incident behind them (1Password, IINA, App Store agent; garbage1_en.xml:2-112). The weakness is where the rules come from and what they are allowed to do, not their content.
findings.after:
macontrol's cleanup rules can never be changed by anything except a signed macontrol release, and rules cannot get past the deletion gate:
