- The rule set is a resource inside the app bundle. It is sealed by the app's code signature and read only from `Bundle.main`, never from ~/Library.
- If out-of-band rule updates are added later, the file carries a detached Ed25519 signature (CryptoKit `Curve25519.Signing`). The public key is compiled into the app. A file that fails verification is deleted and the bundled rules are used. There is no "parse it anyway" path, and a version number alone never makes a file win.
- Rules are validated after loading. Every target must sit under an allowlisted root (`~/Library/Caches`, `~/Library/Logs`, `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData`, `/Library/Caches`, and so on). A rule that points elsewhere is rejected with a log line.
- The deletion gate (protected-path denylist, SIP `SF_RESTRICTED` check, T-0010) runs on every path in both the app and the privileged helper, and it checks every path, not just the first. A rule cannot opt out of it.
- A user-level failure is not retried as root automatically. Root-owned targets are a separate, labelled group that the user confirms, and the helper re-checks them against the gate.
findings.how:
- `RuleStore.load() throws -> [Rule]` reads `Bundle.main.url(forResource: "rules", withExtension: "json")` only. `Rule.validate()` checks the root allowlist and rejects `..`, symlinked roots and bare `/`.
- Test 1: put a rule file with a higher version number in `~/Library/Application Support/macontrol/` and assert it is ignored.
- Test 2: a bundled rule that targets `~/Documents` fails validation, and the load either throws or drops that rule with a diagnostic.
- Test 3: the deletion gate rejects `/`, `/System`, `/usr`, `~/Documents` and `~/Library/Mobile Documents` at any position in a batch, including after a valid first path.
- If signed updates are built: a unit test tampers one byte of a signed rule file and asserts that verification fails and the bundled rules are loaded.
findings.verified: feat/cleaner-catalog: CleanupCatalog.bundled() reads only the resource bundle inside the signed app (no user-writable override path exists), and both bundled() and Cleaner.init run the fail-closed validator, so even a tampered catalog cannot point outside the allowed locations. No privilege escalation exists in the cleaner. Tests: CatalogTests.everyBundledPatternPassesValidation, CleanerScanTests.rulesThatFailValidationNeverExpand (mutation: Cleaner.init without validated() fails it).

findings.title: Depth-2 leftover match selects the whole vendor folder: uninstalling LuLu trashes BlockBlock's data, PyCharm trashes every JetBrains IDE's settings (Pearcleaner, PureMac copy)
findings.problem:
When a leftover match is found two levels under `~/Library` or `/Library`, Pearcleaner selects the match's **parent** folder whenever that parent is not one of 18 standard Library folder names. That parent is usually a vendor folder shared by several apps, so uninstalling one app trashes its siblings' data too. The same code is in PureMac.

All citations are alienator88/Pearcleaner@7724df7 (14,715 stars, Apache-2.0 + Commons Clause, API says NOASSERTION):

- `Pearcleaner/Logic/AppPathsFetch.swift:213-224`: `if isLibraryRootSearch && currentDepth == 2 { ... if !Locations.standardLibrarySubdirectories.contains(parentName) { itemToAdd = parentURL } }`. The comment says this is on purpose ("captures vendor folders like /Library/Objective-See/ instead of /Library/Objective-See/LuLu/").
- `~/Library` and `/Library` are walked to depth 2 (`AppPathsFetch.swift:262-292`), so `~/Library/Application Support/<Vendor>/<App>` is a depth-2 item and `<Vendor>` is selected.
- The parent-wins dedupe then drops the precise child (`AppPathsFetch.swift:669-679`), and every result is pre-selected (`:808`).
- `Conditions.swift:160-165` also force-includes all of `~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/`, `Caches/JetBrains/` and `Logs/JetBrains/` for any bundle id containing `jetbrains`, so every JetBrains IDE uninstall takes all the others' settings.
- Same code in momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083 `PureMac/Logic/Scanning/AppPathFinder.swift:158-166` (derived from Pearcleaner, see T-0013).

**verified-locally** (faithful Swift transcription of the Strict-mode walk, predicate, dedupe and conditions, run on a scratch fixture; `research/sources/alienator88-pearcleaner-repro/repro.swift`, output `out.txt`):
- LuLu (`com.objective-see.lulu`) → selected `~/Library/Application Support/Objective-See` (4 entries), which includes `BlockBlock/rules/rules.plist`.
- PyCharm (`com.jetbrains.pycharm`) → selected `~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains`, which includes `IntelliJIdea2024.1/options/keymap.xml`.
Both pass the delete guard (`UndoManager.swift:24-60`).

Real-world shape: Objective-See (LuLu, BlockBlock, OverSight, KnockKnock), JetBrains (every IDE), Adobe, Microsoft (Office apps share `~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft`), and Google (`~/Library/Caches/Google/<Product>`).
findings.after:
macontrol selects the matched item, never an ancestor it did not match. A vendor folder is offered only when it is provably owned by the app being removed:

- A folder is selectable as a unit only if **it** matched, or every child in it matched the same app, or it is empty after the app's own children are removed.
- Otherwise the UI shows the vendor folder expanded, with only the app's own child ticked (for example `Objective-See/LuLu`), and a note "Objective-See also holds data for BlockBlock". After the uninstall, macontrol offers to remove the vendor folder only if it is now empty.
- Rules never force-include a multi-product vendor root. Per-product paths come from the rule file (for example `JetBrains/PyCharm*`) or the Homebrew zap stanza.
findings.how:
- In the matcher, drop the parent promotion entirely. Store the matched URL.
- Post-pass "collapse to parent" only when `Set(children(parent)) ⊆ Set(matchedForThisApp)`. That is one `contentsOfDirectory` per candidate parent, which is cheap because candidates are few.
- After a successful uninstall, remove now-empty vendor folders (`rmdir` semantics, never recursive).
- Fixture test: `research/bench/uninstall-oracle/fixture.sh` builds `Objective-See/{LuLu,BlockBlock}` and `JetBrains/{PyCharm2024.1,IntelliJIdea2024.1}`. Expect LuLu → only `Objective-See/LuLu`, PyCharm → only `JetBrains/PyCharm2024.1`. The same fixture run through the Pearcleaner transcription shows the defect (regression reference).
findings.verified: Vendor folders are never candidates: only a subfolder named exactly like the app is shown, unselected (LeftoverFinder.exactNames). Items another installed app also claims (same id, more specific id, shared app group, shared content library) carry 'Also used by X' and are not preselected. Tests: LeftoverTests.vendorFolderContributesOnlyTheAppsOwnSubfolder (LuLu vs BlockBlock), itemsAnotherInstalledAppUsesAreNotedAndUnselected (PyCharm vs PyCharm CE, second copy), AppGroupTests. Mutations M3, M9 fail them (feat/uninstaller, Tests/UninstallerTests).

findings.title: Uninstall trashes LaunchAgent/Daemon plists without launchctl bootout: jobs keep running (root daemons until reboot) and KeepAlive respawns (Pearcleaner)
findings.where: Pearcleaner Views/FilesView/FilesView.swift:213-231 handleUninstallAction, Logic/Utilities.swift:363-370 killApp, Logic/UndoManager.swift:62-135 deleteFiles
findings.problem:
Pearcleaner's regular uninstall moves an app's LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plists, privileged helper tools and the app bundle to the Trash without first unloading the launchd jobs. The jobs stay loaded and keep running (root daemons until reboot). KeepAlive jobs then respawn against a binary that is now in the Trash, or that is gone once the Trash is emptied. For a VPN, firewall or EDR agent, "uninstalled" does not mean "stopped".

All citations are alienator88/Pearcleaner@7724df7:

- Uninstall button → `handleUninstallAction` does `killApp(appId:)` and then `moveFilesToTrash` (`Pearcleaner/Views/FilesView/FilesView.swift:213-231`).
- `killApp` only calls `NSRunningApplication.terminate()` on processes whose bundle id equals the app's, and it does not wait for them to exit (`Pearcleaner/Logic/Utilities.swift:363-370`). Helpers with other bundle ids, launchd jobs and XPC services are not touched.
- `moveFilesToTrash` → `FileManagerUndo.deleteFiles` only runs `mkdir` + `mv` (`Pearcleaner/Logic/UndoManager.swift:62-135`).
- `grep -rn launchctl Pearcleaner/` hits only `Logic/Brew/`, `Views/DaemonView.swift` (the manual Services page) and the Sentinel toggle. Nothing on the uninstall path. `LaunchAgents`/`LaunchDaemons` appear only as search roots (`Logic/Locations.swift:87,106-107`).
- `bootout` runs only when the optional "brew cleanup" setting is on and the app is a cask, through `brew uninstall --zap` (`FilesView.swift:311-330`, `Logic/Brew/HomebrewUninstaller.swift:17,29-31`).

**verified-locally** (`research/bench/uninstall-oracle/launchd_probe.sh`, macOS 26.6, a throwaway `/bin/sleep` agent in gui/$UID): after `bootstrap`, the job is `state = running`. After `/bin/mv` of its plist (exactly what Pearcleaner does), it is still `state = running` with the same pid. After the process exits, launchd reports `state = spawn scheduled` (KeepAlive). Only `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/<label>` removed it.
findings.after:
macontrol runs a teardown phase before it moves anything, in Homebrew's proven order (`abstract_uninstall.rb`: launchctl before quit, so that a job does not relaunch the app):

1. **Unload jobs.** For each selected `*.plist` under `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, `/Library/LaunchAgents` or `/Library/LaunchDaemons`, read its `Label` with `PropertyListSerialization` and run `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<Label>` (user) or `system/<Label>` (via the typed root helper). Pass arguments as an argv array, never a shell string. Record jobs that fail to unload and show them.
2. **Unregister login items** that the app registered with `SMAppService`, when they are still reachable from the bundle (open question in the report: whether BTM cleans up by itself).
3. **Quit.** `terminate()` every running process whose bundle URL is inside a selected bundle, wait up to about 5 s for exit (`NSRunningApplication.isTerminated` / KVO), then ask the user before `forceTerminate()`. Match processes by executable path or code-signing identity, never by name substring.
4. **Then** trash the files. Report "stopped 2 background jobs, quit 1 helper".
findings.how:
- `Teardown.plan(selection) -> [Step]` is a pure function over the selected URLs (plists → labels, bundles → running processes), so it can be unit-tested without launchd. `Teardown.run(plan)` executes the steps.
- Integration check: `research/bench/uninstall-oracle/launchd_probe.sh` is the manual oracle. macontrol's uninstall of a fixture app with a KeepAlive agent must leave `launchctl print gui/$UID/<label>` returning "Could not find service".
- The root domain goes through the helper's typed `bootout(label:)` call. It is added to the F-0002 protocol, not as a free-form command.
findings.verified: Order in Uninstaller.uninstall (feat/uninstaller c6677c2): quit (polite NSRunningApplication.terminate, 10 s) -> launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<label> for every in-bundle agent and chosen launchd leftover (exact label, argument array, LaunchdControl.swift) -> quit check again -> one Trash batch. The finding's 'after' (and Homebrew abstract_uninstall.rb:214) puts launchctl before quit, because a job can relaunch the app. macontrol keeps quit first, which is politer than launchd's SIGTERM, and closes the same hole with the second running check: a relaunched copy raises stillRunning and nothing is trashed. A failed bootout stops the uninstall. A job another installed app also uses (AssociatedBundleIdentifiers or its program) is noted and not preselected, so it is not booted out by default. Root daemons: /Library plists are needsAdministrator, and in-bundle LaunchDaemons become a plan note. Tests: UninstallFlowTests.stopsJobsByExactLabelAfterQuittingAndBeforeTrashing (pins quit, bootouts, quit, trash), appRelaunchedBeforeItsJobsStoppedStopsBeforeTrashing, failedBootoutStopsBeforeTrashing, LeftoverTests.agentAssociatedWithAnotherInstalledAppIsNotedAndUnselected. Each fails when its fix is reverted (scratchpad/fix-uninstaller/mutate.py). Updated by fix-uninstaller.

findings.title: Delete guard blocks 12 exact paths only: ~/Library, ~/Documents, ~/Public, ~/.ssh pass, and the user's Locked flag is silently cleared first (Pearcleaner)
findings.problem:
Pearcleaner's only guard before a delete is an exact-string blocklist of 12 system paths plus the app folders. Everything under or next to them passes, including `~/Library`, `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, `~/Public`, `~/.ssh` and `/Library/Application Support`. Before moving files it also clears the user's **Locked** flag (`uchg`) without asking, which removes the one protection a user can set in Finder. So when the matcher over-reaches (F-0011, F-0022), nothing stops the delete.

All citations are alienator88/Pearcleaner@7724df7:

- `validatePath` normalises the path and rejects it only if `blockedPaths.contains(normalizedPath)`. The set is `/`, `/Applications`, `/Library`, `/System`, `/usr`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, `/etc`, `/var`, `/private`, `/opt`, `NSHomeDirectory()` and the user's app folders (`Pearcleaner/Logic/UndoManager.swift:24-60`). There is no prefix or ancestor check, no user-data roots, no SIP/`restricted` flag check, and no check that a path is not an ancestor of the home folder.
- `filterValidFiles` calls `removeImmutableAttribute` on any item where `.immutable == true` and then deletes it (`Pearcleaner/Logic/Logic.swift:504-527,543-546`). That runs for every uninstall and orphan delete (`Logic.swift:474-502`).
- After the guard, the move runs as root through the helper whenever it is installed (`Pearcleaner/Logic/Utilities.swift:855-857`), so file permissions do not stop it either.
- Contrast: PureMac treats `UF_IMMUTABLE`, `SF_IMMUTABLE`, `SF_RESTRICTED` and the `com.apple.rootless` xattr as "protected, skip" (momenbasel/PureMac@bef6083 `PureMac/Logic/Utilities/FileProtection.swift:13-41`).

**verified-locally** (the guard transcribed verbatim into `research/sources/alienator88-pearcleaner-repro/repro.swift`, home mapped to a scratch fixture): `~/Documents`, `~/Library`, `~/Public` and `~/Desktop` all return "allowed". In the same run, the Strict-mode matcher pre-selected `~/Documents/OpenSCAD` (issue #587), `~/Documents/chrome (film simulation)` (issue #571) and `~/.claude` (app named "Claude"), and all passed the guard.
findings.after:
macontrol has one `DeletionPolicy.check(url) -> Allowed | Refused(reason)`, compiled into both the app and the helper. Every delete path goes through it (uninstall, orphans, cleaner, disk map), and the helper runs its own copy (F-0002). It refuses:

1. **Structural roots and their ancestors:** `/`, the volume root, `/System`, `/usr`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, `/etc`, `/var`, `/private` (children are allowed only under explicit cache/tmp/receipt subtrees), `/Library` itself and its standard subfolders themselves (`/Library/Application Support`, `LaunchDaemons`, ...), `$HOME`, `~/Library` and every standard `~/Library/*` folder itself. Any path that is an ancestor of `$HOME` is also refused.
2. **User-content roots and everything under them** unless the user picked the item by hand in the disk map: `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, `~/Downloads`, `~/Pictures`, `~/Movies`, `~/Music`, `~/Public`, iCloud Drive (`~/Library/Mobile Documents`), and dot-folders directly in `$HOME` (`~/.ssh`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.claude`, ...). Uninstall and orphan candidates can never come from here.
3. **Protected by the OS or the user:** `SF_RESTRICTED`, `SF_IMMUTABLE` or `UF_IMMUTABLE` set, the `com.apple.rootless` xattr, a sealed or read-only volume. Locked items are reported as "locked by you, skipped" and are never unlocked silently.

Checks run on the resolved real path (symlinks and `..` resolved) at execution time, not at scan time.
findings.how:
- Implement it as data: three prefix tables plus a flags check, about 60 lines. Match on path components (`/Users/a/Documents` must not match `/Users/a/DocumentsArchive`).
- Unit test (table-driven, temp dir with `chflags uchg`): expect Refused for `~`, `~/Library`, `~/Documents/x`, `~/.ssh`, `/Library/Application Support`, a `uchg` file and `/System/Library/x`. Expect Allowed for `~/Library/Caches/com.example.app`, `~/Library/Application Support/Example` and `/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.example.helper.plist`.
- Regression: run the `research/bench/uninstall-oracle/fixture.sh` cases through the matcher and then the policy. Every "must NOT be pre-selected" row must be either not found or Refused.
findings.verified: Containment, not exact match. An item is refused when it is a protected root or contains one, when it contains a live mount point (getfsstat f_mntonname, compared lowercased), or when it lies inside a never-touch area (Keychains, .ssh, .gnupg, Mail, Messages, TCC, photo libraries, /System, /usr except /usr/local, ...). The Locked flag gives .locked and is never cleared. Tests: ProtectedPathsTests.refusesInsideNeverTouchAreas, refusesRootHomeLibraryAndTheFoldersThatHoldThem, refusesAFolderThatContainsAMountPoint (env-gated disk image), TrashServiceTests.refusesALockedFileAndLeavesItLocked (the flag is still set afterwards). Mutations M1 and M8 on T-0044, N3 on the fix. feat/safety-trash @ 31fc928 (T-0044) Follow-up T-0055 (final-fix, main @ 39b1d2e): a folder holding a locked item is also refused, before the move, as .holdsLocked(<path inside>), so the lock never rides into the Trash with its folder (Clean, Uninstall leftovers and the disk map all go through TrashBatch.trash). Test: SafetyAttackTests/TrashAttackTests.aLockedFileInsideASelectedFolderStays (one and two levels deep; the check removed makes it fail).

findings.title: Glob rules are single-quoted into rm -rf: dry run counts them, clean deletes nothing and reports 0B (mac-cleanup-py #279, verified)
findings.where: mac-cleanup-py core_modules.py:124 Path.__init__, utils.py:21 cmd, utils.py:62-64,92-94 glob guard bypass, core.py:109-187 _get_size, main.py:25-50 cleanup
findings.problem:
mac-cleanup-py's preview and its delete are two different code paths that disagree about globs, so the preview promises space the clean never frees.

- Every `Path` rule becomes the shell string `rm -rf '<path>'` (mac-cleanup/mac-cleanup-py@ba4d6ef `mac_cleanup/core_modules.py:124`), run by `Popen(command, shell=True)` (`mac_cleanup/utils.py:21`). Single quotes switch off shell globbing, so `rm -rf '/Users/x/Library/Caches/*'` looks for a file literally named `*` and deletes nothing. stderr goes to DEVNULL by default (`utils.py:21`, `core_modules.py:94`), so nothing reports it. The quoting was added in commit 8f131675 (2023-03-30) to handle spaces.
- The dry run (`-n`) sizes the same rule with Python `pathlib.glob`, which does expand (`mac_cleanup/core.py:128-187`). So globbed rules count in the estimate but are never deleted.
- 28 of the 91 deletable `Path` literals in `default_modules.py` are globs, and they include the biggest ones: `~/.Trash/*` (:12), `~/Library/Caches/*` (:19), `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/*` (:80), `MobileSync/Backup/*` (:74). This count comes from a regex over the file.
- The "Removed" figure is a `statvfs("/")` free-space delta taken around the whole run (`mac_cleanup/main.py:25-29, 37-50`). It picks up noise from other writers, and `bytes_to_human` prints any value <= 0 as "0B" (`utils.py:114-115`). Nothing checks what was actually removed per item.
- Users hit this. Open issue #279 (https://github.com/mac-cleanup/mac-cleanup-py/issues/279, v3.3.0, all default modules): "`mac-cleanup -n` estimates ~80GB will be removed but after running, it removes 0B".
- The tests pin the string and never test the behaviour: `tests/test_core_modules.py:147` asserts `get_command == f"rm -rf '{path}'"`, and `test_execute` (:196-225) only uses non-glob temp files.

**Verified here** (scratchpad probe that imports the source's own `Path` and `_Collector`, run against a temp fixture only): `Path("<fx>/Caches/*")` gave a dry-run size of 1,052,864 bytes. After `_execute()`, all 4 fixture entries were still there. The non-glob `Path("<fx>/Caches")` deleted the folder.

**A naive fix would open a guard bypass.** The only delete guard, `check_deletable`, returns `True` for any path containing `*` before it checks the protected list (`utils.py:92-94`). `check_exists` does the same (`utils.py:62-64`). Called directly, the source's own function gives `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports` -> False and `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/*` -> True, `~/Documents/*` -> True, `/System/*` -> True. Right now F-0025 hides this, because quoted globs never expand. Unquoting or expanding in Python would make every glob, including globs in custom modules, skip the denylist. Custom modules are arbitrary Python loaded from `~/Documents/mac-cleanup/` by default (`config.py:144, 223-245`), and users run the tool under sudo (#279, #266). The guard requirements themselves are in F-0024. The point here is that they must run on each expanded item, never on the pattern.
findings.before:
mac_cleanup/core_modules.py:121-126 (mac-cleanup-py@ba4d6ef)
    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self.__path: Final[Path_] = Path_(path).expanduser()
        tmp_command = "rm -rf '{path}'".format(path=self.__path.as_posix())
        super().__init__(command_=tmp_command)

mac_cleanup/utils.py:21
    out_tuple = Popen(command, shell=True, stdout=PIPE, stderr=(DEVNULL if ignore_errors else PIPE)).communicate()

mac_cleanup/core.py:180-183  (dry run: pathlib does expand the glob)
    for glob in glob_list:
        for file in path_.glob(glob):
            temp_size += file.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_size

mac_cleanup/main.py:37-49  (result = whole-disk free-space delta)
    free_space_before = self.count_free_space()
    ... module._execute() ...
    free_space_after = self.count_free_space()
    print_panel(text=f"Removed - [success]{bytes_to_human(free_space_after - free_space_before)}", ...)
findings.after:
In macontrol, one resolved plan drives both the preview and the delete:

1. **Resolve once.** The rule engine expands each rule's pattern with `fnmatch` over a directory walk, never through a shell, into concrete `CleanItem`s (URL, dev, inode, allocated size, rule id). The preview UI shows exactly this list.
2. **Delete exactly the list.** Execution iterates the same `CleanItem`s, with no re-globbing and no shell strings. Each item is trashed or unlinked through Foundation/`unlinkat` (disposal per F-0012), after a dev/inode recheck.
3. **Report per item.** Each item records its outcome: removed, skipped plus reason, or failed plus errno. "Freed" is the sum of the removed items' private/allocated sizes (see F-0004), not a volume delta. A volume delta can be shown next to it as a separate "free space change" with a caveat about snapshots and purgeable space.
4. **Mismatch is a visible error.** If preview says N items and fewer were removed, the summary lists the skipped ones and says why. It never shows a silent "0B".
findings.how:
- The `CleanPlan` type is the single source of truth. `preview()` and `execute(plan)` both take it, and `execute` has no path-pattern input at all, so a divergence cannot be written.
- Pattern expansion in Swift: walk the rule's root with a bounded depth and apply `fnmatch(3)` per component (`FNM_PATHNAME|FNM_PERIOD`), so bracket expressions behave like the shell. Note that mac-cleanup-py's `[!Library|var|tmp|Media]*` (`default_modules.py:99`) is a character class, not alternation. Rules that need alternation get an explicit `exclude: [..]` list.
- Test (deliberate-bug proof): fixture `Caches/{a/f1,b/f2}` and rule `Caches/*`. Assert that preview.count == 2 and that, after execute, removed == 2, both paths are gone and freed == the sum of the preview sizes. Reintroduce a shell-quoted `rm -rf` and the test must fail.
- Test: a rule that matches nothing produces a visible "nothing to clean" in the preview, not an estimate.
- The guard (F-0024 `DeletionPolicy`) takes a `CleanItem`, never a pattern. Test: rules `/System/*` and `~/Documents/*` expand to items and every item is refused. If the guard short-circuits on `*`, the test must fail.
- Each rule declares a `root`, and an expanded item must lie strictly inside it (component-wise, after realpath). This is an allowlist on top of F-0024's denylist.
findings.verified: feat/cleaner-catalog: globs expand in-process with fnmatch (CatalogMatcher.expand) into concrete URLs; each match is one CleanupItem whose trashItem is that URL plus its FileIdentity, so what is measured is exactly what TrashService receives; no shell anywhere (SinkAuditTests). Test: CleanerScanTests.globMatchesBecomeConcreteMeasuredTrashItems.

findings.title: Unchecking a file inside a checked folder does not protect it: Clean trashes the whole folder (Mac Sai, verified)
findings.where: Mac Sai CleanActions.swift:46-69,180-204 executeUserClean/prunedToParents; FileListView.swift:146-152 toggle
findings.problem:
In Mac Sai's results list, a folder row and the rows for the files inside it are independent checkboxes. When a user unchecks one file but leaves its parent folder checked, the file is still deleted. Clean dispatches only the folder, and `trashItem(folder)` takes the unchecked file with it. The UI gives no warning, and the unchecked row still looks protected.

- The scanner emits a row for every directory **and** a row for every file below it. For example, User Caches is a recursive `~/Library/Caches` target with no extension filter (iliyami/MacSai@2c9ec77 `Sources/MacCleanKit/Categories/SimpleCategories.swift:9-21`, `Sources/MacClean/Core/Scanner/TargetedScanner.swift:83-131`). `CleanActions.swift:59-68` confirms this in its own comment.
- A row toggle only inserts or removes that one URL (`Sources/MacClean/Views/Shared/FileListView.swift:146-152`).
- `executeUserClean` keeps the selected items, then `prunedToParents` drops every item that has a selected ancestor (`Sources/MacClean/CleanActions.swift:46-69,180-204`). The kept ancestor is trashed whole by `CleaningEngine` (`CleaningEngine.swift:206`).
- User Caches is auto-selected, so this is the default state after every scan (`Sources/MacCleanKit/Models/ScanCategory.swift:147-170`).
- There is no test of `prunedToParents`: `grep -rn prunedToParents Tests` returns 0 hits.

**verified-locally:** I compiled a verbatim copy of `prunedToParents` (CleanActions.swift:180-204) with MacCleanKit's `FileItem`. Items were `[Caches/com.example.editor/, …/offline-drafts.db, …/tmp.bin]`, with everything selected except `offline-drafts.db`. The result dispatched to `clean(.trash)` was `["/Users/u/Library/Caches/com.example.editor"]`, so the unchecked file goes to the Trash with the folder.

The Trash makes this recoverable, but the user's explicit choice is silently overridden. The same pattern would be destructive in any permanent-delete path, such as Trash Bins, which uses `.permanent` through the same pruning (`CleanActions.swift:51-52,70`).
findings.after:
In macontrol, the selection is a tree and a deselection always wins.

- Results are a tree (folder, then its children), not a flat list that contains both. Folder checkboxes are tri-state and derived from their children. Unchecking a child turns the parent to "mixed".
- The deletion plan is built from the tree:
  - A **fully** selected folder is deleted as one unit.
  - For a **mixed** folder, the plan lists only its selected descendants. The folder itself is never passed to `trashItem`/`unlinkat`.
- Before execution, the planner asserts that no path the user deselected sits under any planned deletion. If one does, it refuses and logs the conflict.
- The confirmation sheet shows "N items, M kept inside partially selected folders".
findings.how:
- Model: `SelectionTree`, with per-node state `all | none | mixed` computed bottom-up. Toggling a node sets its subtree and then recomputes its ancestors.
- Plan: `plan(tree) -> [URL]`. Emit a node when its state is `.all` and its parent's state is not `.all`. Recurse into `.mixed` nodes. This is O(n) with no prefix scans.
- Guard: `precondition(deselected.allSatisfy { d in !plan.contains { d.isDescendant(of: $0) } })`, implemented with a sorted-prefix sweep.
- Test: build a fixture folder with 3 files, uncheck 1, and run the plan. Expect exactly the 2 checked files and not the folder. Mutation proof: switching the plan to "emit the folder if any child is selected" must fail the test.
findings.verified: TrashItem.keep: the folder goes to the Trash piece by piece. Safety descends only into folders that hold a kept path, so unchecked descendants stay. The keeps of all items are one set per batch, applied to every item and its pieces before the trashed-ancestor shortcut, so a deselection also holds against another selected item that covers it, from below or from above; an item at or inside a kept path is not moved. Fail closed: if any keep URL in the batch cannot be resolved, nothing in the batch is moved. Keep paths are compared without case, as APFS compares names. An item with nothing moved still reports its own outcome. Tests: TrashServiceTests.keepsUncheckedDescendants, keepSurvivesWhenItsFolderCannotBeOpened, keepSurvivesWhenTheItemIsSpelledInAnotherCase, anItemWithNothingLeftToMoveReportsItself, keepHoldsAgainstASelectedDescendant, keepHoldsAgainstASelectedAncestor (both fail with per-item keep restored). feat/safety-trash @ 8fee903 (T-0044)

findings.title: Pre-checked 'junk' includes iOS device backups, Xcode Archives and the whole CoreSimulator/Devices folder (Mac Sai)
findings.where: Mac Sai SimpleCategories.swift:107-119,152-163; ScanCategory.swift:147-170 autoSelect; SmartScanCleanup.swift:20-26
findings.problem:
Mac Sai's System Junk auto-selects some categories that contain user data. Smart Scan pre-checks every item in those categories (iliyami/MacSai@2c9ec77 `Sources/MacClean/Views/SmartScan/SmartScanCleanup.swift:20-26`). One click on Clean moves them to the Trash.

- **iOS device backups:** every entry in `~/Library/Application Support/MobileSync/Backup` older than 30 days (`Sources/MacCleanKit/Categories/SimpleCategories.swift:107-119`). This is often the user's only backup of a phone. It is old *because* the user backs up rarely.
- **Xcode junk:** lists the top level of `Xcode/Archives` and `Developer/CoreSimulator` non-recursively (`SimpleCategories.swift:152-163`, paths `Constants.swift:132-136`).
  - Archives hold shipped builds and dSYMs, which are needed to symbolicate crash reports.
  - In `CoreSimulator`, the whole `Devices` folder becomes one pre-checked row: every simulator, with its app data and keychains.
  - These sit next to `DerivedData`, which really is safe to delete, in the same category with a single `autoSelect`.
- `autoSelect` is per **category**, and it defaults to `true` for `iosDeviceBackups`, `xcodeJunk` and `documentVersions` (`Sources/MacCleanKit/Models/ScanCategory.swift:147-170`). Only large/old files, duplicates, universal binaries, leftovers, deleted users and developer caches are opted out.
- The category subtitle calls this "junk", and there is no per-row risk label.

Trash-first keeps it recoverable until the Trash is emptied. Mac Sai's own Trash Bins module empties it with `.permanent` (`Sources/MacClean/CleanActions.swift:51-52`), and "cleaned up X GB" suggests the space was freed.
findings.before:

               minAge: 30 * 24 * 3600 // older than 30 days

    ScanTarget(path: MCConstants.xcodeDeviceSupport, recursive: false),
    ScanTarget(path: MCConstants.coreSimulator, recursive: false),

ScanCategory.swift:147-170
