            false
        default:
            true      // includes .iosDeviceBackups, .xcodeJunk, .documentVersions
findings.after:
In macontrol, the risk tier belongs to each rule target, not to the category. Items that hold user data are never pre-selected.

- Each rule target in the JSON rule file carries `risk: regenerable | rebuildable | user-data`. Only `regenerable` targets are pre-checked. Examples: `DerivedData`, `CoreSimulator/Caches`, `iOS DeviceSupport` older than the newest-used OS.
- **iOS backups:** shown as a separate "Device backups" group with device name, date and size, read from each backup's `Info.plist`. Never pre-checked. The newest backup per device is marked "latest", and deleting it needs a second confirmation.
- **Xcode Archives:** shown per `.xcarchive` with app name, version and date. Never pre-checked.
- **Simulators:** never delete `CoreSimulator/Devices` as a folder. Offer "Delete unavailable simulators" (`xcrun simctl delete unavailable`) and per-device rows showing their runtime. The `Caches` part stays a pre-checked regenerable item.
- The clean summary says "moved to Trash: X GB (not freed until the Trash is emptied)".
findings.how:
- Add `risk` to the rule schema (T-0003/T-0008 reuse plan) and derive `preselected = (risk == .regenerable)`. Make it impossible to set `preselected` for `user-data` targets: the loader fails when it is set.
- Split the Xcode rule into targets: DerivedData (regenerable), DeviceSupport (rebuildable, with a per-OS row), Archives (user-data), CoreSimulator/Caches (regenerable), Devices (via `simctl`).
- Test: a fixture home with `MobileSync/Backup/<udid>` aged 40 days and `Xcode/Archives/2026-01-01/App.xcarchive`. Run the scan and assert that both are listed and neither is in the default selection. Mutation proof: flipping `risk` to `regenerable` must fail the test.
findings.verified: feat/cleaner-catalog: device backups, Xcode Archives and macOS Install Data are safety=manual (never preselected, CleanupItem.canClean == false); no rule matches CoreSimulator/Devices, only CoreSimulator/Caches/*. Tests: CatalogTests.irreplaceableDataIsManual, simulatorDevicesAreNeverMatched; CleanerScanTests.manualItemsAreSizedButNeverCleanable.

findings.title: Disk map sizes every .app/.photoslibrary/package as 0 B (skipsPackageDescendants + directories counted 0) (Mac Sai, verified)
findings.problem:
Mac Sai's disk map (Space Lens) gives every package a size of 0 bytes. That covers `.app` bundles, `.photoslibrary`, `.bundle` and `.xcarchive`. The largest items in a typical home therefore disappear from the treemap or sink to the bottom, and parent totals are too small.

- `FileTreeScanner.scanWithSizeAggregation` enumerates with `options: [.skipsPackageDescendants]`, so a package's contents are never visited (iliyami/MacSai@2c9ec77 `Sources/MacClean/Core/Scanner/FileTreeScanner.swift:47-51`).
- The package itself is a directory, and directories are recorded as `size: isDir ? 0 : size` (`FileTreeScanner.swift:88-96`), because `totalFileAllocatedSize` is nil for directories. Nothing adds the package's size back.
- The treemap sorts children by `totalSize` and keeps the top 50 (`Sources/MacClean/Views/Files/SpaceLensView.swift:224-226`), so a 0 B package is dropped or drawn as nothing.
- The file-type color for `.app` never applies, because `category(forFileExtension:isDirectory:)` returns `.folders` for any directory first (`Sources/MacCleanKit/SquarifiedTreemap.swift:34-35`).
- `FileTreeScannerAggregationTests` has no package fixture.

**verified-locally:** a fixture with `Foo.app/Contents/MacOS/big.bin` (8 MiB) and `plain/big.bin` (8 MiB) plus a hard link to it. A harness that mirrors lines 47-108 reported `Foo.app: 0` and `plain: 16777216`: the package counted 0, and the hard-linked file counted twice (F-0010 class).

Every drill-down, up and breadcrumb click also re-walks the folder from disk with no retained tree (`SpaceLensView.swift:67,71,78-79,188-191,216-241`). That part is covered by F-0013 (PureMac) and noted there.
findings.after:
macontrol's scanner always descends into packages for sizing, and the map decides how to *show* them.

- The walk enters every directory, packages included. A package node carries `isPackage = true`, and its subtree size rolls up like any folder's.
- In the map a package is drawn as one leaf tile with its full size and its own color (Applications, Photos Library, ...). Drill-down into it is opt-in ("Show Package Contents"), as in Finder.
- Sizes are allocated bytes with `(dev, ino)` de-duplicated when `nlink > 1` (F-0010), and clones handled per F-0004.
- The rule: the sum of a folder's children plus its own allocation equals its total. A test enforces it.
findings.how:
- Scanner: do not pass `skipsPackageDescendants` (or its getattrlistbulk equivalent) for the sizing walk. Record `isPackage` from `ATTR_CMN_FNDRINFO`/UTType at node creation.
- Model: `Node.isPackage` makes the node render as a leaf in the treemap and list, while its `totalSize` includes its descendants.
- Test: a fixture with `Foo.app` holding an 8 MiB file and `Bar.photoslibrary` holding a 4 MiB file. Assert that the root total is at least 12 MiB, `Foo.app.totalSize >= 8 MiB`, and both appear as tiles. Mutation proof: re-adding `skipsPackageDescendants` must fail the test.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): package folders are walked like any folder and flagged .package (UTType conforming to com.apple.package, cached per extension). Test: ScanEngineTests.packagesAreSizedInFull (Demo.app = 135,168 B, flagged; plain.folder.v2 not flagged).

findings.title: External tools run via shell with no timeout, hidden stderr and inline sudo: runs hang behind the spinner (mac-cleanup-py #192, #272, #211)
findings.where: mac-cleanup-py utils.py:21 cmd, core_modules.py:94 ignore_errors default, default_modules.py:246-299,420-430, progress.py:25-34
findings.problem:
mac-cleanup-py runs every external step as a blocking shell command with no timeout, no stdin policy and no visible output, so one tool waiting for input freezes the whole run behind a spinner.

- `cmd()` is `Popen(command, shell=True, stdout=PIPE, stderr=DEVNULL-or-PIPE).communicate()` (mac-cleanup/mac-cleanup-py@ba4d6ef `mac_cleanup/utils.py:21`). It has no `timeout=`, and stdin is inherited from the terminal. `Command` defaults to `ignore_errors=True`, so stderr goes to DEVNULL (`core_modules.py:94, 111`), and that is where most CLIs print their questions.
- These commands run while a rich `Progress` live display redraws the same terminal (`progress.py:25-34`, `main.py:39-42`). No command output is ever shown to the user.
- Default modules shell out to privileged or interactive tools: `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache`, `sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder` (`default_modules.py:423-424`), `sudo purge` (:430), `brew cleanup -s` / `brew update && brew upgrade` (:256, :263), `docker system prune -af` after silently starting Docker Desktop with `open -jga Docker` (:285-299), and `yarn cache clean --force` (:337). Cancellation is Ctrl-C only (`error_handling.py:33-41`).
- User reports of indefinite hangs: #192 "Stuck on 'Cleaning up DNS cache'" (open, 25 comments, https://github.com/mac-cleanup/mac-cleanup-py/issues/192). #272 "Purging inactive memory stuck" (the `sudo purge` module, closed as a duplicate of #192). #211 "Getting stuck on 'Cleaning up Yarn Cache'". In #211 the reporter later found that yarn needed a missing dependency, and running `yarn cache clean --force` by hand fixed it.

Not reproduced here: this needs an interactive TTY and a sudo password. Code-verified: there is no timeout and stderr is hidden by default. It is plausible but unverified that the sudo prompt is drawn over by the live progress bar. In #192 one user still hung after commenting out the two sudo lines (possibly because they edited a different install, per the thread).
findings.before:
mac_cleanup/utils.py:18-21 (mac-cleanup-py@ba4d6ef)
    from subprocess import DEVNULL, PIPE, Popen
    # Get stdout and stderr from PIPE
    out_tuple = Popen(command, shell=True, stdout=PIPE, stderr=(DEVNULL if ignore_errors else PIPE)).communicate()

mac_cleanup/default_modules.py:420-430
    def dns_cache():
        with clc as unit:
            unit.message("Cleaning up DNS cache")
            unit.add(Command("sudo dscacheutil -flushcache"))
            unit.add(Command("sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder"))
    def inactive_memory():
        with clc as unit:
            unit.message("Purging inactive memory")
            unit.add(Command("sudo purge"))
findings.after:
In macontrol every external tool call (brew, docker, xcrun simctl, npm/yarn/pnpm, go, gem) goes through one `ToolRunner`:

1. **No shell.** `Process` with `executableURL` plus an argv array, the absolute tool path resolved once, and no string interpolation.
2. **Never interactive.** stdin is `/dev/null`, so a prompt fails fast instead of hanging. The env disables known prompts and side effects: `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, `HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS=1`, `CI=1`, `COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0` (the corepack variable is unverified), `NO_COLOR=1`.
3. **Bounded.** Each rule has a timeout (default 60 s, brew 300 s). On timeout macontrol sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after 5 s, and the step shows "timed out". A Cancel button does the same.
4. **Visible.** stdout and stderr are captured and shown on failure. The row says "brew cleanup failed (exit 1): <last stderr line>", and the log keeps the full output.
5. **No sudo in subprocesses, ever.** Privileged steps (DNS flush, `purge`) are either left out or run in the SMAppService helper after an explicit, system-drawn authorization. They are off by default and labelled "not disk cleanup". `purge` frees no disk space and does not belong in a disk cleaner by default.
6. **Do not start apps the user did not start.** If Docker Desktop is not running, the Docker rule is shown as "Docker not running, start it to clean". macontrol does not `open -jga Docker` behind the user's back.
findings.how:
- `ToolRunner.run(tool:args:timeout:) async throws -> ToolResult(exit, stdout, stderr, duration)`, built on `Process` + `terminationHandler`, wrapped in a `withTaskCancellationHandler` that terminates the process.
- Test (deliberate-bug proof): a fixture tool `read x` must return "failed: stdin closed" in under 1 s, and a fixture `sleep 100` with a 1 s timeout must return `.timedOut`. Remove the stdin redirect or the timeout and the test must fail or hang past the harness limit.
- The rule schema adds `command: {tool, args[], timeout, requiresRunning?: bundleId}` for command rules. There is no free-form shell string field.

findings.title: macOS Uninstall runs the Windows pipeline: a failed 'reg query' counts as success, the .app stays, and name-matched Library folders are rm -rf'd with no review (Kudu, verified)
findings.problem:
Kudu (AdventDevInc/kudu@0ef4292, MIT, 3.5k stars, macOS DMG shipped in v3.4.0) runs its Windows uninstall pipeline unchanged on macOS. The Uninstaller page and its button have no platform gate (`src/renderer/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:365-384`, `src/renderer/src/pages/UninstallerPage.tsx:1055-1063`). Clicking Uninstall on a Mac app does this:

1. The macOS program list sets `uninstallString: ''` and `registryKey: ''` (`src/main/services/program-uninstaller.ts:128-152`).
2. `runUninstaller` calls `spawn('')`. Node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE synchronously, and the catch resolves `null` (`program-uninstaller.ts:303-341`). The `.app` bundle is never touched.
3. `verifyUninstall('')` runs `reg query` through `execNativeUtf8`, which starts `cmd.exe` (`exec-utf8.ts:389`). On macOS that fails with ENOENT, and the catch returns `true`, meaning "key gone = uninstalled successfully" (`program-uninstaller.ts:344-351`). A missing tool counts as success (fail open).
4. `scanLeftoversForProgram` matches the app name, its first word and the publisher by substring against every folder in `~/Library/Application Support`, `~/Library/Caches` and `~/Library/Preferences` (`platform/darwin/paths.ts:82-88`, `program-uninstaller.ts:378-419`). It gives every hit `selected: true` (`:550`). Its running-process check is PowerShell-only, and when that fails it marks "nothing as running" (`:421-456`).
5. The IPC handler then calls `safeDelete` (`rm -rf`, no Trash) on every hit. The user never sees or reviews the list (`src/main/ipc/program-uninstaller.ipc.ts:89-118`).

The result: the app stays installed, and data that belongs to other apps is deleted permanently. A string-only probe that uses Kudu's own matcher and safelist verbatim (`research/bench/adventdevinc-kudu/probe.ts`, `node probe.ts`) matches 7 of 8 realistic cases:
- "Logi Options+" matches `Logic` (Logic Pro and GarageBand user data), through its first word "logi".
- "Firefox Developer Edition" matches `Firefox`, which holds the main Firefox profiles.
- "Brave Browser Beta" matches `BraveSoftware`, which holds the stable Brave profile.
- "Affinity Photo 2" matches `Affinity Designer 2`.
- "Postman Agent" matches `Postman`, "Notion Calendar" matches `Notion`, and "Unity Hub" matches `Unity`.

The controls behave as expected: "Obsidian" matches `obsidian`, and "Obsidian" does not match `Signal`.

Steps 2 and 3 were checked with `node` 26 on macOS 26.6: `spawn('')` throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`, and `execFile('cmd.exe')` fails with `ENOENT`. The full run inside the packaged Electron app is unverified, because I did not launch the app.

Related findings: F-0011 and F-0022 cover substring and vendor-folder over-matching in PureMac and Pearcleaner. This finding is about two further failures: the verification fails open, and the matched set is deleted without any review.
findings.after:
macontrol's uninstall pipeline has three steps, and each one fails closed:

1. **Remove the app first, and prove it.** Move the `.app` bundle to the Trash, then `lstat` its original path and require ENOENT. If any helper or tool reports an error, is missing, or returns output we cannot parse, the result is "could not verify". That counts as failure, and nothing further runs.
2. **Propose leftovers, never delete them automatically.** Leftovers appear in a review sheet. Rows are preselected only for strong evidence: an exact bundle id or team id match (`com.vendor.App`, `group.<TEAMID>.*`) in a known `~/Library` location. Name, first-word and publisher matches are shown unselected with the reason ("name contains 'logi'"). They are never preselected. Vendor-level and shared folders are never whole-folder targets (see F-0022).
3. **The user confirms, and deleted items go to the Trash or quarantine**, never `rm -rf` (see F-0012).

Owner-in-use checks use `NSWorkspace.runningApplications` together with the bundle id. If the running-app query fails, every candidate is treated as "in use" and left alone.
findings.how:
- One `UninstallStep` result enum with the values `done`, `failed` and `unverified`. The UI treats `unverified` the same as `failed`. Add a unit test in which the verification helper throws ENOENT and the expected outcome is `failed`, with no leftover scan.
- Leftover matcher tests, taken from the Kudu probe (`research/bench/adventdevinc-kudu/probe.ts`). None of these may be preselected:
  - "Logi Options+" must not select `Logic`.
  - "Firefox Developer Edition" must not select `Firefox`.
  - "Brave Browser Beta" must not select `BraveSoftware`.
  - "Affinity Photo 2" must not select `Affinity Designer 2`.
  
  Exact bundle id hits (`~/Library/Caches/com.logi.optionsplus`) may be preselected.
- In code review, reject any IPC or handler that calls delete on paths the user did not see in a review list.
findings.verified: feat/uninstaller afb0996: uninstall() trashes the app bundle alone first and moves leftovers in a second batch only when the bundle's outcome is .trashed and its path is empty afterwards (lstat), otherwise every leftover is reported 'Not moved, because <App> is still installed.' Leftovers are never deleted unreviewed: only plan items the user chose, Move to Trash through Safety. Tests: UninstallFlowTests.appThatStaysInstalledKeepsItsData(reinstalledAfterTrash: false/true), appThatDoesNotQuitStopsEverything, failedBootoutStopsBeforeTrashing; review-uninstaller-2's probe whenTheBundleStaysNoLeftoverIsTrashed passes against feat/safety-trash 31fc928's real TrashService.

findings.title: Disk map of '/' counts the Data volume twice (firmlinks + /System/Volumes/Data) and walks into VM, Preboot and /Volumes; st_dev cannot tell System from Data (Kudu, verified)
findings.where: Kudu src/main/ipc/disk-analyzer.ipc.ts analyzeDirectory:26-80, measureDirectorySize:127-150, getDrives:186-211, resolveRootPath:215-223
findings.problem:
Kudu's disk analyzer (AdventDevInc/kudu@0ef4292 `src/main/ipc/disk-analyzer.ipc.ts:26-150`) lists every `/dev/*` mount from `df -Pk` as a "drive" (`:186-211`). "Root" is `/`. It then walks the chosen root with `readdir` and `stat`. It never checks the device, the inode, the mount status or the firmlinks. On macOS this causes two errors:

- **The Data volume is counted twice.** `/Users`, `/Applications`, `/Library`, `/private`, `/opt`, `/usr/local` and the other firmlinks lead into the Data volume, and `/System/Volumes/Data` is reachable from `/` as well. Both routes are walked and summed.
- **The walk crosses into every other mount point.** That includes `/System/Volumes/VM` (swap files), `/System/Volumes/Preboot`, and everything under `/Volumes`: external disks, network shares and Time Machine disks. All of it is counted as part of "Root".

Verified locally on macOS 26.6 (25G72):
- `research/bench/adventdevinc-kudu/firmlink_probe.ts` runs Kudu's `measureDirectorySize`, copied verbatim, on one 30,839,917-byte folder through both routes. Each route returns 30,839,917 bytes. `/Users/...` and `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/...` have the same `st_dev` (16777229) and the same `st_ino`, so a walk of `/` sums 61,679,834 bytes.
- On this Mac the Data volume holds 172.9 GB (`df`). A Kudu scan of `/` would overstate the total by roughly that much, plus VM and Preboot, plus any mounted external or network volume. The full `/` scan was not run, because of the load on the machine.
- `stat` reports the same `st_dev` for `/` and `/System/Volumes/Data` (16777229), because the System and Data volumes share one APFS volume group. A `du -x`-style "stay on one device" check therefore does **not** stop the double walk.

Known neighbours: F-0005 (Mole) is the opposite error. That walk skips `/System/Volumes` by name and misses Data-root-only content. F-0010 is about hard links. Neither covers crossing mount points or the fact that `st_dev` cannot separate System from Data.
findings.after:
The volume model follows F-0005: the Data volume is walked once, rooted at `/System/Volumes/Data`, and shown to the user through the firmlink map. On top of that, macontrol's walker has two hard stops that apply to any root the user picks, `/` included:

1. **Never descend into a mount point below the root.** Stop at every directory whose `ATTR_DIR_MOUNTSTATUS` has `DIR_MNTSTATUS_MNTPOINT` set. This attribute comes from the same `getattrlistbulk` call, so it adds no syscalls. Each nested volume is shown as a separate volume tile, or as a link to scan it.
2. **Keep a visited set of `(st_dev, st_ino)` for directories**, so a directory reached through a second route (a firmlink, a bind or nullfs mount, a loop) is counted once and labelled "same as /Users".

Mount identity never relies on `st_dev` alone.
findings.how:
- `research/bench/adventdevinc-kudu/mountstatus_probe.c` (verified on 26.6) shows which paths `getattrlist(ATTR_DIR_MOUNTSTATUS)` flags as `DIR_MNTSTATUS_MNTPOINT`:
  - Flagged: `/`, `/System/Volumes/Data`, `/System/Volumes/VM` and `/System/Volumes/Preboot`.
  - Not flagged: `/Users`, `/Volumes` and `/private/var`.
  
  The same probe shows that `/Users` and `/System/Volumes/Data/Users` share both dev and inode. The rule is to stop at mount points other than the scan root, and to dedupe directories by `(dev, ino)`.
- Check 1: a scan of `/` on a test Mac must equal a scan of `/System/Volumes/Data` plus the system-volume tile, within 1 %, and must not change when a USB disk is mounted.
- Check 2: a unit test with a fixture that reaches one directory through two paths (use a nullfs mount or a bind-like hard-linked dir if available, otherwise mock the walker's stat source). The expected result is that its bytes are counted once.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): entries with ATTR_DIR_MOUNTSTATUS != 0 (mount points and automount triggers) are .mountPoint leaves, never entered; '/' walks only /System/Volumes/Data and places firmlinked entries once. Tests: ScanEngineTests.mountPointsAreLeaves (real /System/Volumes: Data is a 0 B leaf), TreeSinkTests.mountPointEntryIsALeafWithItsFlag, dataVolumeRootIsPlacedAtUserFacingPaths.

findings.title: Rule paths are unconstrained strings: ${HOME}, ${LIBRARY}, '/', '${CACHES}/../..' all pass schema and CI, and the scanner preselects everything older than 60 min in them (Kudu, verified)
findings.where: Kudu rules/schema/rules.schema.json TemplatePath:16-19; src/main/rules/validate.ts:81-88; src/main/rules/loader.ts resolvePath:159-170; src/main/services/file-utils.ts scanDirectory:820-866
findings.problem:
Kudu's cleaning targets are community-editable JSON ("no code required", `rules/RULES.md:3`). That is the model macontrol plans to adopt, but nothing in Kudu's schema, validator or loader restricts where a rule may point.

- **Schema:** the schema's `TemplatePath` is just `"type": "string"`, with no pattern (`rules/schema/rules.schema.json:16-19`).
- **Validator:** `validate.ts` checks only that `${VAR}` names are on the platform allowlist (`src/main/rules/validate.ts:81-88`).
- **Loader:** `resolvePath` substitutes the variables and returns the string. It does not normalise `..`, and it does not refuse a root, `$HOME` or `~/Library` (`src/main/rules/loader.ts:159-170`).
- **Scanner:** there is no deny list. `scanAppRule` → `scanMultipleDirectories` → `scanDirectory` offers every entry older than 60 minutes as a preselected item (`src/main/services/file-utils.ts:820-866`, where `selected: true` is at `:852`).

Verified with `research/bench/adventdevinc-kudu/rule_schema_probe.py`, which runs python-jsonschema on Kudu's own draft-07 schema. The 8 shipped darwin files validate. Every dangerous path below is also accepted as both an `apps.json` path and a `system.json` target:
- `${HOME}`
- `${HOME}/Documents`
- `${LIBRARY}`
- `/`
- `${CACHES}/../..`
- `${APP_SUPPORT}/../Keychains`

The shipped data already relies on reviewers catching this. `apps.json:5` and `:21` use `"paths": ["${HOME}"]`, and only their `cleanupAction` keeps them from being scanned as directories. If a PR deletes that one field, the rule becomes "offer all of `~` older than 60 minutes, preselected", and CI stays green.

There are also broad targets that pass review today:
- `${LIBRARY}/Saved Application State` as a whole (`system.json:12`).
- `/private/tmp` (`system.json:6`). It is cleaned on mtime alone, so a live socket more than 60 minutes old is offered.
- `${CACHES}/Google` labelled "Android Studio" (`apps.json:44`).
- `${HOME}/.m2/repository` (`apps.json:26`), which also holds locally built `mvn install` artifacts that cannot be downloaded again.
findings.after:
macontrol's rule format gives paths a type and checks them twice: once in CI and once at load time.

- **Schema.** A path must start with an allowed anchor variable (`${CACHES}`, `${APP_SUPPORT}`, `${LIBRARY}`, `${HOME}`, `${TMPDIR}`) and have at least N literal segments below it. N is set per anchor: `${HOME}` and `${LIBRARY}` need at least 2 segments, `${CACHES}` and `${APP_SUPPORT}` need at least 1. Segments may not be `.` or `..`, and absolute paths are not allowed, except through an explicit `system` allowlist that needs admin review.
- **Native actions.** A native command (for example `uv cache prune`) is a separate rule kind with no `paths`. It never borrows a directory path as a placeholder.
- **Load-time guard.** The loader normalises the resolved path and rejects the rule if the result equals, or is an ancestor of, a protected root: `/`, `~`, `~/Library`, `~/Library/Application Support`, `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, `~/Downloads`, `~/Library/Keychains`, `~/Library/Mail`, `~/Library/Messages`, `~/Library/Mobile Documents`, and so on. Any rule that fails this check is dropped with a logged error. The rest of the rule set still loads.
- **Per-rule safety fields.** Every rule carries `owner` (bundle id or ownerless), `regenerates: true|false` and `liveCheck` (none, mtime, or openfiles). Rules with `regenerates: false` (Maven's local repo, Saved Application State) are never preselected.
findings.how:
- Schema: `"pattern": "^\\$\\{(CACHES|APP_SUPPORT|LIBRARY|HOME|TMPDIR)\\}(/[^/]+)+$"` plus `"not": {"pattern": "(^|/)\\.\\.?(/|$)"}`. Kudu already uses exactly this `not` pattern for `anchorPaths` (`rules.schema.json:125-126`), just not for paths. The per-anchor depth checks go in a small CI validator.
- Loader guard: `URL(fileURLWithPath:).standardizedFileURL.resolvingSymlinksInPath()` checked against the protected-root set, with one unit test per protected root. Reuse `rule_schema_probe.py`'s six bad paths as negative fixtures: each must fail both the schema and the load-time guard.
- When importing Kudu's MIT darwin rules (T-0018), run them through this validator. Expect the two `${HOME}` placeholder rules to be rewritten as native-action rules, and `m2/repository` and `Saved Application State` to be flagged `regenerates: false`.
findings.verified: feat/cleaner-catalog: PatternValidator refuses anything not starting with ~/ or an allowlisted absolute root (only /System/Volumes/Data/macOS Install Data), $ ~ \ . .. and empty components, globs outside the last component, fewer than 3 levels below home, user content roots, Mobile Documents/CloudStorage/FileProvider/com~apple~, and globs directly in ~/Library/<X> other than Caches/Logs. A rule with one bad pattern is dropped whole, at load and again in Cleaner.init. Tests: PatternValidatorTests.refuses (24 cases incl. ${HOME}/x, /, ~/Library/*, ~/Documents/*, ~/Library/Caches/../.., ~/Library/Caches/*/x*y/*), aRuleWithOneBadPatternIsDroppedWhole; mutation removing the depth check fails them.

findings.title: Dev-artifact scan treats app- and tool-owned folders in ~/Library as projects: 47 offered on this Mac, incl. pnpm global installs; broke Zed (kondo #191, verified)
findings.problem:
kondo calls any folder a "project" if it directly holds a marker file (`package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, any `*.py`, ...), and offers that folder's artifact dirs by name. It never asks who owns the folder. Two things limit the walk. It skips names that start with a dot (`is_hidden`), and it stops descending below a project it found. `~/Library` has no leading dot, so kondo walks it. It also walks a `node_modules` whose parent has no `package.json`, so every package inside becomes a "project" (tbillington/kondo@1d351ca `kondo-lib/src/lib.rs:357-359, 380-386, 446-451`).

Real damage, issue #191 (open, https://github.com/tbillington/kondo/issues/191): the user ran kondo in `~`. It deleted `~/Library/Application Support/Zed/languages/vtsls/node_modules`, and Zed's TypeScript language server then failed with `Cannot find module .../vtsls.js`. The maintainer asked "Is kondo detecting your home directory as a kind of project?". There is no fix at 1d351ca.

Verified locally with the kondo v0.9 release binary in dry-run mode (`-n`), which deletes nothing:
- `kondo -n ~/Library` on the research Mac found **47 projects in 5.1 s**. 39 were `node_modules` folders inside `~/Library/pnpm/store/v11/links/...`, the pnpm global virtual store. 2 were `~/Library/pnpm/global/v11/<hash>/node_modules`, which holds every package installed with `pnpm add -g`. The others were the nested dependencies of a Huawei DevEco Studio plugin, the SDK dependencies of the VS Code agent host, `site-packages` in 3 pipx venvs, and the user's Python `site-packages`. Pressing `a` (all), or passing `--all`, removes every one of them. See `research/bench/tbillington-kondo/results-2026-09-23.txt`.
- On a synthetic home, `probe.sh` case 1 reproduces #191: `home/Library/Application Support/Zed/languages/vtsls Node project └─ node_modules (293.0KiB)`.
- Together they total 1.3 MiB, so a size-sorted list gives no hint that anything is wrong. The first sign of harm is a broken tool days later.
findings.after:
macontrol's dev-artifact scanner only finds projects where users keep code. Folders that belong to apps or tools are never project roots.

1. **Excluded roots, as data in the rule file with a reason:** `~/Library/**` (all of it, including `~/Library/pnpm`, `Application Support/*`, `Python/*`), any bundle or package (`*.app`, `*.framework`, and anything with a bundle bit), `/System`, `/Applications`, `/Library`, and package-manager homes such as `~/.npm`, `~/.cargo/registry`, `~/.rustup`, `~/.m2`, `~/.gradle/caches`, `~/.local/pipx` and `~/.local/share/uv`. Caches in those places are covered only by the curated cache rules, which check the owning app. Mole's purge does the same: it excludes `Library` from its project walk (tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd `lib/clean/project.sh:702,716,771`).
2. **No project inside an artifact.** A directory is never a project root when any ancestor is an artifact dir (`node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`, `venv`, `site-packages`, `Pods`, `.build`, `vendor`, ...). Artifact dirs are sized from the scan tree and never descended into for discovery.
3. **Code-folder roots by default.** The default scan covers the folders that hold `.git` repos under `~` (found once, cached, editable in Settings), not all of `~`. The user can add roots explicitly.
findings.how:
- Exclusion check: during the walk, keep a per-frame flag "inside excluded or artifact ancestor", which is O(1) per directory. The exclusion list lives in the rule file as `{path_glob, reason}`, and tests read the same file.
- Acceptance: `research/bench/tbillington-kondo/probe.sh` case 1 must produce 0 offers. A read-only run over the real `~/Library` must produce 0 offers from the dev-artifact module (kondo v0.9: 47).
- Regression fixture: add `home/Library/pnpm/global/v11/<hash>/{package.json,node_modules/.modules.yaml}` and `home/x/node_modules/pkg/{package.json,node_modules/}`. Expect 0 offers from both.
findings.verified: feat/cleaner-catalog: v1 has no marker-based project-artifact scan at all, so nothing in ~/Library is ever classified as a project; the pnpm store (~/Library/pnpm/store/*, never global/) and Gradle/Maven/Cargo stores are safety=review, not preselected. Tests: CatalogTests.sharedStoresAndDeviceSymbolsNeedReview. Phase 2 (artifacts in user-chosen roots with marker files, never under ~/Library) is not built.

findings.title: Project discovery stops at the first marker file: a stray .py hides every project below it, and a Cargo+Node dir cleans only one type (kondo #175/#29, verified)
findings.problem:
kondo types each directory by the first file, in readdir order, that matches any marker. Any `*.py` file counts as a marker. Once a directory is typed, the walk never goes below it (`skip_current_dir`). A "project" with 0 artifact bytes is then dropped without any message (tbillington/kondo@1d351ca `kondo-lib/src/lib.rs:393-452`, `kondo/src/main.rs:184-186`). This loses real projects and says nothing about it:

Verified with the kondo v0.9 release binary in dry-run mode (`research/bench/tbillington-kondo/probe.sh`, cases 2 and 7):
- **Stray script masks a tree.** `~/code/notes.py`, `~/code/app` (Cargo, 1.9 MiB `target`) and `~/code/web` (Node, 977 KiB `node_modules`). `kondo -n ~/code` prints `Projects cleaned: 0/0, Bytes deleted: 0.0B / 0.0B`. After `notes.py` is deleted it finds 2 projects and 2.9 MiB. Issue #175 is the same report: "Previously I could run kondo in the directory and it would clean every project. Now I'm just getting Projects cleaned: 0".
- **Multi-type directory, readdir order decides.** In `tauri/` (Cargo.toml, package.json, target, node_modules), `ls -f` puts Cargo.toml first, so only `target` is offered and `node_modules` (977 KiB) never is. In `mixed/` (setup.py, package.json, node_modules), the directory is typed Python with 0 bytes and dropped, so `node_modules` never shows.
- **Nested projects are never reached.** `<crate>/examples/*/target` and workspace members with their own `node_modules` stay hidden (#29, where the maintainer says "Essentially, stop recursing if a project is found"; also #117).

The maintainer acknowledges it in #175: "it doesn't handle more than 1 project within a directory, or projects within projects". The fix on branch `discovery-rework` (eab2099, 2025-04-21) runs every project kind against each directory and keeps descending into subdirs that are not artifacts (`kondo-lib/src/search.rs:40-74` on that branch). That branch has not been merged in 17 months.
findings.after:
macontrol types directories by the whole listing and prunes only artifacts.

1. **All rules, every directory.** Every rule's marker is matched against the directory listing the scanner already holds (one `getattrlistbulk` per directory). The directory gets *every* matching type, so a Cargo + Node directory offers both `target` and `node_modules`.
2. **Prune artifacts, not projects.** The scanner never enters artifact subdirs that pass their rule's verification (they are sized from the scan tree). It keeps descending into every other subdir, so nested projects are found and each artifact goes to its nearest project.
3. **Weak markers never stop descent.** `*.py` and `*.ipynb` only enable artifacts that no other tool uses (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.ipynb_checkpoints`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`). Python project markers are `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `requirements*.txt`, `Pipfile`, `uv.lock` and `pixi.toml`.
4. **Nothing disappears silently.** The scan summary shows "N projects without reclaimable files" plus skipped roots and their reasons, so "0 found" always comes with an explanation.
findings.how:
- Rule schema: `markers: [{name|suffix, strength: strong|weak}]`. The walker keeps an ordered set of active rule ids per frame. No readdir-order dependence: the test shuffles the listing and expects the same result.
- Acceptance: `research/bench/tbillington-kondo/probe.sh` expectations. Case 2 offers `code/app/target` and `code/web/node_modules` while `notes.py` is present. Case 7 offers `tauri/target`, `tauri/node_modules` and `mixed/node_modules`.
- Performance guard: pruning artifact dirs keeps the speed kondo got from stopping at projects (CHANGELOG 0.3 says "97.5% runtime reduction"), because `node_modules` and `target` are still never entered. Check this on T-0004's bench tree.

findings.title: Artifact rules match folder names only: a git-tracked build/, Unreal Saved/ autosaves and (released v0.9) .venv are offered like node_modules (kondo, verified)
findings.problem:
In kondo, a rule is just a folder name under a project root. `clean()` checks that the folder exists and then calls `fs::remove_dir_all` on it (tbillington/kondo@1d351ca `kondo-lib/src/lib.rs:316-329`). Nothing checks that the folder is build output. There is no git-tracked check and no check for a generator signature such as `CMakeCache.txt`, or the `CACHEDIR.TAG` that Cargo writes into `target/` (rust-lang/cargo@70ce895 `crates/cargo-util/src/paths.rs:796-815`). There is no content check of any kind.

Several of the 63 names in the tables are generic or can hold the user's work (`lib.rs:35-94`):
- `build` for CMake, Gradle and Pub; `bin` for .NET; `vendor` for Composer, which some PHP repos commit; `Pods` for CocoaPods, which some teams commit.
- Unity `Build` and `Builds` (shipped player builds) and `Library` (reimport time, unverified).
- Unreal `Saved`, which holds `Autosaves/`, `Config/` and `SaveGames/`.
- `.venv` stayed on the list until 1d351ca (2026-01-28: "venvs are created intentionally sometimes, and can also take quite some work to setup"). The latest release, v0.9 (2026-01-23), still deletes it.

Verified with the v0.9 release binary in dry-run mode (`research/bench/tbillington-kondo/probe.sh`, cases 3, 4 and 6):
- a git-tracked `cm/build/` (`release.sh`, `signing-notes.txt`, committed) is offered as `build (195.3KiB)`;
- `game/Saved/Autosaves/Main_Auto1.umap` is offered as `Saved (976.6KiB)`, next to `Intermediate` with the same weight;
- `py/.venv` is offered.

Every offered folder carries the same weight. One `y` removes all artifact dirs of a project, and `a` removes everything after it without asking again (`kondo/src/main.rs:288-294`). The README says it plainly: "Kondo is essentially `rm -rf` with a prompt".

For contrast, Mole's purge refuses a candidate that holds git-tracked files, a nested `.git` or a `*-keypair.json` (tw93/Mole@a7fa8dd `lib/clean/project.sh:506-532`). That check was added after incident #1551, where Solana keypairs were lost.
findings.after:
Each macontrol dev rule is `{marker, artifact, verify, tier}`, and nothing is offered unless `verify` passes:

1. **Positive signature where one exists.** For Cargo `target/`, check for `CACHEDIR.TAG` with signature `8a477f597d28d172789f06886806bc55` (Cargo writes it and also sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey`, per cargo `paths.rs:796-815`). For CMake `build/`, check for `CMakeCache.txt`. For npm `node_modules/`, check for `.package-lock.json`, the npm v7+ hidden lockfile. For pnpm `node_modules/`, check for `.modules.yaml` (seen locally). A generic rule also covers any directory that has a valid `CACHEDIR.TAG` or the backup-exclusion flag, because its creator declared it disposable. Signatures for other tools (yarn, Gradle, Unity, Unreal) are unverified and go to T-0005 and T-0010 as open items.
2. **Nothing tracked.** When the project is a git work tree, the candidate must hold no tracked files. Run `git ls-files -z -- <dir>` read-only with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, the same idea as Mole's guard. A nested `.git` also blocks the candidate.
3. **Tiers.**
   - `regenerable` (preselected): `node_modules`, `target`, `__pycache__`, `.gradle`, `.build`, `DerivedData`, `.dart_tool`, `zig-cache`.
   - `review` (shown with a reason, never preselected): `Saved` ("may contain autosaves and config"), `Build`/`Builds` ("may be shipped builds"), Unity `Library` ("slow reimport"), `vendor`, `Pods`, `.venv`/`venv`, `bin`.
   - `never`: the candidate fails verify.
4. Disposal follows F-0012. Only the `regenerable` tier may be unlinked directly. Every other tier goes to quarantine or Trash.
findings.how:
- Rule schema fields `verify: [cachedir_tag | file:<name> | no_git_tracked]` and `tier`. Keep the table as data (JSON). kondo keeps two copies of its detection table, and they have already drifted apart: `kondo_lib::clean(&str)` at `lib.rs:536-560` lacks Gradle, Unreal, Jupyter, Python, .NET and Turborepo.
- Acceptance, using `research/bench/tbillington-kondo/probe.sh`: `cm/build` is not offered (tracked, no CMakeCache.txt). `game/Intermediate` is preselected, while `game/Saved` is offered unselected with its reason. `py/.venv` is offered unselected.
- The `git ls-files` cost is one process per candidate in a git repo. Batch it per repo with `git ls-files -z -- <dir1> <dir2> ...` and give it a 2 s timeout, as in F-0029's ToolRunner. On timeout, treat the candidate as `review`.

findings.title: Delete renames the item into a hidden .mangodisk-delete-* sibling before removing it: Quit or crash mid-delete orphans it, with no launch-time recovery and no unguarded-quit check (MangoDisk)
findings.where: MangoDisk permanent_delete.rs:551-620 delete_via_staging, :1078-1110 create_staging_directory; src-tauri/src/commands/resident.rs:136 resident_quit; privileged_uninstall.applescript:25-43
findings.problem:
MangoDisk makes every delete a two-step move: it renames the target into a hidden sibling directory, then removes that directory. It has no record or recovery for a process that dies between the two steps. All citations are harry0703/MangoDisk@19e55d2.

- **One path for every delete.** Rule cleanup, the whole-root fast path (DerivedData), analysis-view delete, duplicates, uninstall and leftovers all end in `delete_via_staging` (11 callers of `delete_path_permanently` / `delete_directory_*_permanently_with_cancellation`). It runs `fs::rename(path, <parent>/.mangodisk-delete-<pid>-<n>/target)` (`src-tauri/crates/mangodisk-core/src/filesystem/permanent_delete.rs:563`, name built at `:1081`) and only then removes the tree. The removal is serial, or uses at most 2 workers on macOS (`:33-34`), so a large tree takes a long time.
- **Nothing ever looks for these directories again.** A repo-wide grep finds the `.mangodisk-delete-` string only in its two creators (`permanent_delete.rs:1081`, `mangodisk-platform/src/macos/privileged_uninstall.rs:289`) and two tests (`permanent_delete.rs:1575`, `privileged_uninstall.rs:551`). There is no launch-time sweep. There is also no write-ahead record, because History is written only after execution (`mangodisk-core/src/history/service.rs:50` `append`, `:78` `upsert_deep_cleanup`).
- **Quit is not guarded while a delete runs.** The tray/panel Quit command is `app.exit(0)` with no operation check (`src-tauri/src/commands/resident.rs:136-138`). The run loop handles no `RunEvent::ExitRequested` (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:363-377`). Users do force-quit during cleanup: in issue #24 a stuck cleanup could only be ended by force-quitting (https://github.com/harry0703/MangoDisk/issues/24).
- **What the user sees afterwards.** The item is gone from its path, so it looks deleted. The rest of it still uses disk inside a hidden dot-directory that no rule root matches, for example `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/.mangodisk-delete-812-3/target` next to the `DerivedData` root. History has no entry for the run.
- **Privileged uninstall has the same gap.** The AppleScript does `mv` into staging and then `rm -rf` (`privileged_uninstall.applescript:25,38`). When that fails, the UI says "Uninstall did not finish cleanly; inspect or restore the application before retrying" (`src/locales/en-US.json:2338`) but never says where the app went.

Verification: I read the code and grepped the whole repo at 19e55d2. I did NOT run the kill-mid-delete scenario, because building the Tauri app was skipped on this loaded machine.
findings.after:
macontrol treats "moved aside, not yet gone" as durable state that it owns:

1. **Write ahead.** Before the rename, append `{op_id, original_path, staging_path, dev, ino, bytes, rule_id}` to the cleanup journal and fsync it (this is the same journal F-0012 proposes). Append `done` when removal completes, or `restored` after a rollback.
2. **One known place per volume.** Stage into a single app-owned directory per volume (for example `<volume>/.macontrol-staging/<op_id>/`, or the Trash/quarantine from F-0012), not into a hidden sibling next to each target, so that recovery never has to search the disk.
3. **Reconcile on launch.** For every journal entry without `done`, finish the removal if the rule marks the data regenerable. Otherwise restore it to `original_path` if that path is still free, and fall back to Trash if it is not. Show one banner: "Recovered an interrupted cleanup: N items, X GB", with Reveal.
4. **Guard quit.** While a destructive operation runs, `applicationShouldTerminate` returns `.terminateLater` and shows "Finish now / Stop and restore". The menu-bar Quit goes through the same path.
5. **Name the location on failure.** A "recovery required" message always includes the staged path and a Reveal-in-Finder button.
findings.how:
- Swift: `NSApplicationDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate(_:)` returns `.terminateLater`, and the reply comes once the operation settles. The journal is JSON lines under `~/Library/Application Support/macontrol/journal/`, with `FileHandle.synchronize()` after every write-ahead line.
- Staging rename: `renameat` from an `O_NOFOLLOW` parent fd into the per-volume staging dir. Recheck (dev, ino) on the staged path, as MangoDisk already does (`permanent_delete.rs:568-580`, worth copying as an idea).
- Acceptance test: build a 50k-file fixture, start a delete, `kill -9` the process after the journal shows `staged`, relaunch, and assert that nothing is left under any `.macontrol-staging` dir, the fixture is either fully removed (regenerable) or restored byte-identical, and the banner counts match the journal.
- Related: F-0012 (no quarantine/journal, PureMac). Its proposed quarantine needs this same reconciliation step.
findings.verified: No staging rename: the item goes to the Trash under its own name via FileManager.trashItem, then one journal line is appended and fsynced; a crash leaves at most one visible item in the Trash without a line, and a torn line is skipped and repaired on the next open. Tests: TrashServiceTests.trashesUnderTheItemsOwnNameAndJournalsIt (backend receives the original path), aTornJournalLineIsSkipped. feat/safety-trash (T-0044)

findings.title: Incremental FSEvents rescan re-counts hard links: a 9.2 MB tree reads 26.0 MB after two splices, and the cache keeps it (OpenDisk, verified; see F-0010)
findings.problem:
OpenDisk's full scan counts a hard-linked file once, but its incremental rescan (FSEvents replay + splice, the path behind the README's "20-28x faster" rescans) counts every link again. The error persists in the saved cache, so every later rescan starts from the inflated sizes until a full scan is forced.

All citations are 137137137/OpenDisk@6e3f1f7:

- Full scan: `TraversalScanner.runWorker` keeps a `(st_dev, fileID)` set and zeroes the second and later links (`OpenDisk/Services/Scanning/TraversalScanner.swift:204-221`).
- Splice of a changed directory: `IncrementalUpdater.updateDirectory` re-lists the directory and adds every file at its full `ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE`, with no link check (`OpenDisk/Services/Scanning/IncrementalUpdater.swift:104-109`).
- New directories: `adoptScannedSubtree` runs a fresh `TraversalScanner.scan` whose dedup set starts empty, so links into the rest of the tree count again (`IncrementalUpdater.swift:159-175`).
- Root cause: `FileTree.Node` stores no inode or link count (`FileTree.swift:23-29`), so the cached tree cannot know which files were already counted. The cache is saved right after a splice (`ScanEngine.swift:318-321`).
- No test covers `IncrementalUpdater`, `ScanCache` or the journal (`OpenDiskTests/` has none).

Verified with a probe that compiles OpenDisk's own, unmodified engine files (`research/bench/137137137-opendisk/run_incremental_probe.sh`). Fixture: `A/big.bin` (8 MiB), `B/link.bin` (hard link to it), 200 small files in `B`:
- full scan: 9,207,808 B
- after one splice of `B` (one file added): 17,600,512 B (+8 MiB, the link counted twice)
- after a new dir `C` holding another link: 25,989,120 B from the spliced tree, against 9,211,904 B from a fresh full scan of the same tree (2.8x).

Where this bites: pnpm hard-links every package file from its store into each project's node_modules (https://pnpm.io/motivation). Any `pnpm install` makes those node_modules directories "changed", so the next OpenDisk rescan inflates them, and the "/" total drifts above what macOS reports as used.
findings.after:
macontrol's size rule for hard links (F-0010: each (st_dev, st_ino) counted once) holds for every code path that writes sizes into the tree: full scan, live FSEvents updates, cache replay and post-delete refresh.

- The tree keeps, for every file with nlink > 1, its (dev, ino) and which node owns the bytes, in a side table (a dictionary keyed by (dev, ino)). Only multi-link files pay for it. The table is saved with the cache.
- A splice that re-lists a directory first releases the ownership of the files it removes, then asks the table before sizing each re-listed multi-link file. A subtree scan started by a splice runs with the tree's table, not an empty one.
- When the owning link is deleted, ownership moves to a surviving link (size re-attributed there), so the total stays right and "reclaimable" follows F-0010's rule.
findings.how:
- One engine entry point (`sizeFile(dev:ino:nlink:alloc:)`) used by the walker and by the splicer, so the rule cannot fork again.
- Acceptance test (port of research/bench/137137137-opendisk/incremental_probe.swift to macontrol's engine): fixture A/big.bin 8 MiB + B/link.bin; full scan, touch B, splice, add C/link2.bin, splice root. After every step the tree total must equal a fresh full scan byte-exact (9,211,904 B in the probe run), and `rm A/big.bin` + splice must move the 8 MiB to B/link.bin, not drop it.
- Run it through cache save/load too: scan, save, reload, splice, compare with a fresh scan.

findings.title: Incremental rescans never free replaced nodes: 2,225 nodes for 206 live after 10 splices, cache 10.7x a fresh scan, no compaction (OpenDisk, verified)
findings.problem:
OpenDisk's incremental rescan never frees the nodes it replaces. Every splice unlinks the old children of each changed directory and appends new ones; the old nodes stay in the tree's arrays for good. They are still copied by every partial snapshot, written to the on-disk cache and loaded back, and indexed by search. Nothing compacts them: there is no compaction code, and a full scan happens only when the journal replay fails.

All citations are 137137137/OpenDisk@6e3f1f7:

- `removeAllChildren(of:)` leaves the subtrees "as unreachable garbage nodes" (`OpenDisk/Services/Scanning/FileTree.swift:83-96`). `updateDirectory` calls it and then `addNode`s every re-listed file (`IncrementalUpdater.swift:102-109`). `rescanSubtree` does the same for a whole subtree (`IncrementalUpdater.swift:151-156`).
- `serializedData()` writes all `nodes.count` entries, reachable or not (`FileTree.swift:354-405`), and `ScanEngine` saves the spliced tree as the next cache (`ScanEngine.swift:318-321`).
- `SearchIndex` builds its name blob over every node and hides the garbage with a reachability bitmap (`OpenDisk/Services/Search/SearchIndex.swift`, the `reachable` field), so the garbage also costs index memory and sweep time.
- The snapshot path copies the whole array (copy-on-write) under the scan lock (`ScanEngine.swift:73-88`), so garbage also makes every live snapshot slower.

Verified with OpenDisk's own engine files (`research/bench/137137137-opendisk/run_incremental_probe.sh`): after 10 splices of one 201-file directory the tree held 2,225 nodes, of which 206 were reachable. The serialized cache was 81,127 B against 7,577 B for a fresh scan of the same tree (10.7x). Growth per rescan equals the entry count of every directory FSEvents reports as changed, so a busy home folder (caches, browser profiles, node_modules) grows the "/" tree on every launch or Refresh.
findings.after:
macontrol's tree reuses or reclaims the slots that a splice frees, so memory and cache size track the live tree.

- Freed node ids go on a free list and the next `addNode` reuses them. A splice usually re-adds about as many entries as it removed, so the arrays stay flat.
- Before a cache save, if dead slots exceed 10% of the tree, compact: one reachability pass, a remap table, rewrite parent/child/sibling ids. That is O(n), the same cost as the save itself, and it runs off the main thread.
- The search index is built over live nodes only.
findings.how:
- Test: scan a fixture, splice the same changed directory 10 times, assert `nodeCount - reachableCount <= 10%` of the tree and that the serialized cache is within 10% of a fresh scan's (the probe measured 2,225 vs 206 nodes and 81,127 vs 7,577 B for OpenDisk).
- Test the id remap on its own: compact a tree with holes and assert every path, size and parent link equals the pre-compaction tree.

findings.title: Delete guard matches path strings: ~ reached as /System/Volumes/Data/Users/<me> passes and is deleted permanently; realpath() does not fix it, F_GETPATH does (OpenDisk, verified; extends F-0024)
findings.problem:
OpenDisk's delete guard compares path strings, so the same protected folder reached through its Data-volume alias passes the guard, can be collected, and is then deleted permanently (`FileManager.removeItem`, no Trash).

All citations are 137137137/OpenDisk@6e3f1f7:

- `ProtectedPaths.reason(for:)` matches `standardizingPath` output against a set of string roots, the literal home and `~/Library`, and the parent strings `/Users`, `/Volumes`, `/System/Volumes` (`OpenDisk/Services/ProtectedPaths.swift:9-46`). `standardizingPath` does not resolve firmlinks.
- `Collector.appendOne` relies on this check alone (`OpenDisk/Models/Collector.swift:60-75`), and `deleteAll` removes each item with `FileManager.default.removeItem(atPath:)` (`Collector.swift:150-167`).
- The Data volume is reachable through "Scan Folder…" (`chooseFolder()` opens an `NSOpenPanel` and scans `url.path` as given, `OpenDisk/Views/Main/DevicePickerView.swift:173-186`), and a scan roots all row paths at the chosen folder (`FileTree.path(of:)`).

Verified by compiling OpenDisk's unmodified `ProtectedPaths.swift` and `UserHome.swift` with a probe (`research/bench/137137137-opendisk/protected_paths_probe.swift`). The probe checks strings only and deletes nothing:
- `~` BLOCKED, and `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/<me>` ALLOWED. Both are `dev=16777229 ino=36480`, the same directory.
- `~/Library` BLOCKED, and its alias ALLOWED. `/Users`, `/Applications` BLOCKED, and `/System/Volumes/Data/Users`, `/System/Volumes/Data/Applications`, `/System/Volumes/Data/Library` and `/System/Volumes/Data/private/var` ALLOWED.

This is not a duplicate of F-0024, which covers too few protected roots. F-0024's "after" says checks run "on the resolved real path (symlinks and `..` resolved)". That is not enough: `realpath()` returns `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/<me>` unchanged. A Python check here shows `realpath` keeps the alias and `fcntl(F_GETPATH)` returns `/Users/<me>`.
findings.after:
macontrol's `DeletionPolicy` (F-0024) checks the item's identity, not the string it was reached by:

1. Open the target with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW` (for a symlink, `O_SYMLINK`) at execution time and take its canonical path from `fcntl(fd, F_GETPATH)`. Checked here: it maps `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/<me>` to `/Users/<me>` and `/System/Volumes/Data/private/var` to `/private/var`. `realpath()` does not. Run every policy rule on that canonical path.
2. As a second, string-free check, compare `(st_dev, st_ino)` of the target and of each ancestor (from `fstat` on the same fd and on `..` walks) against a set built at launch from the protected roots ($HOME, ~/Library, /Users, /Applications, /Library, /System, ...). Any match is refused, whatever the spelling.
3. The delete itself works through that fd's path (or `unlinkat` relative to a parent fd opened the same way), so a swap between check and delete is also refused (F-0011/F-0012 cover the swap).
findings.how:
- Table test for the policy, with the alias spellings the OpenDisk probe used: `/System/Volumes/Data` + `$HOME`, `.../Data/Users`, `.../Data/Applications`, `.../Data/Library`, `.../Data/private/var`, plus a symlink to `$HOME` made in a temp dir. Every one must be Refused with the same reason as its canonical spelling.
- Unit-test the canonicalizer: `F_GETPATH(open("/System/Volumes/Data" + $HOME))` == `$HOME`.
- Mutation proof: swap the canonicalizer for `realpath` and the alias rows must fail.
findings.verified: Paths are canonicalised with F_GETPATH on the parent folder, so /System/Volumes/Data/Users/<me> resolves to /Users/<me> and is refused, as are symlinked parents and '..'. Tests: ProtectedPathsTests.refusesHomeReachedThroughTheDataVolume, refusesThroughASymlinkedParent, refusesDotDotSegments, TrashServiceTests.protectedItemsNeverReachTheBackend (mutation M2 on T-0044). feat/safety-trash (T-0044)

findings.title: Auto-summary decides from a 100-entry sample that skips subfolders: a 2 GB file (5,901/6,001 positions) or any-size subfolder vanishes into a 'Summarized' tiny-files node (Radix, verified)
findings.problem:
Radix collapses a big directory into one opaque "Summarized (N files)" node. It decides this from a **100-entry stride sample** of the files. Directory entries do not count in that sample, and nothing checks the decision against the real data afterwards. So a folder of ≥ 5,000 tiny files that also holds one multi-GB file, or a subfolder of any size, is usually folded into the summary. Those big items are then never materialized. They do not appear in the sunburst or treemap, in search, in "largest children" or in the file list. The user sees a node labelled as thousands of small files, which suggests harmless clutter, while it may hold a 2 GB video or a 50 GB subfolder. That undermines the one job of a disk map: showing where the big things are.

All citations are colinvkim/Radix@14a76df:

- Thresholds: at depth ≥ 2, a directory with ≥ 5,000 files and an average of ≤ 4,096 B is summarized (`Radix/Services/ScanEngine.swift:767-778`). It is on by default (`Services/AppPreferencesStore.swift:29`).
- Immediate decision: `if childEntries.count >= minFileCount, try immediateChildrenSuggestAtomicDirectory(...)` (`Services/AtomicDirectorySummarizer.swift:68-74, 111-116`). The function looks at `min(100, count)` entries with stride `count/100`, adds `logicalSize` only `if !childMetadata.isDirectory`, and compares the sampled average with 4 KiB (`Services/AtomicDirectorySummaryProbe.swift:57-83`). The full metadata of every child is already in memory from `getattrlistbulk`, so the sampling saves almost nothing.
- Descendant decision: the probe visits at most `max(1_000, minFileCount)` items and extrapolates their average to the whole subtree (`AtomicDirectorySummaryProbe.swift:117-119`, `AtomicDirectorySummaryModels.swift:210-213`).
- There is no second check. Once the sampled test passes, `summarize(...)` walks the whole subtree, subdirectories included (`AtomicDirectoryParallelSummary.swift:583-593`), and returns a single node (`AtomicDirectorySummarizer.swift:179-248`). The only escape is a manual "Expand Fully" on that node (`Features/FileList/FileBrowserTableView.swift:388-392`).
- Radix's own tests cover only the "all files large" case (`RadixCoreTests/ScanEngineTests.swift:4822-4851`).

**Verified (function level):** `research/bench/colinvkim-radix/autosummary_sample_probe.swift` compiles a verbatim copy of `immediateChildrenSuggestAtomicDirectory` with stub types.
- With 6,000 × 1 KiB files and one 2 GiB file, the true average is 358,878 B, which is 87× the threshold. The folder is still summarized in **5,901 of 6,001** positions of the big file in listing order.
- With 5,000 tiny files and one subdirectory, the result is `summarized=true` whatever the subdirectory's size.

The full scan pipeline was not run: `swift test` builds about 91 k lines, and the machine was loaded.
findings.after:
macontrol may still summarize folders of tiny files, since that is how the memory stays bounded. But the decision uses complete data, and a summary never hides a big item:

1. **Decide on all immediate children.** Sum and max are computed over the full `getattrlistbulk` listing, which is already in memory, at O(n) cost and with no I/O. Summarize only if the average is ≤ 4 KiB **and** the largest file is < `bigItemFloor` (default 16 MiB).
2. **Subdirectories are decided on their own.** A child directory is never folded into its parent's summary before it has been listed. Each child either qualifies as a tiny-file folder in its own right, or it stays a real node that gets scanned normally.
3. **Summaries keep their giants.** The summary pass already visits every descendant to total it up. While it does so it keeps a bounded min-heap of the top K = 32 files by allocated size, plus every file ≥ `bigItemFloor`. Those files stay real, selectable children, next to one "N small files" aggregate child. Search, "largest items" and the map therefore always see them.
4. **Label with facts.** For example "Summarized: 6,000 files, largest 2.0 GB". The label shows the real maximum, not a promise that everything inside is small.
findings.how:
- In `ScanEngine`'s summary gate, replace the sampled check with one pass that computes `(fileCount, sumLogical, maxAllocated)` over `childEntries`.
- In the summary walker, add a `TopK<FileEntry>` heap (K = 32, keyed by allocated size). Emit the kept entries as child nodes, plus one synthetic aggregate node whose size is `summary.total − sum(kept)`. This costs about 30 lines. Memory per summarized folder is O(K).
- Acceptance tests with fixtures in a temp dir, depth 2 below the scan root:
  (a) 6,000 × 1 KiB files + one 64 MiB file: the 64 MiB file is a node, and name search finds it.
  (b) 5,000 × 1 KiB files + `sub/` holding one 64 MiB file: `sub` is a real node and not summarized.
  (c) 6,000 × 1 KiB files only: summarized, parent total unchanged, node count ≤ K + 2.
- Regression probe: `research/bench/colinvkim-radix/autosummary_sample_probe.swift`. Our decision function must return "keep" for every one of the 6,001 positions.
findings.verified: feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e (T-0048): the map's merge decision reads every child's size (sorted, full pass, no sampling), so a big item can never be folded away, and the ScanTree itself never summarizes. Test DiskMapGeometryTests.aHugeFileAmongTinyFilesIsNeverMergedAway (6,000 x 1 KiB + one 2 GiB file mid-listing: the big file is its own element in both styles). Deliberate-bug proof: a Radix-style 100-entry listing sample made it fail.

findings.title: Tree stores each node's full path twice (String id + Foundation URL) plus a path-keyed index: 943 B/node, 1M nodes = 900 MiB; URL alone 579 B vs 120 B compact (Radix, verified)
findings.problem:
Every node in a Radix scan stores its full path twice, once as the `String` id and once inside a Foundation `URL`, plus its name. The finished tree adds a dictionary keyed by the full-path `String`. Measured on this Mac, that comes to **943 B per node**, so 1 M materialized nodes take 900 MiB before any UI state. Of that, `URL(fileURLWithPath:)` alone costs **579 B per node**. A compact record (name + parent index + sizes + inode) costs **120 B per node** in the same probe, about 8× less. For macontrol's "fastest" goal, this is the difference between a full-disk map that fits comfortably in RAM and one that pressures memory on 8 GB Macs. It also costs allocation time on every node.

All citations are colinvkim/Radix@14a76df:

- `makeFileNode` sets `id: path` (with `path = url.path`), `url: url` and `name: ScanTarget.displayName(for: url, ...)` (`Radix/Services/ScanEngine.swift:2958-2984`). Leaf and package nodes do the same (`:2986-3089`).
- The record stores `id: String`, `url: URL`, `name: String` and 17 more fields. `MemoryLayout<FileNodeRecord>.stride` is 176 B before any heap storage (`Radix/Models/FileNodeRecord.swift:10-30`).
- The store keeps `nodeRecords: [FileNodeRecord]` and `indexByNodeID: [String: FileTreeNodeIndex]` keyed by that path (`Radix/Models/FileTreeStore.swift:23-31, 418`, built at `ScanEngine.swift:2255-2289`). The arena topology itself is compact (`parentRawIndices: [UInt32]`, `childSpans`, `childIndices`).
- Radix limits node count mainly by auto-summarizing tiny-file folders, and that decision is unreliable (F-0040). Its issue #53 shows memory bugs of this family are real: 73.8 MiB for 3 visible nodes before the fix.

**Verified:** `research/bench/colinvkim-radix/node_memory_probe_main.swift` compiles an **unmodified** copy of `FileNodeRecord.swift` and builds 1,000,000 records exactly as `makeFileNode` does. Paths average 91 B and look like a real home tree; names are ≤ 15 B, which favours Radix because Swift stores those inline. It then measures the `phys_footprint` delta, with each mode in a fresh process:
- Radix model: 900 MiB (943 B/node);
- `URL` only: 579 B/node;
- compact model with heap-allocated names: 115 MiB (120 B/node).

Two runs gave identical results (macOS 26 / Darwin 25.6, Swift 6.3.3, `-O`).

Not measured: how many nodes a real `/` scan keeps after summarization, and the cost on macOS 14/15, where `URL` is CFURL-backed. Both are unverified.

findings.after:
macontrol keeps Radix's arena topology but drops the per-node path and URL:

- **Node = struct-of-arrays row:** `parent: UInt32`, `firstChild/childCount: UInt32`, `name` (a slice into one per-scan UTF-8 name buffer, `offset: UInt32, len: UInt16`), `allocated`, `logical`, `(dev, ino)`, `cloneID`, and one `flags: UInt16` bitset holding dir, symlink, package, summarized, shared, inaccessible and so on. The target is ≤ 64 B per node plus the name bytes. The compact probe row already measures 120 B with a `String` name.
- **Paths are derived, never stored.** A path is built by walking `parent` when it is needed: display, reveal, trash, Quick Look. `URL` objects are created only at that point.
- **Identity lookup** goes through a `[InodeKey: UInt32]` map (`dev, ino`), or by resolving a path one component at a time through the children of each directory. It never uses a full-path `String` dictionary.
- Actions re-validate the derived path against the recorded `(dev, ino)` before acting, which is Radix's own `verifyTrashIdentity` idea. Storing no path therefore costs no safety.
findings.how:
- Implement `ScanTree` as parallel `ContiguousArray`s plus one `[UInt8]` name arena. `path(of:)` walks the parents into a reusable buffer. Only the tree module changes. Geometry and UI read nodes through an index-based API (Radix's `DiskMapTreeReading` protocol shape already fits).
- Bench gate: run the same probe with the macontrol record replacing `FileNodeRecord`. At 1 M nodes it must be ≤ 150 B/node, and `path(of:)` must return 1 M paths in < 1 s.
- End to end, add a peak-footprint column to the T-0004 scan harness for a `~` scan, and compare against Radix's `RADIX_BENCH_FULL_SCAN_SCALING` numbers if someone runs them.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): ScanTree stores parallel arrays and one name byte arena, no paths or URLs: 52 B/node fixed. Measured on the 311,437-node bench fixture: 23.6 MB = 75.8 B/node including names and array slack (mcscan --stats), process max RSS 56 MB. Test: ScanTreeTests.storageStaysUnderEightyBytesPerNode.

findings.title: Trashed items are counted and painted as 'Freed space' (black, like free space) though a same-volume trash frees 0 bytes until emptied (GrandPerspective, verified)
findings.where: GrandPerspective DirectoryViewControl.m:688-699 deleteSelectedFile; TreeContext.m:277-328 deleteSelectedFileItem, :482-513 updateFreedSpaceForDeletedItem; TreeDrawer.m:114-120
findings.problem:
GrandPerspective (GPL-2.0-or-later, SourceForge git @3e0088c, v3.8.1) tells the user that a deleted item's space is "freed" and paints it the same black as the volume's real free space, although its delete is a move to the Trash, which frees nothing until the Trash is emptied.

- `deleteSelectedFile` calls `trashItemAtURL:` and, on success, `[treeContext deleteSelectedFileItem:]` (control/DirectoryViewControl.m:688-699).
- `deleteSelectedFileItem:` replaces the item with a non-physical item labelled `FreedSpace` of the same size (tree/TreeContext.m:281-288). `updateFreedSpaceForDeletedItem:` adds every physical file under it to `_freedSpace`/`_freedFiles` (TreeContext.m:500-510). The Info panel prints that as "Freed space" (control/ControlPanelControl.m:543, en.lproj/Names.strings:155).
- `TreeDrawer` paints freed space with `freeSpaceColor` (black), the colour it also uses for the volume's free space (view/TreeDrawer.m:38, :114-120).
- The code knows the number can be wrong: the comment at TreeContext.m:494-498 counts hard-linked items as freed on purpose, "even though the free space on the harddrive won't be increased until all instances have been deleted". Clones are counted at full size too (see F-0004).

Verified locally (macOS 26.6 25G72, scratchpad probe `trash_probe.swift`): a 64 MiB file moved with `FileManager.trashItem` kept the same (dev, inode) = (16777229, 97959298) and the same `st_blocks*512` = 67,108,864 B at `~/.Trash/...`, and `volumeAvailableCapacity` changed by 0.0 MiB. A same-volume trash is a rename.

Consequence: the user trashes 20 GB in the map, sees a 20 GB black "Freed space" block and a "Freed space: 20 GB" counter, while the disk still has the same free space. This is the classic "I deleted it but the space didn't come back" support question, and the app's own numbers cause it.
findings.after:
macontrol keeps "removed from the map" separate from "space returned to the volume":

- A trashed node becomes an **In Trash** tile, drawn with its own style (hatched, not the free-space colour), with the label "In Trash, frees 1.2 GB when emptied".
- The counters are "Moved to Trash: N items, X GB" and "Freed: Y GB". Freed only counts bytes that have actually left the volume.
- A banner offers **Empty these from Trash**. It permanently removes exactly the items macontrol moved, found by the `resultingItemURL` that `trashItem` returned plus a (dev, inode) recheck. It never empties the user's whole Trash.
- Freed is measured, not assumed: per item it is the clone-aware private size (F-0004), and hard-linked inodes count only when their last link goes (link count 1 before the unlink). After the batch, the sheet reports the `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage` delta next to the computed figure.
- Items on another volume, or on a volume with no Trash, say so, because their trash location and free-space effect differ.

This builds on F-0012 (journal and undo) and F-0018 (count the freed total from real results only). It adds the one thing they do not cover: trash is not free space, and the UI must not say it is.
findings.how:
- Store, per removed node: `{origPath, trashURL, dev, ino, allocSize, privateSize, nlink, state: .inTrash | .freed | .failed}` in the cleanup journal (F-0012).
- Map renderer: a `.inTrash` state gets a distinct fill pattern and a legend entry. Only `.freed` nodes may use the free-space colour.
- "Empty these from Trash": for each journal entry, `lstat(trashURL)` and compare (dev, ino); on a match `unlinkat`/`removeItem`, then state = `.freed`. A mismatch is skipped and logged.
- Acceptance test (fixture, 64 MiB file on the boot volume): after a trash, the UI shows In Trash 64 MiB and Freed 0 B, and the file keeps the same inode under ~/.Trash. After "Empty these from Trash", Freed shows 64 MiB and the volume capacity delta is at least 60 MiB over 2 runs (noise rule from M-0001). A second fixture hard-links the file first and expects Freed 0 B with the note "still linked elsewhere".
findings.verified: feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e (T-0048): trashed nodes are listed as 'In Trash' rows (struck through, not counted) and totalled as 'In Trash: N items, X. Space returns when the Trash is emptied'; there is no 'freed' counter, and the review sheet says 'frees about X once the Trash is emptied'. Test DiskMapModelTests.trashedItemsAreSplicedOutWithoutARescan (inTrashBytes and the In Trash row).

findings.title: Treemap rasterized at 1 px per point and upscaled on Retina: on a 622k-file tree 139,591 files get a tile vs 323,604 at native 2x (GrandPerspective layout, measured)
findings.where: GrandPerspective GradientRectangleDrawer.m:77-111 setupBitmap/createImageFromBitmap; DirectoryView.m:496-531 drawRect, :812-826 startTreeDrawTask; TreeLayoutBuilder.m:33-40
findings.problem:
GrandPerspective (@3e0088c, v3.8.1) renders its treemap at 1 pixel per point and lets AppKit upscale it. On a Retina display the map is half resolution, and every tile smaller than 1 pt (4 device pixels) is dropped.

- The draw task receives the view bounds in points (view/DirectoryView.m:816-820, `bounds: self.bounds`).
- `setupBitmap:` makes an `NSBitmapImageRep` with `pixelsWide: bounds.size.width` and `pixelsHigh: bounds.size.height` in `NSDeviceRGBColorSpace` (view/GradientRectangleDrawer.m:77-90). `createImageFromBitmap` wraps it in an `NSImage` of the same point size (:103-110). `drawRect:` then stretches it over `self.bounds` (DirectoryView.m:528-531).
- The drawing path never reads the backing scale. `grep -rn "backingScale|convertRectToBacking|contentsScale"` over all .m files finds only DirectoryViewControl.m:612, which is the Quick Look zoom frame.
- `TreeLayoutBuilder` stops at any rect that does not contain a pixel centre in these point units (tree/TreeLayoutBuilder.m:33-40), so sub-point items never get a tile.
- Colours are packed as DeviceRGB with no colour management (GradientRectangleDrawer.m:88, :113-118).

Measured with GP's own node, balancer and layout classes compiled `-Os` (like its Deployment config). The probe is `research/bench/sourceforge-net-p-grandperspectiv-source/run_tile_visibility_probe.sh`. It mirrors a folder with fts, using GP's defaults: physical size, hard links counted once, zero-byte files skipped. It then counts the files that get a tile at GP's default window size of 1168x688 pt:

| tree | files | 1x (what GP draws) | 2x (native Retina) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~/projects | 622,664 | 139,591 files (22.4%), 91.9% of bytes | 323,604 files (52.0%), 96.0% of bytes |
| research/sources | 10,325 | 10,244 (99.2%) | 10,307 (99.8%) |

On a large tree, 2.3x as many files are visible at native resolution. At 1x, 8.1% of the bytes sit in files that get no tile at all. This Mac's built-in display is "Retina LCD 2560 x 1600" (system_profiler). I did not screenshot the app itself (unverified). The numbers come from GP's layout code, not from its window.

findings.after:
macontrol lays out and rasterizes the map in device pixels:

- Layout bounds are `bounds × window.backingScaleFactor`. The map re-lays out on `viewDidChangeBackingProperties` when the window moves between a 1x and a 2x screen. The minimum tile is 1 device pixel, not 1 point.
- Tiles are drawn by the GPU (a CALayer with `contentsScale = backingScaleFactor`, or Metal instanced quads) in an sRGB or Display P3 colour space. The CPU never fills pixels in a loop.
- Items too small for even one device pixel are not dropped silently. They are aggregated into one "N small items, X MB" tile per folder, which can be hovered and selected. This is the aggregation rule from F-0016, and the area rule from F-0020 applies.
- A performance budget covers the 4x pixel count: layout is O(visible tiles), and drawing is one instanced draw call per frame.
findings.how:
- `let scale = view.window?.backingScaleFactor ?? 2`, `layer.contentsScale = scale`, `layout(root, in: CGRect(origin: .zero, size: bounds.size * scale))`, and hit-testing divides by `scale`.
- Colour: create the palette as `CGColor` in `CGColorSpace(name: CGColorSpace.displayP3)!`. Do not pack DeviceRGB ints.
- Acceptance test: run the probe tree (or the bench fixture) through macontrol's layout at 1168x688 pt with scale 2. It must give a tile, or an aggregate tile, to 100% of bytes, and it must draw at least as many individual tiles as GP's layout gives at 2336x1376 (323,604 on ~/projects in this measurement). Add one snapshot test at scale 2 so that a scale-1 regression shows up as a visible diff.
findings.verified: feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e (T-0048): layouts take the display scale; the smaller-items thresholds are in device pixels (4 px wedge arc, 100 px^2 tile), and SwiftUI Canvas draws vector paths at the backing scale, re-laid out when the scale changes (it is part of the layout key). Test DiskMapGeometryTests.smallItemThresholdIsInDevicePixels: a 2x layout names more items than a 1x one and no named tile is under the pixel floor.

findings.title: Tree layout/refresh recurse per folder level on 512 KiB NSThread stacks: 3,500 nested folders crash with SIGBUS, 3,000 do not (GrandPerspective, verified; cf. open bug #125)
findings.problem:
GrandPerspective (@3e0088c, v3.8.1) walks its in-memory tree with recursion, one or more native frames per folder level. It runs that recursion on plain NSThreads, whose default stack is 512 KiB. A deep enough folder chain overflows the stack, and the whole app dies with SIGBUS.

- `TreeLayoutBuilder layoutItemTree:inRect:traverser:depth:` recurses into `fileItems`/`directoryItems` and into every `CompoundItem` level (tree/TreeLayoutBuilder.m:29-82). Drawing, overlay drawing, scanning, filtering and XML read/write each run on a thread created by `detachNewThreadSelector:` (util/AsynchronousTaskManager.m:47; the managers are created at view/DirectoryView.m:153,161 and control/MainMenuControl.m:287-319). `NSThread.stackSize` there is 524,288 B (printed by the probe).
- `TreeRefresher` recurses the same way per level (`refreshItemTree` → `refreshVia…ItemTree` → `CompoundItem visitFileItemChildren` → block → `refreshItemTree`, tree/TreeRefresher.m:82-217) and puts more frames on the stack per level. I did not measure it.
- Verified locally (macOS 26.6, `research/bench/sourceforge-net-p-grandperspectiv-source/run_layout_depth_probe.sh`): GP's own Item/DirectoryItem/CompoundItem/TreeBalancer/TreeLayoutBuilder, compiled `-Os`, lay out a chain of N nested folders at the default 1168x688 view. Depths 500 to 3,000 are fine on the thread. 3,500, 4,000 and 8,000 end in "Bus error: 10" (exit 138). The same layout on the 8 MiB main thread survives 8,000. Wide folders are safe: 1,000,000 siblings in the unbalanced list that `addSubdir:` builds visit fine at `-Os`, because the recursion into `second` is a tail call.
- Open bug #125 (v3.6.4, macOS 26.3.1, https://sourceforge.net/p/grandperspectiv/bugs/125/) is a crash on Thread 2 with "EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGBUS) … Thread stack size exceeded due to excessive recursion". The maintainer could not symbolize it, so its root cause is **unconfirmed**. This mechanism is one candidate.
- Chains this deep are pathological, but they do happen: runaway copy or backup loops, and SMB shares that present server-side symlink cycles as real folders (the reporter of bug #130 describes exactly that). A disk tool gets pointed at exactly those broken trees, and a crash loses the scan.
findings.after:
No macontrol tree algorithm uses native recursion whose depth grows with folder nesting:

- Layout, hit-testing, aggregation, filtering, serialization and teardown all run on an explicit work stack (`[(node, rect, depth)]`) in a loop.
- Nodes live in flat arrays (struct-of-arrays, parent and first-child indices). Freeing a tree is one array release, not a dealloc chain whose depth is the tree's depth.
- As a second guard, background threads that touch the tree get an explicit `stackSize` (for example 8 MiB).
- The map has a display depth guard: below N levels, a subtree is drawn as one tile labelled "deeper than N levels".
- The scanner is already fd-relative and not limited by PATH_MAX (F-0008), so a deep tree reaches the model intact. It has to survive the model too.
findings.how:
- Swift: `var work: [(Int32, CGRect, Int16)] = [(root, bounds, 0)]; while let (n, r, d) = work.popLast() { … push children … }`. The same pattern serves `sum`, `filter` and `encode`.
- Bench fixture: add `deepchain/` with a 10,000-level chain (fd-relative mkdir, as `make_fixture.sh` builds `pathmax/`) and a 64 KiB file at the bottom.
- Acceptance test: scan, lay out at 1x and 2x, hit-test the bottom file, trash it and refresh on that fixture, from a background thread created with the default stack size. It must finish, with no crash and correct totals. The GP probe above is the negative control.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): no recursion anywhere (LIFO job stack, iterative record freeing and path rebuilding) and bulk buffers on the heap. Test: ScanEngineTests.fourThousandLevelsOfNesting (4,000 nested folders, 8,000-byte path, scan and measure both exact).
