findings.title: Scan cache saves every scanned name (Mail, Messages, Documents...) unencrypted, 0644, in Application Support: any app without Full Disk Access reads what the FDA scan saw (Neodisk, verified)
findings.where: Neodisk Sources/NeodiskKit/Services/ScanSnapshotCache.swift:136-148 defaultDirectoryURL, :169-238 save, :585-591 writeSlotData; ScanSnapshotCodec.swift:12-27,174,217; DuplicateHashCache.swift (.ndhash keyed by path)
findings.problem:
Neodisk asks for Full Disk Access so that it can scan "Mail, Safari, Messages, and Library content" (`Sources/NeodiskUI/App/SettingsView.swift:268-269`). It then saves every completed scan to disk so that the location reopens instantly and the Changes tab can diff it. The problem is where and how it saves them:

- The folder is `~/Library/Application Support/Neodisk/ScanCache/` (`Sources/NeodiskKit/Services/ScanSnapshotCache.swift:136-148`). Each target keeps its latest `.ndscan` and the one before it (`.prev.ndscan`), plus `.nddiff` change lists, `.nddup` duplicate results and one shared `duplicate-hashes.ndhash`, which is keyed by absolute path (`ScanSnapshotCache.swift:8-19, 103-108`; `DuplicateHashCache.swift:86-89`).
- A snapshot holds **every node's name**, with its size, its mtime and the tree shape. The payload is only LZFSE-compressed, and the metadata JSON (target path, counts) is not compressed at all (`ScanSnapshotCodec.swift:12-27, 174, 217`). There is no encryption, no key and no MAC.
- It is written with `data.write(to:options: .atomic)` at the default mode (`ScanSnapshotCache.swift:230, 590`), so 0644 under a 0700 `~/Library`. Nothing sets `isExcludedFromBackup`, so Time Machine copies it too.

Since `~/Library/Application Support/<app>` is not a TCC-protected location, **any process running as the user, with no Full Disk Access and no Files & Folders grant, can read the complete listing** of everything Neodisk saw with FDA. That includes the names in `~/Library/Mail`, `~/Library/Messages/Attachments`, `~/Library/Safari`, other apps' `~/Library/Containers/*` and `Group Containers/*`, and `~/Desktop`, `~/Documents` and `~/Downloads`. Getting any of those listings directly would take an FDA grant or a user prompt. The cache turns a one-time FDA grant to one app into a free, persistent metadata copy for every app. Apple treats this pattern (protected data copied to an unprotected place) as a TCC bypass.

**Verified locally** (`research/bench/tkslucas-neodisk/cache_tcc_probe.sh`, run twice on macOS 26.6). An ad-hoc-signed app with its own TCC identity, launched through `open` and without FDA, read a canary file in `~/Library/Application Support/<dir>/` (52 bytes, content printed). It got `errno 1 (EPERM)` on `~/Library/Safari`. I did not install Neodisk itself; the path and write mode come from the code cited above.

macontrol will also need FDA, and it will also want persisted scans for instant reopen, diffs and "what grew". So the same design would leak the same data.
findings.after:
Persisted scans must not be readable by processes that lack the access macontrol used to produce them.

1. **Encrypt every persisted scan artifact** (snapshots, diffs, duplicate results, hash cache) with AES-GCM (CryptoKit). Use a random 256-bit key created on first run and stored as a generic-password item in the user's keychain, owned by macontrol's code signature. The ciphertext on disk is useless without the key. Another app asking for the key gets a keychain prompt or a denial (the ACL behaviour of the legacy file keychain vs. the data-protection keychain for a Developer ID app is **unverified**, so decide it with a probe before shipping). If the key is missing, treat that as a cache miss and rescan. It is never an error.
2. **Do not persist names under TCC-protected roots unless the user opts in.** For `~/Library/{Mail,Messages,Safari,Containers,Group Containers,…}`, `~/Desktop`, `~/Documents`, `~/Downloads` and cloud-storage roots, save only an aggregate node (size, file count). Relist them live when the user opens one. This is defence in depth for the case where the key leaks.
3. Set the cache directory to 0700 and the files to 0600, set `URLResourceValues.isExcludedFromBackup = true` on the directory, and delete the cache when the FDA status changes from granted to not granted.
4. The Settings pane says what is stored and has a "Clear scan history" button.
findings.how:
- Add a `SnapshotVault` in front of the cache writer, with `seal(Data) -> Data` and `open(Data) -> Data?`, using `AES.GCM` and a key from `SecItemCopyMatching` / `SecItemAdd`. About 60 lines. Route every `write(to:)` and `Data(contentsOf:)` of the scan cache through it.
- Add a `protectedRoots` list (shared with the FDA probe's sentinel list). The snapshot encoder writes an aggregate record for any node under one of them.
- Acceptance tests:
  (a) Unit: encoding a tree that contains `~/Library/Mail/x.emlx` yields bytes that do not contain `x.emlx`, even after LZFSE decode of the raw file.
  (b) Unit: decoding with a wrong key returns nil (a cache miss), never a crash.
  (c) Manual/CI on a Mac: `research/bench/tkslucas-neodisk/cache_tcc_probe.sh`, pointed at the real macontrol cache file. The non-FDA probe app must print ciphertext only and no path strings.
- Cost: one keychain read per launch. Encrypting a 100 MB snapshot with AES-GCM is well under a second on Apple silicon (unverified here, to be measured by the T-0004 harness).

findings.title: Duplicate hash cache trusts size+mtime+inode (no ctime): an in-place rewrite with restored mtime returns the old full digest, so a unique file can be 'verified identical' and deleted (Neodisk, verified)
findings.where: Neodisk Sources/NeodiskKit/Services/DuplicateHashCache.swift:12-16,41-50,123-131 FileStamp/cachedDigest; DuplicateFinder.swift:303-318 full tier, :470-481 hashableStamp
findings.problem:
Neodisk's duplicate finder caches each file's tier digests (4 KB head, 256 KB head+tail, full SHA-256) across runs. It trusts a cached digest whenever the file's **size + mtime (ns) + inode** match a fresh `stat` (`Sources/NeodiskKit/Services/DuplicateHashCache.swift:12-16, 36-50, 121-131`; stamp built in `DuplicateFinder.swift:470-481`). This holds even for the full-content tier, which is the tier that "confirms" two files are byte-identical (`DuplicateFinder.swift:303-318`).

The header says outright that "a tool that rewrites content while restoring the old mtime defeats it, which is the accepted trade" (`DuplicateHashCache.swift:12-14`). For a read-only viewer that trade only costs a wrong row in a list. For macontrol, which will offer "delete duplicates", a stale digest means **a unique file is shown as a verified duplicate of another, and deleting "the extra copy" destroys the only copy of its content.**

The stamp leaves out `st_ctime`. User-space tools cannot set ctime: `utimes`, `touch -r`, `cp -p` and `rsync -t` all update it. So ctime is the field that would have closed the hole at no cost.

**Verified locally** (`research/bench/tkslucas-neodisk/run_hashcache_probe.sh`, which compiles the source's `DuplicateHashCache.swift` unmodified; run twice). The probe creates a 2 MiB file, caches its full digest, then rewrites the contents in place (same inode, same size) and restores the old mtime with `utimensat`. The result:

    stamp equal after rewrite+restore: true  inode 98013714 -> 98013714
    ctime changed: true
    cache returned digest: true  stale: true
    cached: 5b766f6d76a99963  actual: 7995dfceebfb9fa8

The persisted cache also outlives the scan (`duplicate-hashes.ndhash`, up to 100 000 entries; `DuplicateHashCache.swift:86-90`, `ScanSnapshotCache.swift:564-583`). Duplicate results are also computed on reopened snapshots (commit 8e872b4b). So the window between hashing and acting can be days.
findings.after:
Cached digests may rank and group candidates, but a deletion is never decided from a cached digest.

1. **Stamp = (dev, ino, size, mtime ns, ctime ns).** Add `st_ctimespec` and `st_dev` to the freshness key. User tools cannot restore ctime, so the restore-mtime rewrite misses the cache.
2. **Verify at action time.** When the user confirms "remove N copies", do the following for each copy to be removed. First re-`lstat` the kept copy and the copy to remove, and check (dev, ino, size) against the scan. Then compare the two byte by byte, streaming with `F_NOCACHE`, and do not use the cache. Trash the copy only if the bytes are equal and the identity is unchanged after the compare (re-check `fstat` on the open fds). Any mismatch drops that copy from the batch and shows the reason.
3. **Never offer a clone-only group for deletion** (Neodisk already marks it `isAllClones`, `DuplicateFinder.swift:48-52`), and never offer both sides of a hard link.
4. The UI labels the state honestly: "matched by cache" before verification, "verified identical" after.
findings.how:
- `FileStamp` gains `device: UInt64` and `changedAtNanoseconds: Int64`, and the persisted format version is bumped so old caches drop.
- `DuplicateDeleteVerifier.verify(kept:remove:) async throws -> Verdict` opens both files `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` (so a path swapped for a FIFO cannot block the worker), checks `S_ISREG` via `fstat`, and compares 4 MiB chunks. It is cancellable and bounded like the hashing workers.
- Acceptance tests:
  (a) `research/bench/tkslucas-neodisk/run_hashcache_probe.sh`, ported to macontrol's cache, must print `cache returned digest: false`.
  (b) Fixture: two identical 2 MiB files, hashed and cached. Then rewrite one in place and restore its mtime. The delete flow must refuse with "content changed".
  (c) Fixture: a hard-link pair and a `cp -c` clone pair must never appear as deletable duplicates.

findings.title: Hard-linked files read 0 B in their real folders; the bytes move to a synthetic <Hardlinks> node at the drive root, so a folder that frees 4 MiB shows 0 B, and folder scans skip the rule (WinDirStat #448, model verified; see F-0010)
findings.problem:
WinDirStat handles hard links with a post-scan pass. It is on by default (`ProcessHardlinks` = true, `Options.h:236`). All citations are windirstat/windirstat@da13ad6 (GPL-2.0, study only).

- `DoHardlinkAdjustment` walks the whole drive tree and collects every file whose file index is seen twice or more (`Item.Extended.cpp:843-875`).
- Each such link gets `ITF_HARDLINK`, and its physical size is subtracted from its real parent chain (`Item.Extended.cpp:906-914, 936-940`). `GetSizePhysical()` then returns 0 for it (`Item.cpp:386-389`).
- One copy per index (the max size) is added to a synthetic `<Hardlinks>` item under the drive. It is split into 20 "Index Set" buckets by `index % 20` (`Item.Extended.cpp:746-764, 888-935`). The treemap draws each index there as one brown leaf (`Item.h:239`, `Item.Extended.cpp:1130-1133`).

What this does:
1. **A folder's size no longer tells you what deleting it frees.** A folder whose files are linked only to each other reads 0 B, yet deleting it frees their full size. Probe `research/bench/windirstat-windirstat/hardlink_attribution_probe.py` re-implements the rule above on a real APFS fixture. `A/` holds `x.bin` (4 MiB) and `A/sub/x_link.bin`. WinDirStat's rule gives A = 0.0 M, but freed-if-deleted = 4.0 M. The 8.0 M of linked data sits in `<Hardlinks>` at the drive root, far from the folders that own it.
2. **Folder scans skip the rule.** `FindHardlinksItem` returns nullptr for folder roots (`Item.Extended.cpp:767-771`), and the adjustment only runs for drive items (`WinDirStatModel.Actions.cpp:1245-1253`). So a scan of `C:\Users` counts every link in full (the F-0010 defect), while a scan of `C:\` does not. The same bytes get two different answers.
3. **Every refresh re-walks the whole drive.** This includes the refresh after each delete. It drops and rebuilds the drive's hard-link snapshot (`WinDirStatModel.Actions.cpp:1063-1072, 1245-1253`), an O(files on drive) walk with a hash map reserved at `GetFilesCount()` (`Item.Extended.cpp:846`).

Users asked for in-place attribution in #448 (9 comments, labelled "not planned"). A contributor wrote there: "With hardlinks awareness enabled, disk space saved by hardlinks are counted into `<Unknown>` mixed with the actual unknown amount".

This matters on macOS too. On this Mac, 385 of the 1,833 files in /usr/bin, /usr/sbin and /usr/libexec have st_nlink > 1. Git local clones and pnpm stores create multi-link files in user trees.

Related findings: F-0010 (a link counted once per link), F-0037 (incremental re-count), F-0004 (clones).
findings.after:
macontrol gives the bytes of a multi-link inode to the **deepest folder that contains every link seen in the scan** (the lowest common ancestor, LCA). Each link is still shown in place, with a "linked x N" badge and 0 bytes of its own.

- The total still counts each (st_dev, st_ino) once, so F-0010's rule is kept.
- Every folder's size equals what deleting that folder frees, for the links seen in the scan. In the probe, LCA == freed-if-deleted for A, B, C, D and the root.
- The result is deterministic. It does not depend on which link a parallel walker reached first, so two scans of an unchanged tree agree. F-0010's "first link reached gets the bytes" does depend on traversal order under a parallel scan. LCA replaces that rule, and F-0037's (dev, ino) side table stores the LCA node instead of an owner link.
- When st_nlink is greater than the links seen (other links live outside the scanned root), the bytes stay at the LCA but carry a flag: "also linked outside this scan: deleting frees 0 until the other N links go".
- The same rule applies to folder scans and whole-volume scans.
- It is incremental. A splice or delete updates the LCA only for the inodes it touched, through the (dev, ino) -> [link nodes] table. There is never a whole-volume re-walk.
- There is no synthetic node at the volume root. The map draws one "shared by N links" tile inside the LCA folder.
findings.how:
- Pure-function test on the fixture in `research/bench/windirstat-windirstat/hardlink_attribution_probe.py`. For every folder, displayed size == freed-if-deleted (computed from st_nlink and link locations), and the root total == `du -sk` (each inode counted once).
- Scan `research/bench/fixtures/tree` 3 times with 8 threads. Per-folder sizes must be byte-identical across runs, and totals must equal `visible_to_non_root.allocated_all` in ground_truth.json (the hardlinks/ dir has 503 extra links).
- Delete one link of a 3-link file. Only that inode's attribution may change. Assert that the number of nodes visited is O(links of that inode), not O(tree).
- A scan of a subfolder and a scan of the whole volume give the same size for every folder that both include.
findings.verified: integrator, main c99e07e: a hard-linked file's bytes stay in its real folder. The link with the smallest path keeps them and the other links read 0 B with a sharedHardLink flag; there is no synthetic root node. ScanEngineTests.hardLinkOwnerIsTheSmallestPathInEveryRun checks the owner's real folder over 20 runs. ReclaimTests.hardLinkFreesOnlyWhenEveryLinkIsSelected covers what trashing frees, and DiskMapReviewTests.trashingTheCarryingHardLinkKeepsBytesThatStayOnDisk (its known-issue wrapper was dropped at integration) covers the splice.

findings.title: Dedupe replaces each duplicate with a hard link: an edit to either path then changes both, the replaced file takes the kept file's mode and mtime (600 became 644), and failed links are skipped silently (WinDirStat #655, APFS probe; see F-0046)
findings.problem:
WinDirStat's "deduplicate with hardlink" action runs from the duplicate list with 2 or more files selected. It replaces every selected copy except the first of each hash group with a hard link to that first copy. Citations are windirstat/windirstat@da13ad6 (GPL-2.0, study only).

- `OnCreateHardlink` builds (source, target) pairs from the duplicate groups. After one confirmation it calls `CreateHardlinkFromFile` for each pair (`WinDirStatModel.Actions.cpp:1401-1436`).
- `CreateHardlinkFromFile` creates a link to the source named `<target><GUID>`, then uses `MoveFileEx(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` to put it over the target (`HelpersTasks.cpp:688-704`).
- The groups are the ones built during the scan: size first, then XXH3-64 over the first 4 KiB, then 1 MiB, then the whole file (`Controls/FileDupeControl.cpp:56, 63, 84, 103-108`; `HelpersTasks.cpp:775-778`). Neither file is read again before the replace. The only guards are "scan settled", "not sampled" and "same volume" (`WinDirStatModel.Actions.cpp:1370-1399, 1404`).
- The bool returned by `CreateHardlinkFromFile` is dropped (`:1431`). In #655 the reporter says NTFS's 1024-link limit "stops the hardlink operation entirely", and after the fix that it "still happens silently".
- The detector has shipped false duplicates before: #175 "dedup is buggy", #267 "Duplicates identified of nonidentical files", #368 "files of different size ... reported as duplicates". In #655, two hash groups were merged into one (4 files became 1 inode) until 860d840 ("Correct Hardlink Creation Group", 2026-09-05).

Measured on APFS with `research/bench/windirstat-windirstat/dedupe_probe.sh`. It uses the same shape: link to a temp name, then rename over the target. Output is in results.txt.
- After the replace, `dup.bin` has `keep.bin`'s inode, mode (`-rw-r--r--` instead of its own `-rw-------`) and mtime (2026 instead of 2020). A private file became world-readable.
- Appending 1 byte to `keep.bin` makes `dup.bin` 1,048,577 bytes too. The "duplicate" is now the same file.
- An edit made to `dup.bin` after the hash was taken is lost ("dup.bin edit LOST").

F-0046 (Neodisk) already requires byte verification at action time before any delete. This finding covers what F-0046 does not: the replacement primitive, the replaced file's metadata, and reporting failures.
findings.after:
If macontrol offers "reclaim space from duplicates without deleting them", it replaces a copy with an **APFS clone, never a hard link**. It verifies first and reports every pair:

1. At action time, for each pair: re-`lstat` both files and check (dev, ino, size, mtime, ctime) against the scan. Then byte-compare them with `F_NOCACHE` (F-0046, step 2). Skip pairs that are already the same inode or already clones (equal `ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONEID`).
2. Call `clonefile(keep, <target dir>/.macontrol-dedupe-<uuid>, CLONE_NOFOLLOW)` (SDK sys/clonefile.h:33,51). Copy the target's own metadata onto the clone with `copyfile(target, tmp, NULL, COPYFILE_METADATA)`. That is STAT|ACL|XATTR (copyfile.h:93-98): mode, owner, flags, times, ACL and xattrs. Then call `renamex_np(tmp, target, RENAME_SWAP)` (sys/stdio.h:36,52). The swap leaves the original at the temp name. Byte-compare the new target against keep once more, then move the swapped-out original into macontrol's quarantine (F-0012) instead of unlinking it.
3. If the target's fstat changed during the compare, swap back and skip the pair.
4. Report every failure per pair (not APFS, EXDEV, ENOTSUP, file changed). The summary reads "N of M replaced, X bytes reclaimed". X is measured with `ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE`, not file size (F-0004).
5. The UI says what happened in plain words: "copies stay separate files; editing one never changes the other".
findings.how:
- Fixture test, shaped like dedupe_probe.sh: two equal files with different modes, mtimes and xattrs. After the dedupe they have different inodes, the target keeps its own metadata, appending to one leaves the other unchanged, and the target's private size is about 0.
- Race test: edit the target between scan and action. The pair is skipped with a reason, and its bytes are intact.
- Failure test: put the target on a small HFS+ disk image (`hdiutil create -fs HFS+ -size 20m`). The error is reported for that pair, nothing is replaced, and the other pairs still run.
- Grep check: the dedupe code path contains no `link(`/`linkat(` call.

findings.title: File-type colours are 18 saturated hues by rank: green/yellow (ranks 3/4) are dE00 7.0 apart for deuteranopes and 4.7 for protanopes, 22 of 136 pairs fall under dE00 10, and every type from rank 18 down shares one gray (WinDirStat, measured)
findings.problem:
WinDirStat colours each treemap leaf by its file extension. `RebuildExtensionData` ranks extensions by total bytes and gives rank r the colour `colors[min(r, 17)]` from an 18-entry palette (`WinDirStatModel.cpp:460-496`). The palette is fully saturated primaries and secondaries plus white, each normalised to brightness 0.6 (`Controls/TreeMap.h:355-374`, `TreeMap.cpp:247-252`, `TreeMap.h:91-169`). Cushion shading then varies each tile's lightness from ambient 0.13 up to full (`TreeMap.cpp:1006-1069`). So lightness cannot carry the category, and only hue does. All citations are windirstat/windirstat@da13ad6 (GPL-2.0, study only).

`research/bench/windirstat-windirstat/palette_probe.py` measures this with CIEDE2000 and the Machado 2009 colour-vision-deficiency simulation at severity 1.0. Output is in results.txt.
- Normal vision: 7 of the 136 pairs among the 17 distinct ranks are under ΔE00 10. Examples: violet/indigo 5.3, spring green/aquamarine 6.6, hot pink/deep pink 6.8.
- Deuteranopia: 22 pairs are under 10. Blue (rank 1) vs indigo (rank 17) is 1.4, yellow (4) vs lime (10) is 1.8, green (3) vs yellow (4) is 7.0.
- Protanopia: 21 pairs are under 10. Green vs yellow is 4.7, violet vs indigo 0.4.
- Every rank from 18 down gets the same gray (153,153,153). A disk has hundreds of extensions, so a large part of the map is one colour with no legend row that names it.
- Pseudo items reuse palette hues. `<Unknown>` is yellow + LIGHTER and `<Free Space>` is gray + DARKER (`Item.Extended.cpp:1115-1128`). Unknown space therefore looks like rank 4, and free space like the rank-18+ bucket.
- Rank uses logical bytes (`Item.cpp:53-55, 519-525`; `WinDirStatModel.cpp:463-475`), but the map area uses physical bytes by default (`Item.Extended.cpp:483-486`, `Options.h:229`). For sparse, compressed or cloned files, the colour order and the area order can disagree.
- Ranks are recomputed every scan, so a type's colour changes between disks and between scans.

The same codebase already has a better palette. Folder frames, sunburst and flame-graph branches use an 8-colour palette close to Okabe-Ito, which is designed for colour-vision deficiency. It is blended toward the background by depth (`Controls/TreeMap.cpp:105-108, 165`). Only the file-type cushion palette still uses the saturated 18.
findings.after:
- **Colour by kind, not by extension.** Use about 8-10 fixed kinds: video, images, audio, archives & disk images, apps & bundles, developer artifacts, documents, caches & logs, system, other. They are mapped by UTType conformance (for example `UTType(filenameExtension:)?.conforms(to: .movie)`), with bundle detection for .app and .photoslibrary. A kind keeps its colour across scans and disks.
- **The palette is tested.** A unit test checks that every pair of kind colours is at least ΔE00 10 apart in normal vision and under deutan and protan simulation, in both light and dark appearance. palette_probe.py's `de2000`/`simulate` are the reference implementation.
- **Hue is not the only channel.** The hover label names the kind. The legend is clickable and highlights every tile of that kind; keep WinDirStat's extension-highlight behaviour (`Views/TreeMapView.cpp:98-115`). "Other" is a named legend row that lists its extensions.
- Unknown/purgeable space and free space get a treatment outside the palette (hatched or neutral outline), so they cannot be mistaken for a file kind.
- The legend's sizes and order use the same size metric as the map.
findings.how:
- Unit test `palette_distinct`: port `de2000` and `simulate` from palette_probe.py, or run the Python in CI, against the app's kind colours. Assert min pairwise ΔE00 >= 10 for normal, deutan and protan, for both appearances.
- Snapshot test: render the fixture treemap. Every leaf's fill must belong to the kind palette, and each legend row's byte sum must equal the sum of its tiles' sizes.
- Manual check: turn on System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Color Filters (Deuteranopia, Protanopia) and confirm the demo tree's kinds can still be told apart.
findings.verified: feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e (T-0048): map colour is one hue per top-level branch (8 hues) plus a neutral grey for smaller items, chosen by exhaustive search with palette_probe.py's de2000/simulate: 0 of 36 pairs under dE00 10; closest normal 15.72, deutan 14.96, protan 15.21. Tests DiskMapPaletteTests.everyPairOfBranchColoursIsAtLeastTenApartUnderDeutanAndProtan (Swift port checked against the probe's reference value) and theRingNeverClosesOnTwoNeighboursOfOneColour. Hue is not the only channel: tooltips, list rows and the inspector name every item.

findings.title: Hard delete (rm -rf) runs on the raw multi-selection: the auto-selected scan root stays in it when children are Cmd-clicked, and the 7-line confirmation (hash order) can hide it (QDirStat #267/#293/#316)
findings.where: qdirstat@88a577f CleanupCollection.cpp:295-308 execute, :26,361-379 confirmation; MainWindow.cpp:595,495,808-809 root auto-select; StdCleanup.cpp:162-176
findings.problem:
QDirStat's "Delete (no way to undelete!)" (`rm -rf %p`, Ctrl+Delete and a toolbar button) runs once for **every item in the raw selection**. That includes a directory selected together with its own descendants. The scan root is auto-selected when every scan finishes. So a user who expands a branch and Ctrl-clicks two children gets a selection of three items, and the root is one of them. The confirmation shows at most 7 paths, taken in QSet hash order, so with 8 or more items the root can fall behind "...". Nothing refuses the scan root, `$HOME` or `/`.

All citations are shundhammer/qdirstat@88a577f (2,593 stars, GPL-2.0-only, `gh api repos/shundhammer/qdirstat`, 2026-09-23). The macOS build `jesusha123/qdirstat-macos` 2.0-macos.2 compiles the same code unpatched.

1. **No normalization, on purpose.** `CleanupCollection::execute` (src/CleanupCollection.cpp:295-308) says "Intentionally not using the normalized FileInfoSet here" and calls `cleanup->execute(item)` for each selected item. Only the AssumeDeleted refresh path normalizes (:313-327).
2. **The root is selected for you.** `openDir` sets `_futureSelection.setUrl(url)` (src/MainWindow.cpp:595). When reading finishes, `applyFutureSelection()` (:495) calls `setCurrentItem(sel, true)` (:808-809). The tree view uses `ExtendedSelection` (src/DirTreeView.cpp:43), so a Ctrl-click adds to that selection instead of replacing it.
3. **Confirmation is truncated, and its order is random.** `FileInfoSet` is a `QSet<FileInfo *>` (src/FileInfoSet.h:23). `confirmation()` takes `urls.mid(0, 7)` (src/CleanupCollection.cpp:26,361-379) in set iteration order, which follows the pointer hash, and appends "... (N items total)". The paths go unescaped into an `<html>` rich-text message (:349-352, 408-414). Whether a crafted name can hide lines is unverified.
4. **No guard.** A grep for `homePath|isToplevel` in Cleanup*.cpp finds nothing. The command is plain `rm -rf` (src/StdCleanup.cpp:162-176).

**User impact, reported upstream:**
- #316 (2026-08, "QDirStat wiped my /home directory"). The maintainer's reconstruction: the toplevel stays selected and the Ctrl-clicks are added to it.
- #267 (2023): the parent was deleted "in the middle of a list of its subdirectories". The output window showed `rm -rf` of the parent, and then its children failed.
- #293 (2025): 100 GB lost.

The maintainer declined to change the flow ("I do that all the time", #267).
findings.after:
In macontrol, a delete acts on a **normalized plan**, never on the raw selection:

- **Plan = normalized selection.** Before anything is shown, drop every item that has a selected ancestor, and dedupe by (dev, inode). The confirmation says "3 selected, 1 folder already includes 2 of them" when that happens. That makes the ancestor visible as the unit that will be removed.
- **The scan root and protected ancestors are not deletable from the map.** The scan root, the volume root, `$HOME` and its top-level folders (Desktop, Documents, Library...), and anything on the protected list (see F-0024/F-0039) cannot enter a delete plan. The Delete action greys out and explains why. Selecting the scan root is only for showing its details and is never a delete target.
- **No sticky implicit selection.** After a scan, or when drilling into a folder, the root is the *focused/current* item but not *selected*. A Cmd-click then starts a new selection instead of extending one the user never made.
- **Confirmation shows the whole plan, deterministically.** Sort it by size, largest first, and name the 5 largest. Always add "N items, X GB total", plus a line "includes folder <name> (Y GB, Z items)" for every folder in the plan. Render the names as plain text (SwiftUI `Text(verbatim:)`), never as markup.
- Move to Trash with a journal, not `rm -rf`, as the default (F-0012, T-0026). Undo covers the rest.
findings.how:
- `DeletionPlanner.plan(selection: Set<NodeID>, tree:) -> Plan` does four things:
  - It removes descendants with one pass over the selection sorted by path depth, checking whether a selected ancestor exists through the parent chain.
  - It rejects protected nodes, returning a `Plan.blocked([NodeID: Reason])`.
  - It computes the totals from the tree (clone- and hard-link-aware sizes, F-0004/F-0010).
  - It exposes `topItems(5)` and `folders` for the sheet.
- Selection model: `focused: NodeID?` and `selected: Set<NodeID>` are kept separate. Scan completion and drill-down set only `focused`.
- Tests:
  - Select {root, root/a, root/a/b, root/c} and assert that the plan is blocked for root. With the root removed, assert the plan is {root/a, root/c}.
  - Select 9 siblings plus their parent and assert that the sheet lists the parent as a folder line, whatever the hash order.
  - Give a node a name containing `<b>` and `<!--` and assert the sheet text shows it literally.
findings.verified: A selected item inside another selected item is never trashed separately: items run shallowest-first and a descendant of a trashed folder is reported as trashed via it; '/' or home in a multi-selection is refused while the rest proceeds. Tests: TrashServiceTests.trashesAnAncestorAndItsSelectedDescendantOnce (one backend call, one journal line), protectedItemsNeverReachTheBackend (mutation M5 on T-0044). feat/safety-trash (T-0044)

findings.title: Action templates expand %p, %n, %d in sequence: a '%d' in a filename re-expands inside the quoted path, so rm -rf gets split args, '&' in the folder name runs a command, $(...) executes (QDirStat, verified)
findings.problem:
QDirStat's cleanup actions are shell templates. `Cleanup::expandVariables` fills them with three **sequential** `QString::replace` calls: `%p`, then `%n`, then `%d`. Each value is correctly single-quoted, with `'` escaped as `'\''`. But the second and third passes also scan the text that the first pass inserted. A path that itself contains `%n` or `%d` gets another quoted string spliced into the middle of its own quotes. That closes the quote, so the parent directory's text ends up **unquoted** in the `sh -c` command.

The results:
- The path splits into several `rm -rf` arguments, one of them relative to the item's directory.
- A `&` or `;` in the directory name becomes a shell operator, and the rest of the name runs as a command.
- `$(...)` in the directory name executes.

Realistic names that trigger it include `Sales 100%done.xlsx`, `frame%d.png` (printf-style frame patterns) and `100%natural`.

Citations are shundhammer/qdirstat@88a577f (2,593 stars, GPL-2.0-only), unchanged in the shipped macOS build 2.0-macos.2:
- src/Cleanup.cpp:176-196 `expandVariables` (replace %p, %n, %d in that order)
- :199-225 `quoted`/`escaped`
- :265-294 `runCommand`: `QProcess(shell, ["-c", cmd])`, with the cwd set to the item's directory
- :336-372: the shell is `$SHELL` first, which is zsh on macOS
- Templates that use `%p` include the default Delete, `rm -rf %p` (src/StdCleanup.cpp:162-176), and any user action.

**Verified-locally (macOS 26.6).** `research/bench/shundhammer-qdirstat/expand_probe.py` is a behavioural model of those lines. Python `str.replace` has the same non-rescanning semantics as `QString::replace`. I ran each expanded command through /bin/zsh and /bin/bash with `rm` shadowed by an argv printer, inside a temp dir. Output is in `expand_probe.out`:

- `My Files/Sales 100%done.xlsx` with `rm -rf %p` expands to `rm -rf '$TMP/My Files/Sales 100'$TMP/My Files'one.xlsx'`. rm receives `<$TMP/My Files/Sales 100$TMP/My>` and `<Filesone.xlsx>`. The file is not deleted (`-f` stays silent), and a sibling named `Filesone.xlsx` in cwd would be.
- `Tom & Jerry/frame%d.png` makes zsh background an `rm` and then run `Jerry.png` as a command ("command not found: Jerry.png", exit 127).
- `x$(touch PWNED)/frame%d.png` runs the substitution: the marker file was created in the item's directory, in both shells.

The item's directory comes from disk, so any downloaded archive or synced folder can supply such names. This is related to F-0002, where shell strings are built from paths in the Pearcleaner helper. The difference here is that correct POSIX escaping still fails, because the template engine re-expands its own output.
findings.after:
If macontrol ships user-defined actions ("Open in…", "Run script on selection"), paths never become shell text:

- **Paths are passed as data.** Tokenize the template **once**, left to right, into literal segments and placeholder tokens. Emit an argv array, with each `{path}`/`{name}`/`{dir}` becoming its own argv element. No substituted value is scanned again.
- **When the user writes shell,** run `/bin/sh -c '<user script>' macontrol <path1> <path2> …` and document `"$1"`/`"$@"` as the only way to reach the paths. The script text is fixed and user-authored, and paths only arrive as positional parameters. The shell never parses them.
- **No `rm` template for delete.** Built-in delete and trash stay in-process (`FileManager.trashItem`, journaled, F-0012/T-0026). Custom actions cannot be bound as the Delete key or button.
- **Preview.** The action sheet shows the exact argv (one line per argument) before the first run, and it is logged per run.
findings.how:
- `ActionTemplate.parse(_ s: String) -> [Token]` is a single-pass scanner over `{path}`, `{name}`, `{dir}` and `{{`. `render(tokens, item) -> [String]` returns argv.
- Run it with `Process.executableURL` plus `arguments`. There is no `-c` unless the user chose "shell script", and in that case the paths go in as positional args after `$0`.
- Test: port the 4 probe cases (`Sales 100%done.xlsx`, `Tom & Jerry/frame%d.png`, `x$(touch PWNED)/frame%d.png`, plus a name with `'`). Assert that argv equals exactly `[path]`, that no marker file appears, and that an `rm` stand-in receives the path byte-for-byte.
- Reference probe: `research/bench/shundhammer-qdirstat/expand_probe.py` (keep it as a regression oracle for any template feature).

findings.title: Every delete re-reads the parent from disk (the whole tree when it is the scan root) and disables all delete actions until the rescan ends; the no-I/O splice exists but is opt-in (QDirStat #293)
findings.where: qdirstat@88a577f DirTree.cpp:201-245 refresh; CleanupCollection.cpp:156-157 updateActions; StdCleanup.cpp:172; MainWindow.cpp:335,1159-1165
findings.problem:
After every Delete or Move to Trash, QDirStat throws away the parent's subtree and **re-reads it from disk**. If the parent is the scan root, it rescans the **entire tree**. Until that finishes, every refreshing action is disabled: Delete, Move to Trash, Clear Directory, Compress, make clean and git clean. So a cleanup session turns into delete, then a full rescan, then delete again.

Citations are shundhammer/qdirstat@88a577f (2,593 stars, GPL-2.0-only):
- Delete uses `RefreshParent` (src/StdCleanup.cpp:172). Move to Trash builds `Refresher::parents(selection)` (src/MainWindow.cpp:1159-1165).
- `DirTree::refresh(DirInfo*)`:
  - If the subtree has no parent, meaning it is the scan root, it calls `startReading(firstToplevel()->url())`, a full new scan (src/DirTree.cpp:220-224).
  - Otherwise it runs `clearSubtree` plus `reset` plus a new `LocalDirReadJob` (:231-244).
  - Deleting any direct child of the scan root therefore rescans everything.
- While the tree is busy, `updateActions` disables every cleanup whose refresh policy is not NoRefresh (src/CleanupCollection.cpp:156-157). Move to Trash is disabled while `reading` (src/MainWindow.cpp:335).
- The scanner is single-threaded on the GUI thread (a grep for QThread/QtConcurrent/std::thread in src/ finds nothing, and see DirReadJob.cpp:854-860). The rescan costs as much as the first scan.
- A cheap path exists but is opt-in: the `AssumeDeleted` policy splices the nodes out without I/O (src/Cleanup.h:188, src/CleanupCollection.cpp:313-327). No default action uses it, and it cannot be combined with Recurse (src/Cleanup.cpp:97-104, issue #251).

**User evidence.** In issue #293 (2025) a user writes that the delete button's "full refresh each time you activate it… can take over an hour. Even a few hours!", and that they switched to a custom AssumeDeleted action. The maintainer measured 2.8 s for 360k files on Linux. Scan cost on macOS is higher: on the T-0004 bench, a serial `du` over about 469k entries took 5.9 s warm (F-0009). That is a code-read plus user-report finding. I did not time QDirStat itself because there is no Qt on this Mac.
findings.after:
In macontrol, a delete updates the model **in place** and is verified **per item**. The rest of the tree is not rescanned:

- **Splice.** For each item in the plan, `trashItem` succeeds, then `lstat(original path)` returns ENOENT, then the node is removed and its size is subtracted from every ancestor, in O(depth). The node becomes an "In Trash" record if F-0042 is followed.
- **A failure stays on the map.** If trashing an item fails, or it still exists afterwards, the node stays and is marked with the error. Only the affected directory is re-read, and only when the user asks. No policy knob is needed.
- **The map stays usable.** The next delete is available immediately. Background FSEvents reconciliation (F-0017/F-0037/F-0038) catches outside changes later, per dirty directory. Deletes never trigger a whole-tree rescan.
- **Measured, not assumed.** The freed-space line uses the volume capacity delta after the batch (F-0042). Nothing depends on a re-read of the tree.
findings.how:
- `Tree.remove(node:)` subtracts `node.totalAllocated` (clone/hard-link aware per F-0004/F-0010) from its ancestors and unlinks the node. Unit-test it against a fresh scan of the same fixture, where the totals must match byte-exactly.
- `DeleteExecutor` runs the plan off the main actor. For each item it calls `trashItem`, then `lstat`, then `tree.remove`, and publishes progress. Actions stay enabled while a background scan or reconcile runs. They work on the snapshot, and the executor re-validates (dev, inode) before each trash.
- Test: scan the fixture, delete a direct child of the root, and assert that there is no new scan job (count of walker invocations = 0) and that the root total drops by exactly the child's size. Then delete a second item without waiting.
findings.verified: feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e (T-0048): after Move to Trash, DiskMapModel.apply(_:) splices each trashed node out with ScanTree.removeSubtree (O(depth)), without a rescan; refused or failed items stay on the map and in the pile with their reason, and staging stays available at once. Test DiskMapModelTests.trashedItemsAreSplicedOutWithoutARescan (totals drop by exactly the trashed bytes, tree version bumps once, focus leaves the removed folder, next item stages immediately); refusalsLeaveTheMapAndThePileAsTheyWere covers the refusal path.

findings.title: Move to Trash on macOS writes to ~/.local/share/Trash (XDG spec): Finder never sees it, Empty Trash never frees it, restore/empty not implemented (QDirStat 2.0-macos.2, verified in shipped binary)
findings.problem:
QDirStat's "Move to Trash" follows the freedesktop.org (Linux) trash spec on every platform:
- Items on the home volume go to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/Trash` or `~/.local/share/Trash/files`, with a `.trashinfo` next to them.
- Items on other volumes go to `<volume>/.Trash/$UID` or `<volume>/.Trash-$UID`.

On macOS the result:
- Finder's Trash (`~/.Trash`, `<volume>/.Trashes/$UID`) never sees the item, and it has no Put Back record.
- **Emptying the Trash in Finder never frees the space.**
- On external disks it creates a hidden `.Trash-501` folder at the volume root.
- QDirStat itself cannot restore or empty: `Trash::restore()` and `Trash::empty()` are "Not implemented".
- The output window says "Moved to trash: <path>", and the refresh removes the item from the map. The user believes the space is on its way back, but the bytes are now in an invisible folder under `~/.local`.

Citations are shundhammer/qdirstat@88a577f (2,593 stars, GPL-2.0-only):
- src/Trash.cpp:40-53: the home trash is `QDir::homePath() + "/.local/share"` + `/Trash`, with no `Q_OS_MAC` branch. A grep for Q_OS_MAC in src/ finds only Cleanup.cpp:486, DirReadJob.cpp:406, MainWindow.cpp:186 and SysUtil.cpp:27.
- :106-174: the per-volume `.Trash-%1`.
- :177-199 `trash()`, and :300-313 `QFile::rename`.
- :204-218: "Not implemented".
- src/MainWindow.cpp:1139-1183: `moveToTrash`, with no confirmation and a success message per item.

**Verified in the shipped macOS app.** `jesusha123/qdirstat-macos` release 2.0-macos.2 (2026-08-23, 131 stars) builds upstream at `cb014eb` with no source patches (.github/workflows/build.yml only appends to src.pro). `gh api .../contents/src/Trash.cpp?ref=cb014eb` shows the same lines 40-48. I mounted `QDirStat.dmg` read-only, and `strings -a QDirStat.app/Contents/MacOS/QDirStat` finds `/.local/share`, `/.Trash` and `/.Trash-%1` in both architecture slices. Nothing refers to `~/.Trash` or an NSFileManager trash API. I did not click Move to Trash, because there is no GUI automation of a third-party app on this Mac.

This is related to F-0042 (GrandPerspective counts trashed bytes as freed). Here the trash is not even the system Trash.
findings.after:
macontrol uses only the platform trash, and it proves where the item went:

- `FileManager.default.trashItem(at:resultingItemURL:)` for everything the user owns. It picks the right per-volume Trash (`~/.Trash`, `/Volumes/X/.Trashes/<uid>`) and writes Finder's Put Back record (verified-locally in the T-0010 report). The privileged helper path is the typed `trash(paths:)` from F-0002.
- Check `resultingItemURL`. It must be non-nil, and its path must be inside a Trash directory of the same volume. Journal it (T-0026) so that Undo and "Empty just these" (F-0042) find the exact item.
- If a volume has no Trash (some network or FAT volumes), `trashItem` throws. The UI then offers "Delete permanently" as an explicit second step, and nothing falls back silently.
- The copy says "Moved to Trash (frees X GB when emptied)", never "freed".
findings.how:
- A single `TrashService.trash(_ url: URL) throws -> TrashRecord { original, resulting, dev, ino, bytes }` is used by every delete path. A lint or grep check in CI forbids `rename`/`moveItem` into any path containing `/Trash` or `/.local/share`.
- Test (no TCC prompt, scratch dir on the boot volume): trash a temp file. Assert that `resulting.path` starts with `NSHomeDirectory()/.Trash/`, that `~/.local/share/Trash` does not exist or is untouched, and that the Undo from the journal restores the original path and inode.
- Manual check on an external APFS or ExFAT disk: the resulting URL is under `/Volumes/X/.Trashes/<uid>/` and no `.Trash-<uid>` folder is created.
findings.verified: The default backend is FileManager.trashItem, i.e. Finder's Trash with Put Back and per-volume .Trashes (topic-platform-constraints D1-D5, verified-locally); no XDG path exists. SafetySinkTests.safetyOnlyTrashesAndRestores asserts exactly one FileManager.default.trashItem(at: call in Sources/Safety. Tests never trash for real, so the Finder side rests on the D1-D5 probes. feat/safety-trash (T-0044)

findings.title: Per-folder sizes change between identical scans: a shared hard link or APFS clone is charged to whichever folder the parallel walk reaches first (dua, verified: 17/13 of 30 runs; see F-0047)
findings.where: Byron/dua-cli@cf59618 src/inodefilter.rs add_dev_inode / ApfsFilter::add_clone; src/aggregate.rs:332-334; src/traverse.rs integrate_traversal_event
findings.problem:
dua counts each hard-linked inode and (with `--deduplicate-apfs-clones`) each full APFS clone group once, which keeps the **total** right. But the bytes go to whichever link or clone the parallel walker hands over first, and that order is not fixed. So identical scans of an unchanged disk give different **per-folder** sizes. A folder's row, its percentage, its sort position and (in a disk map) its tile size change between rescans, and a folder can show "8 MB" in one scan and "160 KB" in the next.

It also misleads deletion. The folder that happens to hold the bytes looks like the place to reclaim them. Deleting it frees nothing for a hard link (the other link keeps the data) and nothing for a clone (the other clone keeps the blocks).

Verified locally (macOS 26.6, dua 2.45.0 Homebrew, source @cf59618). Fixture: `A/` and `B/` each hold 40 small files and one 8 MiB file. In `hl/` the two big files are hard links of one inode. In `cl/` they are `cp -c` clones of a third file outside the root. `du -sk hl` = 8512 KiB.
- `dua -f bytes aggregate --depth 2 hl`, 30 runs: A charged 8,552,448 B in 17 runs, B in 13 (the other folder shows 163,840 B). A later 20-run pass: 14 / 6.
- `dua -f bytes --deduplicate-apfs-clones aggregate --depth 2 cl`, 30 runs: 16 / 14. A later pass: 12 / 8.
- Two roots, `dua aggregate hl/A hl/B`, 30 runs: 15 / 15.
- Interactive mode (`dua i`, ParentFirst order, driven through a pty with `--once`), 12 runs: A 5, B 7.
Totals were byte-identical in every run, so a totals-only check (the bench's `total_stable_across_runs`) cannot see this.

Related findings: F-0010's "after" says "the first link reached gets the bytes", and under a parallel walker "first reached" is a race. F-0047 (WinDirStat) argued the same point from a model and proposed the lowest-common-ancestor rule for hard links. This finding measures the race in a real parallel engine, the one T-0006 proposes to port, and shows it also affects APFS clone groups, which F-0047 does not cover.
findings.after:
macontrol does not port dua's first-seen `InodeFilter` rule. Shared bytes go to an owner that the walk order cannot change:

1. **Hard links: use F-0047's lowest-common-ancestor rule.** The bytes of a multi-link inode go to the deepest folder that contains every link seen. F-0047 proposed that rule because first-seen attribution depends on traversal order. This finding is the measured proof of that in the fastest parallel engine we studied.
2. **Full APFS clone groups: same rule.** Key the group by `(dev, ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONEID)`, counted only when `EF_MAY_SHARE_BLOCKS` is set, as dua does. Charge the shared data-fork allocation once, at the LCA of all members seen. Each member keeps only its private part (`allocated - data_allocated`, as `src/inodefilter.rs:177-186` computes it) and gets a "cloned x N" badge. If `ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONE_REFCNT` is larger than the number of members seen, add the flag "also cloned outside this scan: deleting frees 0". The "frees now" figure stays as F-0004 defines it.
3. **One entry point for every writer.** Full scan, subtree refresh and FSEvents splice all update the `(dev, ino)` and `(dev, cloneid)` side tables through one function (F-0037). dua's refresh builds a fresh `InodeFilter` (`src/traverse.rs:1137`), and that is how its refresh ends up double counting (see T-0022, F-0037).

Result: a scan of an unchanged disk gives byte-identical per-node sizes and the same sort order every time, with any worker count.
findings.how:
- Probe: `research/bench/byron-dua-cli/attribution_probe.sh [runs]`. It builds an A/B hard-link fixture and an A/B clone fixture in a temp dir and counts which folder dua charges on each run. Its optional Q2 drives the TUI through `pty_once.py`, which needs pyte in a venv, and shows the refresh double count.
- macontrol acceptance test: scan that fixture 20 times with 8 workers and dump `(path, size)` for every node. All 20 dumps must be byte-identical. For both `hl/` and `cl/`, the 8 MiB must sit on the parent folder (the LCA), with A and B at 163,840 B each. Add a third link under `hl/C/` and splice only `C/`. The bytes must stay on `hl/`, and no total may change.
- Bench: next to `total_stable_across_runs`, add `per_node_stable_across_runs` to research/bench/run.sh by hashing each run's depth-2 listing. Then this race is caught for every parallel scanner, including ours.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): ScanTree.finalizeTotals charges each hard-linked inode to the link with the byte-wise smallest path, so per-folder sizes do not depend on which worker met a link first. Tests: ScanEngineTests.hardLinkOwnerIsTheSmallestPathInEveryRun (20 runs, one set of folder sizes), ScanTreeTests.smallestPathKeepsHardLinkBytesInAnyInsertionOrder, BenchFixtureTests (503 extra links, identical per-folder sizes 20/20). Clones stay at full size in the map, as in Finder and du.

findings.title: Root helper outlives its app: DaisyDisk's SMJobBless helper has no in-app removal, its guide names the wrong plist, and the Homebrew cask uninstalls a label the bundle never installs (DaisyDisk, verified from bundle metadata)
findings.where: DaisyDisk 4.34.2 Contents/Info.plist SMPrivilegedExecutables, Contents/Library/LaunchServices/com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskStandAlone.AdminHelper (research/sources/daisydisk/bundle-metadata.txt:93-95,205-211); guide EnableAdmin para 23-25; homebrew-cask Casks/d/daisydisk.rb:20-21
findings.problem:
DaisyDisk (closed source; stand-alone 4.34.2) installs a root helper that nothing ever removes: not the app, not its guide, and not the Homebrew cask. The evidence comes from bundle metadata, the docs and the cask. There was no disassembly, and the app was not launched.

- **Install.** DaisyDisk uses SMJobBless:
  - Info.plist `SMPrivilegedExecutables = { "com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskStandAlone.AdminHelper": <Developer ID requirement> }`.
  - The tool sits at `Contents/Library/LaunchServices/com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskStandAlone.AdminHelper`.
  - Its embedded launchd plist is `Label` = that name, `MachServices`, `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers = com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskStandAlone` (`research/sources/daisydisk/bundle-metadata.txt:93-95,17,205-211`).
  - It is installed on the first "Scan as Administrator" (https://daisydiskapp.com/guide/4/en/EnableAdmin/ para 7).
  - SMJobBless copies the tool to `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/<label>` and writes `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist`. It has been deprecated since macOS 13: "Please use SMAppService instead" (SDK `ServiceManagement.h:253,260`).
- **No in-app removal.** The only removal the vendor documents is "Quit DaisyDisk … and delete the following files", followed by `/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskStandAlone.AdminHelper` (no `.plist`) and `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/…` (EnableAdmin para 23-25). The plist name is wrong: SMJobBless plists end in `<label>.plist`. The same convention on this Mac: `/Library/LaunchDaemons/io.macfuse.app.launchservice.daemon.plist` → `Program /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/io.macfuse.app.launchservice.daemon`.
- **The cask removes a different label.** `Homebrew/homebrew-cask@4691afd4c4 Casks/d/daisydisk.rb:20-21` has `uninstall launchctl: "com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskAdminHelper", delete: "/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskAdminHelper"`. The `StandAlone.` segment is missing, so neither name matches what 4.34.2 installs.
  - Brew's `uninstall_launchctl` removes only services it finds under that label, plus `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<that label>.plist`, with `must_succeed: false` (`Homebrew/brew@d19643b36b Library/Homebrew/cask/artifact/abstract_uninstall.rb:232-256`).
  - So `brew uninstall --zap --cask daisydisk` finishes without an error and leaves the root helper binary and its launchd job in place.
- **The same class is live on this Mac.** `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.docker.socket` and `com.docker.vmnetd` are root-owned (dated Aug 11). No LaunchDaemon plist refers to them, `mdfind "kMDItemCFBundleIdentifier == 'com.docker.docker'"` finds no app, and `launchctl print system/com.docker.vmnetd` says "Could not find service". They are orphaned root binaries that no tool lists.
- **How common it is.** 85 of 7,755 casks hard-code `PrivilegedHelperTools` paths in uninstall or zap (https://formulae.brew.sh/api/cask.json, 2026-09-23). Each one is a label that can drift away from the bundle, as DaisyDisk's did.

For macontrol this matters twice:
1. It needs its own root helper (T-0010), and that helper must not become the next orphan.
2. Its uninstaller (T-0005) must find the helpers of other apps. The cask zap data that T-0005 surveyed as a rule source misses this one.
findings.before:
- The DaisyDisk bundle: `Info.plist` `SMPrivilegedExecutables` (bundle-metadata.txt:93-95). The helper's embedded `SMAuthorizedClients` (:184-186). The embedded launchd plist with `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` (:205-211). The app has no "remove helper" command anywhere in the guide.
- The guide's manual removal path lacks `.plist` (https://daisydiskapp.com/guide/4/en/EnableAdmin/ para 24).
- Homebrew cask `Casks/d/daisydisk.rb:20-21` (@4691afd4c4) removes `com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskAdminHelper`, a label that 4.34.2 does not install.
- Brew `abstract_uninstall.rb:232-256` (@d19643b36b) skips the missing label without an error.
findings.after:
1. **macontrol's own helper is SMAppService, and the user can remove it.**
   - Register it with `SMAppService.daemon(plistName:)`, with the plist in `Contents/Library/LaunchDaemons/` and a `BundleProgram` inside macontrol.app. Nothing is copied into `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools` (SDK `SMAppService.h:54-62`; topic-platform-constraints.md E1).
   - Install it lazily, only when a root-owned item is actually selected.
   - Settings shows the helper's status and a **Remove helper** button that calls `unregister()`. macontrol's own "Uninstall macontrol" unregisters first.
2. **The uninstaller finds helpers from the target bundle, not from names or casks.** For an app being removed, collect:
   (a) the keys of `SMPrivilegedExecutables` in its Info.plist,
   (b) the files in `Contents/Library/LaunchServices/`,
   (c) the plists in `Contents/Library/LaunchDaemons|LaunchAgents/` (SMAppService),
   (d) every `/Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist` and `/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist` that meets any of these: its `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` contains the bundle id, its `Label` is in (a), or its `Program`/`ProgramArguments[0]` resolves into the bundle or into `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/<label from a-c>`.
   Show every hit with its codesign Team ID. Pre-select it only when the Team ID matches the app's own. Tear down in the F-0023 order: bootout, then delete through the typed root helper.
3. **Cask zap and uninstall data is a hint, never ground truth.** Check that each path exists. When a cask label matches nothing but (a)-(d) found something, report "cask names X (not installed); found Y" instead of skipping in silence.
4. **Orphan helper scan** (read-only, in the Leftovers view). List:
   - binaries in `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools` that no LaunchDaemon plist points at,
   - LaunchDaemon plists whose `Program` is missing,
   - LaunchDaemon plists whose `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` app LaunchServices cannot resolve.
   Show the signer and the date for each. Removal goes through the same bootout-then-delete path, with explicit confirmation. This view would have found the two Docker helpers on this Mac.
findings.how:
**Acceptance test (fixture, no root, no real /Library):** run discovery against a temp root that contains:
- `App.app/Contents/Info.plist` with `SMPrivilegedExecutables {com.x.App.Helper: ...}`,
- `App.app/Contents/Library/LaunchServices/com.x.App.Helper`,
- `<root>/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.x.App.Helper.plist` (Program pointing into `<root>/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.x.App.Helper`, `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers = com.x.App`),
- a cask-style hint `com.x.AppHelper` (the wrong label),
- an orphan `<root>/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.y.orphan` with no plist.

Assert that:
1. The helper binary and the plist are found through (a), (b) and (d).
2. The cask hint is reported as "not installed".
3. The orphan is listed by the orphan scan.
4. Nothing outside the temp root is read. Pass the root in as a parameter.

**Verified here:**
- The bundle metadata dump (`codesign`, `plutil`, `launchctl plist __TEXT,__launchd_plist`).
- The SDK header lines.
- The cask and brew source lines (`gh api .../contents`).
- The macFUSE plist naming.
- The Docker orphans (`ls`, `mdfind`, `launchctl print`).
- The count of 85 casks, from `cask.json`.

**Unverified:**
- The runtime install of DaisyDisk's helper (installing it needs launching the app and an admin password).
- Whether the cask's label came from an older DaisyDisk version.
- Whether BTM (`sfltool dumpbtm`) lists SMJobBless helpers.

findings.title: Snapshot purge shares the file Collector and Delete button, and the guide suggests it right after a permanent delete: it removes the local Time Machine copies that are the only way back (DaisyDisk, docs)
findings.where: DaisyDisk guide DeletingFiles para 16-20, Snapshots para 25, PurgeableSpace para 20, WhatToDelete para 12, Undelete para 6-8 (snapshots in research/sources/daisydisk/guide4/)
findings.problem:
DaisyDisk (closed source) sends local Time Machine snapshot deletion and "purgeable space" purging through the same Collector and the same Delete button as file deletion. Its guide suggests that purge right after a permanent delete. The result is that the one route back to a file the user just deleted by mistake gets destroyed. All evidence is from the public guide. The runtime dialogs are **unverified**, because the app was not launched.

- **File deletes are permanent.** "Clicking the Delete button starts deletion process, but you'll have 5 seconds to change your mind … DaisyDisk permanently removes files and folders instead of moving them to the system Trash" (https://daisydiskapp.com/guide/4/en/DeletingFiles/ para 16-17; Undelete para 6).
- **The documented safety net is Time Machine.** "make sure your Time Machine is always up and running! In this case even if you delete something accidentally, you will always be able to roll back" (WhatToDelete para 12). On APFS, the local snapshots are what still hold a just-deleted file until the next backup: "when you delete a file, its copy may still be retained in the local snapshots" (DeletingFiles para 20).
- **Right after a delete, the guide suggests removing that net.** Under "Free space not appearing after deletion?" it says: "Alternatively, you can forcedly purge it with DaisyDisk" (DeletingFiles para 18-20).
- **Purging looks like deleting a file.** Drag "the snapshots item (or any of its child snapshot items), or alternatively the purgeable space item to the Collector, and delete as you'd do with a regular file or folder" (Snapshots para 25). Also "by dragging the purgeable space item to the Collector" (PurgeableSpace para 20). The guide's only purge screenshot shows a progress bar, "Reclaiming purgeable space… [Stop]" (`/img/guide/4/en/dd_c_purging.png`). Nothing documents a warning that restore points are being deleted.
- **The Undelete page omits the one working recourse.** It lists third-party recovery tools and "turn your Mac off" (Undelete para 7-8), and never mentions restoring from local snapshots.

Net effect: a user who deleted the wrong folder and sees "free space not appearing" is steered, through the same tray and button they just used, into deleting the only remaining copy.
findings.before:
- Snapshots, and the purgeable-space virtual item, are ordinary Collector entries next to files. One Delete button and one 5-second countdown handle them all (guide: DeletingFiles para 16-20, Snapshots para 25, PurgeableSpace para 20).
- The purge is presented as the fix for "free space not appearing after deletion" (DeletingFiles para 18-20).
- File deletes are permanent (DeletingFiles para 17, Undelete para 6-8).
findings.after:
1. **System-space actions are never Collector items.** Purgeable space and snapshots live in the hidden-space breakdown panel (keep DaisyDisk's breakdown: purgeable / other volumes / snapshots / still hidden). They cannot be dragged into the file tray. A single Delete never mixes files with snapshots.
2. **A confirm that states the consequence with numbers.** For example: "Thins local Time Machine snapshots to free ~8 GB. The oldest remaining restore point will be 2026-09-23 09:00. Files deleted before then, including 12.4 GB removed by macontrol today, can no longer be restored from them." The dates come from `tmutil listlocalsnapshotdates`. The "removed today" figure comes from macontrol's delete journal (F-0012).
3. **Default to thinning by amount, not delete-all.** Run `tmutil thinlocalsnapshots / <bytes> <urgency>` for just the space the user asked for (`man tmutil`, thinlocalsnapshots, verified on this Mac). Per-snapshot `tmutil deletelocalsnapshots <date>` is an advanced action.
4. **Journal-aware guard.** If the journal holds deletions newer than the oldest local snapshot, the panel says so and requires an explicit extra checkbox ("I don't need to restore those").
5. **"Space didn't appear" gets the right answer.** macontrol's own file deletes go to the Trash or quarantine (F-0012), and the post-delete sheet offers "Empty these from Trash" (F-0042). The snapshot explanation is shown, and a snapshot purge is never the suggested next step.
6. **Keep DaisyDisk's good part.** List third-party snapshots (CCC and others) read-only, with the app that owns them (guide: Snapshots para 20-21).
findings.how:
**Tests:**
- **UI model test:** adding a snapshot or purgeable node to the Collector is rejected with a reason that points to the System-space panel.
- **Unit test for the guard:** given fake snapshot dates [T-3h, T-1h] and a journal entry at T-2h, the confirm text must name the journal bytes and require the checkbox. Given a journal entry at T-5h, it must not.
- **Command-shape test:** the thin action builds the argv `["/usr/bin/tmutil","thinlocalsnapshots","/","<bytes>","<1-4>"]` with no shell string, and it runs as the user. Whether it needs root for TM snapshots on macOS 26 is **unverified**; probe it before shipping.

**Verified:** the guide quotes (snapshots in `research/sources/daisydisk/guide4/*.txt`) and the `man tmutil` syntax on this Mac.

**Unverified:** whether DaisyDisk shows an extra confirm at runtime (not launched), and how its purge is implemented.

findings.title: Unreadable folders show as 0 B, identical to empty ones: no flag in the tree or JSON, exit 0, and the maintainer's advice for macOS TCC errors is --silent-errors (pdu #134, verified)
findings.problem:
pdu turns every failed `read_dir` into an ordinary node with no children. Its size is only the directory's own inode size, which is 0 on APFS in the default block-size mode. The error goes to stderr and nowhere else. The tree has no field for it, the JSON export has no field for it, and the process exits 0. An unreadable folder therefore looks exactly like an empty one, and every ancestor total is silently a lower bound.

Verified with pdu 0.24.0 (Homebrew arm64, macOS 26.6) using `research/bench/ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage/repro.sh unreadable`. The folder `Locked/` holds a 16 MiB file and is `chmod 000`, and `Empty/` is empty:
- Text chart: `0 ├──Locked` right above `0 └──Empty`, plus one `[error] read_dir ... Permission denied` line on stderr.
- `--json-output`: `{"name":"Locked","size":0,"children":[]}` and `{"name":"Empty","size":0,"children":[]}`, byte-identical apart from the name. Exit 0.
- With `-s/--silent-errors`, nothing on any channel shows that 16 MiB were not counted.

On macOS the common trigger is TCC, not chmod. Open issue #134 ("Lots of errors on runtime on macOS by default") lists EPERM on ~/Library/Mail, Safari, Messages, Biome, .Trash and more. The maintainer's answer was "`pdu` has `--silent-errors`" (https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage/issues/134). So the documented workflow for a scan without Full Disk Access shows the biggest private folders as empty, with the undercount hidden.

The test for this path, `tests/cli_errors.rs:120-190` (`fs_errors`), checks only the two stderr lines and that stdout equals the library's own rendering of the same tree. It never checks the exit status (it only `dbg!`s it) or that the unreadable node is marked in any way.
findings.after:
Every macontrol node carries a scan state next to its size:
- `complete`
- `denied`: open or read failed with EPERM or EACCES (TCC, or file mode)
- `partial`: the folder was read, but some entries failed to stat
- `skipped`: deliberately not walked (other volume, excluded, or beyond an fd or depth limit; see F-0008)

Each node also keeps a count of incomplete descendants, maintained during aggregation, so any ancestor knows at once that its total is a lower bound.

In the UI:
- A denied folder shows a lock badge and "No access", never "0 B" or "Empty". Its treemap tile is drawn hatched at a minimum size, so it stays visible and clickable.
- Any total with incomplete descendants reads "at least 41.2 GB", with a count ("3 folders could not be read").
- One banner per scan groups the denied folders by cause. For TCC it offers the Full Disk Access onboarding and a rescan of just those folders once access is granted.
- Exports, the scan cache and the cleanup engine keep the state. A cleanup rule never treats a denied folder as empty or as "0 B to free".

This goes beyond F-0008 (whose "after" says skipped subtrees are flagged) and F-0016 (whose "after" gives unattributable space its own row). It defines the state model both of those assume.
findings.how:
- Fixture test (as in repro.sh `unreadable`): `Locked/` (chmod 000) holds a 16 MiB file, and `Empty/` is empty. Assert that Locked has state `denied`, that its size text is "No access" and not "0 B", and that Empty is `complete` with 0 B. Assert that the root has incompleteDescendants == 1 and renders "at least".
- TCC test: run the scan engine inside the ad-hoc-signed probe .app from topic-platform-constraints (T-0010), without FDA, on a root that contains ~/Library/Safari. Assert state `denied` (errno 1) for Safari, and that the banner offers FDA. Include an FDA-free control path in the same run.
- Regression guard: the scan result type cannot be constructed without a state, so a new walker path cannot drop it silently. Every error branch in the walker sets it.
- pdu repro: `research/bench/ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage/repro.sh unreadable`.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): EACCES/EPERM on open or listing flags the folder .unreadable, other errors .incomplete, per-entry ATTR_CMN_ERROR .incomplete; measure() sets isIncomplete and reclaimable() sets ReclaimEstimate.isIncomplete; mcscan exits 1 and names the count. Tests: ScanEngineTests.unreadableFolderIsFlagged, ReclaimTests.unreadableFolderMakesTheEstimateALowerBound.

findings.title: Hard-link summary panics when a scan sees more paths than nlink: a firmlink alias of a root passes the realpath-prefix overlap check, sizes double, and pdu -H aborts with exit 101 and no JSON (verified; extends F-0039, F-0031)
findings.problem:
If a scan reaches the same hard-linked inode by more paths than its `st_nlink`, pdu `-H` aborts at the end with a panic. Firmlinks make that easy on macOS. Two defects combine:

1. **Overlapping roots are detected by realpath string prefix.** `realpath` does not collapse firmlinks (F-0039), so `X` and `/System/Volumes/Data/X` both survive the overlap check, even though `stat` gives both the same (dev 16777229, ino 98186661). The whole tree is walked twice.
2. **The hard-link summary asserts `nlink >= detected paths`** and panics otherwise. The filesystem can break that "invariant" (firmlinks, a tree walked twice, a link added during the scan), so a scan that took minutes ends in a crash.

Verified with pdu 0.24.0 (Homebrew arm64, macOS 26.6), `research/bench/ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage/repro.sh alias`. The folder holds one 4 MiB file with 3 links:
- `pdu -H -b plain -d 1 X /System/Volumes/Data/X` prints the chart and then `panicked at src/hardlink/hardlink_list/summary.rs:92:21: Impossible! Total of nlink (3) is less than detected paths (6)`, exit 101.
- With `--json-output`, 0 bytes reach stdout, exit 101. The whole scan result is lost.
- In an earlier run with non-linked files next to the linked one, the chart showed `(total)` 21,282,816 B for a 12,738,560 B folder. Everything unlinked was counted twice.

Within one root, inferred from code but not run: `/` contains both `/Users` (a firmlink) and `/System/Volumes/Data/Users`, and both have the same st_dev (F-0031), so `-x` does not separate them either. `pdu -H /` would therefore see every multi-link file on the Data volume through twice as many paths as nlink and hit the same panic after a full-disk scan. I did not run a full-disk scan on this loaded machine, so this part is unverified.
findings.after:
- **Identity is (dev, ino), never a path string.** Before a multi-root scan, macontrol opens each root with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` and records its (dev, ino). It drops a root whose (dev, ino) equals another root's, or equals any ancestor of another root. It finds ancestors by `fstatat(fd, "..")` up to the volume root, or compares canonical `F_GETPATH` results, which do resolve firmlinks (F-0039). A whole-disk scan walks `/System/Volumes/Data` plus the System-volume-only parts, not `/` (F-0031).
- **Link bookkeeping tolerates a filesystem that disagrees with itself.** The (dev, ino) side table (F-0037, F-0047) stores node ids, and a node id is added at most once. If more links are seen than `st_nlink` says, or nlink or size changes between two links, the scan records a diagnostic ("inode seen through more paths than links: firmlink, repeated root, or changed during scan"), keeps the lowest-common-ancestor attribution, and completes.
- **No assert or panic on filesystem-derived data.** The engine treats metadata as untrusted input: it may change mid-scan, and firmlinks or other mounts may repeat a subtree. A failed consistency check only lowers a node's state to `partial` (F-0057) and never loses the scan result.
findings.how:
- Test 1 (roots): X holds a 3-link 4 MiB file plus 8 MiB of unlinked data. Scanning roots [X, /System/Volumes/Data + X] must give exactly the result of scanning [X], with no crash and one "duplicate root dropped" note. Build X with `pwd -P` so the /private firmlink alias exists (repro.sh does this).
- Test 2 (invariant): add a link to a file from a second thread while the walker is between two of its links, or inject a stat result with a lower nlink in a unit test of the side table. The scan must complete, emit the diagnostic and keep attribution deterministic.
- Test 3 (whole disk, T-0004 harness): a whole-disk scan's total equals the Data volume scan plus the System-only parts, and no inode is attributed twice (F-0031).
- pdu repro: `research/bench/ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage/repro.sh alias` (exit 101, 0 bytes of JSON).
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043): reclaimable() dedupes folders by identity and files by (parent identity, name), drops items inside another selected folder (checked by ancestor identity, so firmlink aliases match), and counts a hard link as freed when seen >= nlink, never asserting ==. Test: ReclaimTests.aliasedSelectionIsCountedOnce (folder + its /System/Volumes/Data alias + an aliased file inside = 1 MiB once, no crash).

findings.title: With -H, sort order and the 1% cutoff use pre-dedup sizes: a 4 MiB folder is listed above an 8 MiB one, a 1.2% file is hidden and rows stop adding up (pdu, verified)
findings.problem:
pdu corrects hard-link sizes (`-H`) only after it has sorted the tree and cut small items. The chart then prints corrected sizes in the uncorrected order, and it hides items using the inflated total.

Verified with pdu 0.24.0 (Homebrew arm64, macOS 26.6), `research/bench/ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage/repro.sh order`. `A/` holds one 4 MiB inode with 3 links (12 MiB before dedup), `B/` an 8 MiB file, and `C` a 150 KiB file. `pdu -H --top-down -b plain .` shows:
- A (4,194,304) listed **before** B (8,388,608), although the list is meant to run largest first.
- C (155,648 B, 1.22% of the 12,738,560 B root shown) **missing**. The default `--min-ratio 0.01` was applied against the pre-dedup total (21,127,168 B, where 1% = 211 KB).
- The rows shown (A + B = 12,582,912) do not add up to the root, and nothing says an item was hidden.

The dedup tests cannot catch this. Every test re-sorts the JSON tree by name before comparing (`tests/hardlinks_deduplication.rs:60`) and passes `--min-ratio=0` (`:454, 680, 891, 1020, 1187`).

For macontrol, the lesson is ordering: any size correction applied as a later pass (hard links, clones, errors) goes stale in every view built before it. WinDirStat's post-scan `DoHardlinkAdjustment` (F-0047) has the same structure.
findings.after:
macontrol computes sizes in one fixed order. First the final sizes: hard-link and clone attribution (F-0047/F-0054) and error state are resolved during aggregation. Only then come the views derived from those sizes: sort order, percentages, "smaller items" grouping and treemap layout.

- Nothing reads a size before its corrections are in. The model exposes only final sizes, and a pass that changes sizes after aggregation is not allowed.
- Any later size change (delete, FSEvents splice, refresh) re-aggregates the affected parent chain. It then re-sorts and re-groups each changed parent, so order and grouping never go stale.
- Grouped or hidden items always appear as an explicit "N smaller items, X" row, so the rows add up to the parent (as F-0016 requires).
findings.how:
- Fixture (as in repro.sh `order`): A/{f,f2,f3} (one 4 MiB inode, 3 links), B/g (8 MiB), C (150 KiB). Assert that the root's children are ordered B, A, C by final size. C must be visible, or counted in a "smaller items" row whose size is included, and the rows must sum to the root.
- Delete f2 and f3 through the app. A must stay at 4 MiB and keep its place after B. Then add 3 links to g. B's size must not change, and the order must be recomputed.
- Property test over random trees with random hard links: after any sequence of splices, every folder's children are sorted by the displayed size, and the displayed rows sum to the parent.
- pdu repro: `research/bench/ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage/repro.sh order`.

findings.title: Out of fds (EMFILE) counts a folder as 0 B, and each failed listing leaks its fd: 61 unlistable folders zero out 79% of a tree, exit 0; totals vary per run (dumac #2, verified)
findings.where: healeycodes/dumac@1ffbe3c src/main.rs:191-201 get_dir_info open; :233-243 bulk-read error path (no close); :173-179 Err -> 0; :16-17 MAX_FILE_HANDLES
findings.problem:
dumac (healeycodes/dumac@1ffbe3c) turns every failure to open or list a folder into "this subtree is 0 bytes" and still exits 0. Two things make this worse than a plain skip:

- **EMFILE is treated as permanent.** "Too many open files" is transient: it clears as soon as another worker closes its fd. dumac drops the subtree and moves on, so under fd pressure the total shrinks by a different amount on every run and nothing says it is incomplete.
- **A failed listing leaks the directory fd.** If `open()` succeeds but `getattrlistbulk()` fails, the function returns before `close()`. Each such folder holds one fd until the process exits, and the leaked fds then cause EMFILE on unrelated folders, which the first bullet zeroes out.

Verified locally (macOS 26.6, M1; dumac built from @1ffbe3c in a scratch copy, with only its final println changed to print bytes; `research/bench/healeycodes-dumac/run_probes.sh`, output in `results.txt`):
- Bench fixture (du/dua total 2,359,623,680 B): with `ulimit -n 8`, three identical runs returned 659,345,408, 80,183,296 and 304,017,408 B, all exit 0. With `ulimit -n 12` all three returned 2,360,152,064 B. stderr only says "Cannot access directory" (EMFILE is never named).
- Fd leak: 300 readable-but-unsearchable (`r--`) folders next to 300 normal folders with one 5,000 B file each (expected 2,457,600 B). At `ulimit -n 64` dumac reported 516,096 B (21 %) and exit 0: 61 "Permission denied" listings leaked 61 fds, after which 476 opens failed with "Cannot access directory". At `ulimit -n 1024` it reported 2,457,600 B, so the leak only shows once the fds run out.
- In the wild: issue #2 (https://github.com/healeycodes/dumac/issues/2) reported 870.8G, 1.0T, 949.4G, 1.1T, 916.4G and 949.8G on consecutive runs over the same $HOME, while du said 1.4T. The maintainer traced it to open file handles and capped the thread count (commits 931ac28, 03846c1). The error path was never changed.

Why it matters for macontrol: a GUI app starts with the launchd soft limit of 256 fds (`launchctl limit maxfiles` prints `256 unlimited` on this Mac), and it shares that table with everything else in the process. F-0008's fd-relative walker holds directory fds along the path, and the duplicate finder and previews open files too. EMFILE will happen there. It must cost time, not bytes.
findings.after:
macontrol's walker treats running out of fds as back-pressure, keeps every byte it has already read, and never reports a partial number as complete:

1. **Fd budget.** At launch, raise the soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE`. Verified here: an unprivileged process starting at a soft limit of 256 raised it to 10,240 (`kern.maxfilesperproc`), and 65,536 was accepted too. OpenDisk already does this (137137137/OpenDisk@6e3f1f7 `OpenDisk/Services/Scanning/ScanEngine.swift:92-99`). Then give the scanner an explicit budget taken from `getrlimit` (for example `min(soft / 4, 1024)`), enforced by a counting semaphore that every `openat` acquires. Directory fds held for the fd-relative walk (F-0008) count against it.
2. **Transient errors are retried, not counted.** On EMFILE, ENFILE, EINTR or EAGAIN from `openat` or `getattrlistbulk`, the worker releases what it holds, waits on the semaphore and retries the same folder with backoff. Only when the retries run out (for example, because other code in the process holds the fds) does the folder take F-0057's `skipped` state, with the reason "too many open files" named. It is never shown as 0 B.
3. **Permanent errors keep what was read.** On EACCES, EPERM (TCC) or ENOENT (deleted mid-scan), the node keeps the entries already read and takes F-0057's `denied` or `partial` state. That state model, and the "at least N GB" display, are defined in F-0057 and are not repeated here. This finding adds one rule to it: running out of fds is handled by point 2 first. It normally costs time, not bytes.
4. **Every fd is closed on every path.** Use `defer { close(fd) }` right after a successful `openat`, including the paths that fail mid-listing.
findings.how:
