- **Fault injection:** scan `research/bench/fixtures/tree` with the fd budget forced to 2 (or the process soft limit set to 16 in a test process). The total must equal `ground_truth.json` `visible_to_non_root.allocated_all` byte-exact in 3 of 3 runs, just slower. The only incomplete node allowed is `unreadable/locked`. dumac is the negative control: `DUMAC=<bytes build> research/bench/healeycodes-dumac/run_probes.sh`, sections 3 and 4.
- **Unit test with a fake directory source:** return EMFILE for the first N opens and EACCES halfway through one listing. Expect the full total from the retried folders, and the EACCES folder marked `incomplete(EACCES)` with its first-page entries kept.
- **Leak check:** count open fds (`proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDLISTFDS)`) before and after a scan of the `r--` fixture from run_probes.sh section 4. The two counts must be equal.
findings.verified: macontrol feat/scan-engine (T-0043, fix round 1 @ 4131bda): the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE is raised once to min(hard, OPEN_MAX), and each walk budgets a quarter of it (at most 1024). Over budget, the shallowest idle parent is closed and reopened later by name from an open ancestor, with a (dev, ino) check. EMFILE/ENFILE from outside the budget (other walks, other code) is waited out for up to 5 s, on first opens and on every reopen step alike (FolderWalk.openWaiting). Only then is the folder flagged .incomplete, never 0. Failed listings keep what was read and close their fd. Tests: ScanEngineTests.tinyDescriptorBudgetGivesTheExactTotal (budget 6 on a 1,093-folder tree: exact total and folder sizes, reopenCount > 0). DescriptorPressureTests.concurrentWalksOverTheProcessLimitStayExact (env MACONTROL_FD_PRESSURE=1, because it lowers the process limit): 5 concurrent measures at soft limit 96 are all exact; with the old reopen it failed 3/3 rounds.

findings.title: Imported report stays deletable and its names are trusted: a nested entry named with an absolute path or ../ is deleted outside the report root (gdu -f, verified); ncdu disables delete on import
findings.problem:
`gdu -f report.json` loads an ncdu-format export and keeps `d` (delete) and `e` (empty) enabled. The README presents this as a normal workflow: `gdu -o- / | gzip -c >report.json.gz  # write all info to JSON file for later analysis`, then `zcat report.json.gz | gdu -f-`. Delete then runs `os.RemoveAll` on a path rebuilt from the names in the file, and those names are never validated.

- A nested directory whose `"name"` contains `/` has its `BasePath` set from that name (`report/import.go:134-140`). `Dir.GetPath()` returns `BasePath + Name` before it looks at the parent (`pkg/analyze/file.go:463-466`). The row shows only the last component.
- A file named `../x` is joined with `filepath.Join`, which cleans the `..` away (`file.go:53-56`).

**Verified** with gdu's own `report.ReadAnalysis` and `remove.ItemFromDir`, which are what `-f` and then `d` + Yes run (`research/bench/dundee-gdu/run.sh`, TestProbeImportDelete; scratch temp dir only). The report root was `<tmp>/report-root` and did not need to exist.
- A nested row shown as `victim` removed `<tmp>/elsewhere/victim`, outside the report root, with err=nil.
- A row named `../elsewhere/victim2.txt` removed `<tmp>/elsewhere/victim2.txt`, with err=nil.

Crafted names are not required for harm. An old export, or one from another machine, deletes whatever lives at that path today. The format cannot even detect it: the exporter writes `ino` only for hard links, and only in full exports (`pkg/analyze/encode.go`; gdu issue #667). `-r` (read a stored `--db`) has the same property. It loads the stored tree with no freshness check (`tui/actions.go:270-286`), and delete stays on (code-read).

ncdu, whose format gdu imports, turns these actions off: "will assume that the directory information in the imported file does not represent the filesystem on which the file is being imported. That is, the refresh, file deletion and shell spawning options in the browser will be disabled" (ncdu.1:79-84, https://code.blicky.net/yorhel/ncdu/raw/branch/zig/ncdu.1).
findings.before:
dundee/gdu @ 848a5dd (MIT):

- `cmd/gdu/app/app.go:765-779`: `case a.Flags.InputFile != "":` → `ui.ReadAnalysis(input)`. `SetNoDelete` is called only for `--no-delete` (`app.go:684-687`).
- `report/import.go:57-61`: `name, ok := item["name"].(string) … file.Name = name`. There is no check for `/`, `..` or empty names.
- `report/import.go:134-140`: `slashPos := strings.LastIndex(name, "/"); if slashPos > -1 { dir.Name = name[slashPos+1:]; dir.BasePath = name[:slashPos+1] }`. This runs for nested directories too, not only the root.
- `pkg/analyze/file.go:463-466`: `func (f *Dir) GetPath() string { if f.BasePath != "" { return filepath.Join(f.BasePath, f.Name) } …`
- `pkg/remove/remove.go:11-19`: `err := os.RemoveAll(item.GetPath())`, with no identity check against the live filesystem.
- `tui/tui.go:660-676`: `confirmDeletion` checks only `noDelete` and `noDeleteWithFilter`.
findings.after:
In macontrol, a tree that did not come from a live scan in this process is read-only. That covers saved scans, imported files, caches and snapshots.

- Delete, Trash and Empty are offered only on nodes of a live scan. On a loaded tree the same place offers "Rescan this folder". The action becomes available once the live rescan has produced the node.
- Names are validated when any tree is deserialized. A name must be exactly one path component: non-empty, no `/`, no NUL, and not `.` or `..`. One bad record rejects the whole file. Paths are never stored per node. A node holds its name and a parent link, and the root path comes from the live scan, never from the file.
- Before any delete, the target is re-resolved fd-relative from the scan root (`openat` per component with `O_NOFOLLOW`). Its `(st_dev, st_ino, file type)` is compared with what the scan recorded, and on a mismatch the delete is refused and a rescan is offered. Persisted scans store dev+ino for every node so this check is always possible (see F-0017 for freshness and F-0045 for cache privacy).
findings.how:
1. Loader test: a snapshot or import with a nested directory named `/tmp/x/victim`, a file named `../victim2`, a name `a/b` and an empty name. Each load must fail with a validation error, and nothing on disk is touched.
2. Stale-tree test: scan a fixture, replace `f.bin` with a different file at the same path (new inode), then attempt to delete `f.bin` from the old tree. It must be refused with "changed since scan", and the new file must still exist.
3. UI test: open an imported or saved tree. The Delete, Trash and Empty actions are absent or disabled, and "Rescan" is offered.
4. The gdu reproduction stays runnable as a reference: `bash research/bench/dundee-gdu/run.sh` (TestProbeImportDelete).

findings.title: With a --type filter the TUI shows a folder at its filtered size (4 KiB) but Delete removes the whole folder, 4 MiB of hidden files included; only time filters block it, the web UI blocks both (gdu, verified)
findings.problem:
`gdu --type log <dir>` (also `--exclude-type`) builds the tree from matching files only, so a folder row shows only the bytes of its matching files. Pressing `d` on that row still runs `os.RemoveAll` on the whole folder, including every file the filter hid. The TUI blocks deletion only while a *time* filter is active. The web UI in the same program blocks it for any file filter, so the two frontends disagree on the same state.

**Verified** in gdu's own `tui` package (`research/bench/dundee-gdu/run.sh`, TestProbeTypeFilterDelete; scratch temp dir only). The test calls `CreateUI` and `SetIncludeTypes(["log"])`, which is what `--type log` does, then `confirmDeletion` and `deleteSelected`, which is what `d` and Yes do. `logs/` held `app.log` (2 KiB) and `video.mov` (4 MiB).
- The `logs` row showed usage = 4096 B and size = 2048 B.
- After `d`, the front page was the `confirm` modal, with `IsFilteringFiles=true` and `noDeleteWithFilter=false`.
- After Yes, `logs/` and `video.mov` were gone.

The confirmation reads only `Are you sure you want to delete "logs"?`, with no size and no hint that most of the folder is hidden (`tui/tui.go:692-700`). It also offers "don't ask me again", which switches confirmation off for the rest of the session (`tui.go:700-705`).
findings.before:
dundee/gdu @ 848a5dd (MIT):

- `cmd/gdu/app/app.go:319-325`: `--type` → `ui.SetIncludeTypes`, `--exclude-type` → `ui.SetIgnoreTypes`.
- `tui/actions.go:93`: `analyzer.AnalyzeDir(path, ui.CreateIgnoreFunc(), ui.CreateFileTypeFilter())`. Non-matching files never enter the tree.
- `tui/tui.go:722-735`: `SetNoDeleteWithFilter()` is called only from `SetTimeFilterWithInfo`. `tui.go:752-763` `isDeleteAllowedWithFilter` looks only at `hasActiveTimeFilter()`.
- `tui/tui.go:660-676`: `confirmDeletion` checks `noDelete` and `noDeleteWithFilter` and nothing else.
- `pkg/remove/remove.go:11-19`: `os.RemoveAll(item.GetPath())` on the folder.
- Contrast, same repo: `webui/handlers.go:123-133` `deleteDisabledReason` refuses when `ui.IsFilteringFiles()`, and `internal/common/ignore.go:307-309` returns true for type filters.
findings.after:
In macontrol, a filter changes what is shown. It never widens what a delete touches beyond what is shown.

- While any filter hides entries (type, age, size, name or search), a delete on a folder row acts only on the matching files inside it: the plan is a list of file nodes. The confirmation says "N matching files, X GB. M other items in this folder stay." Removing the folder itself requires clearing the filter first.
- There is one delete planner. Every entry point (map, list, search results, context menu, keyboard, Cleanup tab) calls it, so two surfaces cannot disagree the way gdu's TUI and web UI do.
- The confirmation always shows the item count and the on-disk bytes of exactly what the plan removes, computed from the plan, not from the row. There is no session-wide "don't ask again" for permanent deletes.
findings.how:
Engine plus UI test. Fixture `logs/` with `app.log` (2 KiB) and `video.mov` (4 MiB). Set filter type=log and trigger delete on the `logs` folder from every entry point (list, map, keyboard, context menu).
- The plan contains exactly `logs/app.log` (1 file, 2 KiB) and reports "1 other item stays".
- After confirming, `video.mov` and `logs/` still exist.
- With the filter cleared, the same action plans the whole folder (2 items, 4 MiB + 2 KiB).
Reference reproduction of the gdu behaviour: `bash research/bench/dundee-gdu/run.sh` (TestProbeTypeFilterDelete).

findings.title: Deleting one hard link subtracts the file's full size from every ancestor though it was counted 0 B and frees nothing: a folder reads -4 MiB and the total drops 4 MiB below disk (gdu, verified; see F-0047, F-0054)
findings.problem:
gdu counts a multi-link inode once. The first link reached while totals are computed gets the bytes, and every other link contributes 0 B (`alreadyCounted`, `pkg/analyze/file.go:108-121`). After a delete, however, `Dir.RemoveFile` → `subtractStats` subtracts the deleted item's *raw* size and usage from its folder and from every ancestor (`file.go:513-543`), not what that item contributed. The TUI only redraws after a delete and never recomputes (`tui/actions.go:350-358`).

**Verified** with gdu's own `ParallelAnalyzer`, `UpdateStats` and `remove.ItemFromDir`, the TUI's default remover (`research/bench/dundee-gdu/run.sh`, TestProbeHardlinkDelete; scratch temp dir only). Fixture: `a/data.bin` (4 MiB) hard-linked as `b/data.bin`, plus `keep/other.bin` (1 MiB). Before any delete: root = 5,242,880, a = 4,194,304, b = 0.
- Delete `b/data.bin`, the link counted as 0 B. Result: root = 1,048,576, a = 4,194,304, **b = −4,194,304**.
- Delete `a/data.bin`, the counted link, instead. Result: root = 1,048,576, a = 0, b = 0.
- In both cases 5,242,880 B are still allocated on disk, because the other link keeps the data.

So a folder goes negative and the total drops 4 MiB below reality, while the delete freed nothing. Users hit both halves:
- gdu #267: "When I press d to delete a file, there is no more space on the filesystem because it is a hardlink".
- gdu #439 (rsnapshot): sizes are "attributed to different directories" across refreshes. That is the order-dependent attribution class of F-0054.
findings.before:
dundee/gdu @ 848a5dd (MIT):

- `pkg/analyze/dir_unix.go:28-30`: `if stat.Nlink > 1 { file.Mli = stat.Ino }`. The inode is keyed without `st_dev`.
- `pkg/analyze/file.go:108-121` `alreadyCounted`: the first link seen in `linkedItems[mli]` is counted, later ones return `(1, 0, 0)` from `GetItemStats` (`:135-140`).
- `pkg/analyze/file.go:526-543` `subtractStats`: `itemCount, size, usage := item.GetItemCount(), item.GetSize(), item.GetUsage()`, then each ancestor gets `cur.Size -= size; cur.Usage -= usage`. For a `File`, `GetUsage()` is the raw `Usage` (`:70-73`), whether or not it was counted.
- `pkg/remove/remove.go:11-19`: `os.RemoveAll(item.GetPath()); dir.RemoveFile(item)`. The `ui.linkedItems` map is never updated.
findings.after:
In macontrol, totals after any tree mutation (delete, trash, splice) come from the same dedup table the scan used, never from the removed node's raw size.

- Side table `(st_dev, st_ino) → {link nodes seen, bytes, st_nlink}` (the table F-0037 and F-0047 already call for). Deleting a link removes that node from its entry. The bytes leave the totals only when the entry's last seen link is deleted *and* `fstatat` on a surviving path, or the parent's re-read, shows no remaining link inside the scan.
- Attribution of the touched inodes is recomputed with the lowest-common-ancestor rule of F-0047, so folder sizes stay deterministic (F-0054) and never go negative.
- In debug builds, an invariant runs after every mutation: for each folder `size == own + sum(children) >= 0`, and the root total equals the sum over distinct `(dev, ino)`.
- The delete result reports "freed X" from the plan: 0 B for a link whose inode survives, with the reason ("still linked from b/data.bin"). This answers gdu #267 up front.
findings.how:
Engine test on the probe's fixture: `a/data.bin` (4 MiB), `b/data.bin` as a hard link, and `keep/other.bin` (1 MiB).
1. Scan. The root is 5 MiB and the 4 MiB sit with the lowest common ancestor.
2. Delete `b/data.bin`. The plan says freed 0 B, the root stays 5 MiB, and no folder is negative.
3. Delete `a/data.bin`. The plan says freed 4 MiB and the root becomes 1 MiB.
4. After each step, compare the mutated tree with a fresh full scan, byte-exact. Also run the steps in the other order.
Reference reproduction of gdu: `bash research/bench/dundee-gdu/run.sh` (TestProbeHardlinkDelete).
findings.verified: Closed jointly. Disk map (T-0048): trashing a hard link counted at 0 B leaves every total alone (DiskMapModelTests.trashingAZeroByteHardLinkLeavesTotalsAlone). Scan engine (T-0043 fix round 1, feat/scan-engine @ 4131bda): ScanTree.removeSubtree hands a removed owner link's bytes to the surviving link with the smallest path (the finalizeTotals rule) and adds them back to its ancestors. The bytes leave the totals only with the last link. Test: ScanTreeTests.removingTheChargedLinkMovesItsBytesToTheNextLink. Once both branches merge, DiskMapReviewTests.trashingTheCarryingHardLinkKeepsBytesThatStayOnDisk flips out of withKnownIssue ('known issue not recorded'), and the disk map drops the wrapper.

findings.title: Trash mode leaves each cleaned item in the Trash as a hidden '.mactools-staged-<UUID>': Finder does not show it, Put Back restores the hidden name, and later scans protect it forever (MacTools DiskClean, verified)
findings.problem:
MacTools Disk Cleanup (ggbond268/MacTools@bf6550a, GPL-3.0, study only) moves items to the Trash by default (`DiskCleanPlan.swift:32`, `?? .trash`). To close the path-replacement window it first renames each verified item in place to `.mactools-staged-<UUID>` (`DiskCleanRemovalPrimitive.swift:89,105`, `stage()` :240-293, `renameatx_np(RENAME_EXCL)` :266). It then trashes **the staged path** (`moveToTrash()` :328-350). The item never gets its real name back. Three consequences:

- **It is invisible in the Trash.** The name starts with a dot, so Finder hides it. Verified: `research/bench/ggbond268-mactools/trash_name_probe.swift` repeats the same rename + `FileManager.trashItem` on a scratch folder. The Trash entry is `.mactools-staged-90D08C77-…` with `URLResourceValues.isHidden == true`. A user who opens the Trash to recover "that one cache folder" sees nothing, and only MacTools' history page shows the UUID (`DiskCleanCleanupHistoryView.swift:412-424`).
- **Put Back restores the hidden name, not the original.** MacTools says so itself: `DiskCleanRemovalPrimitive.swift:13-14` ("Restoring will land under the staged name") and the mode description string "Putting back uses the staged name" (`Localizable.xcstrings`, key `detail.removalMode.trash.description`). The app that owned the folder does not find it under that name, so Put Back does not undo the cleanup. MacTools has no in-app restore.
- **A put-back item is then protected from every later scan.** `DiskCleanSafetyPolicy.swift:144-145` marks any path with a `.mactools-staged-` component as `protected("staging in progress")`. The startup reconciler only processes journal entries that never completed (`DiskCleanStagingReconciler.swift:70`), and a trashed entry is completed with status `trashed` (`DiskCleanRemovalPrimitive.swift:348`). So a restored folder becomes a hidden, permanently skipped copy that no MacTools feature can reclaim or rename.

The same repo shows a better pattern that keeps the original name. StorageExplorer moves the item to `<parent>/.mactools-trash-<UUID>/<original name>` and trashes that path (`StorageExplorerSafetyPolicy.swift:256-296`). The same probe shows the Trash entry as `Cache-StorageExplorer`, visible (`isHidden == false`). But StorageExplorer then `rmdir`s the staging folder (:310-316), so a Finder Put Back has no original folder to return to. What Finder does in that case is **unverified** here.

Neighbours: F-0036 is about staging names orphaned by a crash (MangoDisk). F-0053 is about the wrong Trash location (QDirStat). F-0042 is about trashed bytes counted as freed. None covers an item that reaches the real Trash under a name the user cannot see or restore. Undo design is tracked in T-0026.

    StorageExpl.: in Trash as "Cache-StorageExplorer" isHidden(Finder)=false
findings.after:
macontrol keeps MacTools' identity freeze but never lets the freeze name reach the Trash, and it owns the undo.

1. **Freeze into a private staging folder that keeps the real name.** Take an fd on the parent, verify `(dev, ino, type, mtime)` of the leaf with `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`, then `renameatx_np(RENAME_EXCL)` the leaf into a private staging folder **under its original name**: `<staging dir>/<op_id>/<original name>`. The staging dir is the per-volume app-owned folder from F-0036 where it is writable, otherwise a `0700` sibling folder. The move is on the same volume and atomic. Re-verify identity there, then trash that path. The Trash entry carries the original, visible name.
2. **Write our own undo record before the move and after it.** The journal entry stores `{original path, identity, staging path, trash URL from resultingItemURL}`. "Restore" in macontrol renames the Trash item back to the original path with `RENAME_EXCL`. If something now exists at that path, restore asks the user instead of overwriting. Restore never depends on Finder's Put Back metadata. This is the T-0026 journal.
3. **The staging folder is removed only after the trash call returns.** Launch-time reconciliation (as in MacTools' `DiskCleanStagingReconciler`, and F-0036) moves any leftover staged item back to its original name.
4. **Protection is keyed on the journal, not on a name prefix.** The scanner skips paths that have an open journal entry. A folder the user restored is an ordinary folder again and can be cleaned by the next scan.
5. The clean summary names the Trash and offers "Restore all" and per-item "Restore" for the whole retention window.
findings.how:
- Run `research/bench/ggbond268-mactools/trash_name_probe.swift` (build: `swiftc -O trash_name_probe.swift -o tp && ./tp <scratch dir>`). It creates only its own scratch folders, trashes them the way each MacTools plugin does, prints the Trash name and Finder's `isHidden`, then removes exactly what it created from the Trash. Verified on macOS 26.6 (MacTools@bf6550a).
- macontrol acceptance test: trash a fixture folder `Cache-X` through the cleanup executor. Assert (a) `resultingItemURL.lastPathComponent == "Cache-X"` and `isHidden == false`, (b) the journal holds the original path and the Trash URL, (c) "Restore" puts `Cache-X` back at its original path with the same inode, (d) a scan afterwards offers `Cache-X` again, (e) with a new `Cache-X` created at the original path, restore refuses to overwrite and asks the user.
- Kill the process between the staging rename and the trash call. The next launch must put `Cache-X` back under its original name.
findings.verified: Items keep their visible name in the Trash (no hidden staging copy), and History/Undo come from the journal, not from scanning the Trash. Tests: TrashServiceTests.trashesUnderTheItemsOwnNameAndJournalsIt (backend gets the item's own path), undoRestoresTheSameBytesAndIdentity. feat/safety-trash (T-0044)

findings.title: Each cleanup item is sized by one thread under a hard 20 s wall clock, and a cut-short size makes it uncleanable: at the measured 34-40k files/s any cache folder over ~0.7-0.8M files can never be cleaned (MacTools DiskClean, measured)
findings.problem:
MacTools Disk Cleanup (ggbond268/MacTools@bf6550a, GPL-3.0, study only) sizes each cleanup candidate with **one** thread. `DiskCleanDirectoryTreeWalker.walk()` is a serial explicit-stack DFS (`DiskCleanDirectoryTreeWalker.swift:90-191`). Concurrency exists only *across* candidates, at most 3 at a time (`DiskCleanScanEngine.swift:58`, `DiskCleanWorkerPool.swift:84`). Every candidate gets a hard wall-clock budget of 20 s (`DiskCleanScanEngine.swift:54`, :556-565). When the budget runs out, the walker returns `partial([.timedOut])`. A partial size is **not cleanable**: `DiskCleanCandidate.isCleanable` requires `sizeResult.completeness.isComplete` (`DiskCleanModels.swift:324-327`). The Planner and the executor enforce the same rule (`DiskCleanPlan.swift:183`). The UI shows the row as "Timed out" (`DiskCleanDetailView.swift:624-625`), and a rescan hits the same wall.

Measured throughput of MacTools' own `DiskCleanFastWalker` on this Mac (M1, 8 GB, `kern.maxvnodes` 120,350, load avg 3-12). The probe is `research/bench/ggbond268-mactools/walker_throughput_main.swift`, built from the unmodified sources:
- 728k-file tree larger than the vnode cache: 21.25 s and 18.32 s, which is **34-40k files/s**. So the 20 s cap is reached at about **0.7-0.8M files**.
- 23k-file tree in cache: 160-190k files/s, which puts the cap at about 3.2-3.8M files.

So the largest single cache folders are exactly the ones MacTools can never clean. Examples are a Yarn/npm/Gradle cache or a big `~/Library/Caches/<app>` folder, especially on a loaded or cold machine. The cleaner then drops the biggest wins with no way to override. When 3 threads compete for the same disk, each one is slower, which lowers the threshold further. **Unverified:** how many real users have one cache folder above that size. The largest cache folder on this Mac holds 28k entries (`.gradle/wrapper`).

The wall-clock budget has a second cost. `DiskCleanWorkerPool.handleTimeout` (:265-321) uses the **same** deadline to decide that a thread is stuck in a syscall. It abandons the thread, blacklists its device for the life of the process, and after 3 abandons it stops all sizing. A cooperative walk normally notices its deadline first (`research/bench/ggbond268-mactools/pool_timeout_probe_main.swift`: the walker won 10 of 10 races at 0.25 s). A single slow batch, such as a dataless folder or a cold disk, can still lose the race, and then the whole Data volume is refused until relaunch.

Neighbour: F-0009 is about serial walkers being slow. This finding is about the design that turns a slow size into "cannot clean".
findings.before:
ggbond268/MacTools@bf6550a:

`DiskCleanScanEngine.swift:53-58`

    /// Per-item deadline (design §4.2 item 3). Timeout → `partial([.timedOut])`.
    var itemTimeout: TimeInterval = 20
    var globalTimeout: TimeInterval = 300
    var maximumConcurrentSizing: Int = 3

`DiskCleanModels.swift:324-327`

    var isCleanable: Bool {
        guard safety.isCleanable, let sizeResult else { return false }
        return sizeResult.completeness.isComplete && sizeResult.rootIdentity != nil
    }

`DiskCleanDirectoryTreeWalker.swift:121-126`, a single-thread DFS that stops on the wall clock:

    while let frame = stack.last {
        if context.shouldStop {            // isCancelled() || now() >= deadline
            accumulator.add(.timedOut)
            break

Probe output (`MAIN=walker_throughput_main.swift pool_timeout_probe.sh ~/projects 120`):

    files=728063 bytes=37697480310 elapsed=21.25s files/s=34270
    files=728735 bytes=37707222878 elapsed=18.32s files/s=39773
findings.after:
In macontrol, "how big is it" and "may we delete it" are two separate questions, and sizing is limited by progress, not by the clock.

1. **Parallel sizing inside a candidate.** The bounded work-stealing directory pool from F-0009 walks directories from all candidates, with one accumulator per candidate. MacTools' own StorageExplorer already walks with `DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform`. A single huge cache folder then uses every worker, not one.
2. **Stall watchdog instead of a wall-clock budget.** Each walker bumps a progress counter per `getattrlistbulk` batch. The watchdog abandons a worker only when the counter has not moved for N seconds (for example 10 s). A healthy walk of 5M files is never cut. A stuck syscall is still caught, and only then is the device fenced.
3. **A size cut short is still cleanable after review.** If the user stops sizing or the watchdog fires, the row shows "at least X GB (not fully counted)" and stays selectable. It is never pre-selected. Deletion safety comes from the execute-time gate, not from the scan: fd-anchored identity check, then a prewalk that stops at `ATTR_DIR_MOUNTSTATUS` mount points (see F-0031) and at unreadable subfolders, then the move to Trash.

findings.title: Cask zap data is not 'exact': 272 paths in 217 casks trash user work (~/eclipse-workspace, ~/Music/Ableton, iCloud Drive folders) and 290 are shared by 2+ products (Word trashes Edge's Microsoft folder); brew applies all with no ownership check (Homebrew cask, measured)
findings.where: homebrew-cask Casks/*/*.rb zap stanzas via brew Library/Homebrew/cask/artifact/abstract_uninstall.rb uninstall_trash/uninstall_pkgutil; cask/installer.rb:311
findings.problem:
The Homebrew cask `zap` data is the best curated leftover list available (BSD-2-Clause), but it is not an "exact, safe to preselect" list. By design it mixes three kinds of path: the app's own leftovers, folders that hold the user's own work, and resources that other products share. Homebrew applies all of them the same way, with no ownership check. F-0011's "after" currently puts "cask zap path" in the **exact, preselected** tier, and that would preselect all of the paths below.

Sources: feed https://formulae.brew.sh/api/cask.json (Last-Modified 2026-09-23 07:42:02 GMT, etag "6ab382ca-120c57b"), Homebrew/homebrew-cask@0e47c3a, Homebrew/brew@570982948a. Counted by `research/bench/homebrew-homebrew-cask/analyze_zap.py`, with the inline scripts quoted under "how".

**The policy allows it.** `docs/Cask-Cookbook.md:1357-1364` (brew): zap "may remove ... Shared resources such as application updaters. Since shared resources may be removed, other applications may be affected by `brew uninstall --zap`. Understanding that is the responsibility of the end user." The only exclusion is "Files created by the user directly." Reviewers enforce that exclusion by hand, and the data shows it is not enforced consistently.

**User-content roots (measured):** 272 `trash`/`delete` zap paths in 217 casks point into folders that hold user work:
- `/Users/Shared`: 73
- `~/Documents`: 69
- `~/Music`: 19
- `~/Pictures`: 7
- `~/Desktop`: 6
- `~/Movies`: 5
- `~/Library/Mobile Documents` (iCloud Drive): 5
- non-dot folders directly under ~: 88

Examples:
- `Casks/e/eclipse-java.rb:24` `"~/eclipse-workspace"` is Eclipse's default workspace, where the user's projects live. It appears in 6 Eclipse casks.
- `Casks/a/ableton-live-suite.rb:33-35` `"~/Music/Ableton"`, `"~/Documents/Max [0-9]"`, `"/Users/Shared/Max [0-9]"` are the Ableton User Library, recordings and Max patches.
- `Casks/f/fxfactory.rb:39` `"~/Movies/Motion Templates.localized"` is the templates folder of Apple Motion and Final Cut Pro, not only FxFactory's.
- `Casks/o/omnigraffle.rb:48` `"~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~com~omnigroup~OmniGraffle"` is the app's iCloud Drive folder. Moving it to the Trash removes the documents from iCloud Drive on every signed-in device. iCloud's 30-day "Recently Deleted" is the only way back (not verified here).

**Shared with other products (measured):** 290 literal zap paths (no glob) are trashed or deleted by 2 or more distinct products (base token, with `@variant` suffixes merged). Examples:
- `~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft`: `Casks/m/microsoft-word.rb:62` trashes it. `microsoft-edge.rb:45-46` and `microsoft-teams` only `rmdir` it (remove it if empty), because Edge and Teams keep data there.
- `~/.conda` + `~/.condarc`: anaconda, miniconda, miniforge.
- `~/.android` (the emulator AVDs): android-studio, android-cli, android-commandlinetools, android-studio-preview.
- `~/Library/Application Support/Ableton`: 4 Live editions.

The same pattern exists in the default `uninstall`, without `--zap`. 78 `pkgutil`/`launchctl` IDs are listed by 2 or more products. `microsoft-word.rb:51-56` removes receipt `com.microsoft.pkg.licensing` and job `com.microsoft.office.licensingV2.helper`, and 5 other Office casks list the same IDs (`microsoft-excel.rb:51,55`).

**No ownership check when applied.** `uninstall_trash` / `uninstall_pkgutil` (`Library/Homebrew/cask/artifact/abstract_uninstall.rb:592-626`) act on every resolved path and receipt. The installer passes `@default_uninstall_artifacts || @cask.artifacts` (`cask/installer.rb:311`), and the only caller that restricts that set is the rename migrator (`cask/migrator.rb:116`). The only path guard is an exact-match set (`cask/macos.rb:241-379`). It stops `~/Documents` itself but not `~/Documents/Max 8`, and the TODO at `:239-240` says so: "There should be a way to specify a containing directory under which nothing can be deleted."

findings.after:
macontrol imports the cask data as **hints with an ownership class**. A cask path is never preselected just because it is in the data. The class is computed once, at rule-build time, and stored in the shipped rules JSON. Every hint is still existence-checked on the user's disk.

1. **user-content**: the path is under `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, `~/Downloads`, `~/Movies`, `~/Music`, `~/Pictures`, `~/Public`, `/Users/Shared` or `~/Library/Mobile Documents`, or it is a non-dot folder directly under `~`.
   - Never preselected.
   - Shown in its own section, "Files you made with <App>", with size and Reveal in Finder, and never included in "Select all".
   - `~/Library/Mobile Documents/*` also carries the note "removes these documents from iCloud Drive on all your devices".
2. **shared**: the path is trashed or deleted by 2 or more products in the data (base token), another cask `rmdir`s it, or it is a vendor folder that does not contain the app's name or bundle ID.
   - Preselected only when no other *installed* app claims it. Installed apps are resolved by bundle ID and app name against the same data.
   - Otherwise it is shown unticked, with "also used by Microsoft Excel".
3. **own**: the path contains the app's bundle ID or app name and nothing else claims it. Preselected.

Receipts and launchd jobs in the data get the same treatment:
- A `pkgutil` ID listed by another installed app's cask is not forgotten or removed.
- Files are removed from a receipt only when no other receipt lists them. This is the reference-counting that munki does in `rmpkgs.swift:373-390` (see T-0005).

This replaces "cask zap path: exact, preselected" in F-0011's tiers. Only class 3 is exact.
findings.how:
- The rule builder (`tools/build-cask-rules`, Python, runs in CI) reads `cask.json` and writes `rules/cask-hints.json`: `{token, bundleIds[], appNames[], paths:[{p, kind: trash|delete|rmdir, cls: own|shared|user}], pkgutil[], launchctl[]}`.
  - The classes come from the counts above. `research/bench/homebrew-homebrew-cask/analyze_zap.py` already computes the shared-path and user-root sets, so it is the starting point.
  - Filter `variations` to macOS tags only (drop `*_linux`).
  - Keep the BSD-2 notice ("Copyright (c) 2013, Paul Hinze & Contributors") in Acknowledgements.
- The CI acceptance test uses a fixture HOME with `~/Music/Ableton/Project.als`, `~/eclipse-workspace/app/src/Main.java`, `~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft/Edge-data` and `~/Library/Preferences/com.ableton.live.plist`. It "installs" ableton-live-lite + ableton-live-suite and microsoft-word + microsoft-edge (fake bundles with the right bundle IDs), then plans an uninstall of ableton-live-lite and of microsoft-word. Expected:
  - only `com.ableton.live.plist`-type own paths are preselected;
  - `~/Music/Ableton` and `~/eclipse-workspace` are listed as user-content and unticked;
  - `Application Support/Microsoft` is unticked with "also used by Microsoft Edge".
- To reproduce the counts, run `python3 research/bench/homebrew-homebrew-cask/analyze_zap.py > zap_stats.json`. The relevant keys are `user_content_trash_paths*`, `trash_paths_of_2plus_products*`, `trashed_by_one_rmdired_by_another` and `uninstall_ids_of_2plus_products`. The committed output is `research/bench/homebrew-homebrew-cask/zap_stats.json`.
- Nothing was run against a real HOME. This is data plus code reading. The fixture test above is the runtime check.

Its own search never leaves Library folders and holds back shared items with a note. CaskOracleTests plants every zap path of 20 casks and requires nothing outside Library to be found (~/.vscode etc.), while shared vendor items (Google Keystone, Mozilla crash reporter) are not attributed; recall floor 133/169 shown, 113 preselected. findings.title: Wildcard launchctl entries resolve only against running jobs in the user's own launchctl list, unanchored: stopped agents and root daemons are skipped silently, a label that merely contains the pattern is removed (brew, verified with its own resolver)
findings.problem:
In the cask data, a launchd label containing `*` (for example `com.paragon-software.ntfs*`) is resolved by `find_launchctl_with_wildcard`. That function reads `launchctl list` **as the calling user** and keeps only rows whose PID is non-zero. It then matches the label with an **unanchored** regex. The results:
- a stopped agent (PID `-`) is never found;
- a root LaunchDaemon, which the user's `launchctl list` does not show, is never found;
- an unrelated label that merely *contains* the pattern is found.

Nothing is reported for the missed jobs. `next if found_services.blank?` skips them silently, and only the jobs that were found get `launchctl remove` and their `<label>.plist` deleted.

Citations are Homebrew/brew@570982948a, `Library/Homebrew/cask/artifact/abstract_uninstall.rb`:
- `:173-181`: `system_command!("/bin/launchctl", args: ["list"])` with no sudo, then `id if pid.to_i.nonzero? && id&.match?(regex)`. `"-".to_i` is 0, so every stopped job is dropped.
- `:174` + `:362-365`: `wildcard_pattern` returns an unanchored fragment, and `String#match?` searches anywhere in the label.
- `:343-358`: `quit:`/`signal:` wildcards, by contrast, are anchored ("Anchored so that e.g. `com.example*` cannot match `org.other.com.example`"). Commit f281e43a1c (2026-08-19, "cask/artifact: tighten uninstall wildcard safety") added that anchoring for quit/signal only, and launchctl stayed unanchored.
- `:222-230`: when the wildcard finds nothing, no warning is printed.
- Tests: `test/cask/artifact/shared_examples/uninstall_zap.rb:91-150`. The fixture's matching rows are all running. The test "searches installed launchctl items" stubs `find_launchctl_with_wildcard` itself, so the domain/state gap is never exercised.

**Verified by running brew's own method** (`research/bench/homebrew-homebrew-cask/wildcard_probe.rb`, with `brew ruby` and a fake `launchctl list`, so no system state was read or changed):

    com.wacom.TabletDriver*
      brew resolves : ["com.wacom.TabletDriverUI", "org.other.com.wacom.TabletDriverHelper"]
      exists (anchored, any state): ["com.wacom.TabletDriver.agent", "com.wacom.TabletDriverUI"]
    com.paragon-software.ntfs*
      brew resolves : []
      exists (anchored, any state): ["com.paragon-software.ntfs.notification-agent"]

**On this Mac (read-only):** `launchctl list` as the user shows 527 jobs. 333 of them are stopped (PID `-`), and brew's wildcard can never match those. `com.apple.mDNSResponder` (a system daemon) appears 0 times in that list and 5 times in `launchctl print system`.

**Where it applies:** the feed has 26 wildcard launchctl patterns in 22 casks. 11 of them are `application.<bundle id>.*` app-instance jobs, where "running only" is intended. The other 15, in 12 casks, name real agents or daemons: paragon-ntfs, paragon-extfs, wacom-tablet, elgato-stream-deck, krisp, pearcleaner, adobe-creative-cloud, fantastical, rockxy, spotify, intune-company-portal. For `paragon-ntfs.rb:22` (`uninstall launchctl: "com.paragon-software.ntfs*"`) the wildcard is the cask's only launchctl directive.

In the current data, the unanchored overmatch hits only another cask of the same vendor (paragon-extfs@11 → `com.paragon-software.extfsd`), so the practical defect is the miss. This class is separate from F-0023 (no bootout at all) and F-0055 (a stale literal label).

findings.after:
macontrol resolves an app's launchd jobs from **what is on disk and loaded in every domain, whatever their state**, and matches patterns **anchored**:

1. **Candidates from disk.** List the `*.plist` files in `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, `/Library/LaunchAgents` and `/Library/LaunchDaemons`. Read `Label`, `Program` / `ProgramArguments[0]` and `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` with `PropertyListSerialization`. Do not trust the file name: a plist's name can differ from its label (F-0055).
2. **Candidates from launchd.** Read `launchctl print gui/<uid>` and `launchctl print system` (read-only, no root needed). Add the Background Task Management / SMAppService items of the target bundle. Loaded jobs whose plist lives elsewhere are covered this way.
3. **Match.**
   - Match a rule label or cask pattern as `\A<escaped, * -> .*>\z` against `Label`.
   - Also claim any job whose program path is inside the app bundle being removed, or whose `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` contains its bundle ID.
   - Keep the lint from brew's own cop: a wildcard needs at least 3 ID parts (`rubocops/cask/uninstall_wildcard.rb:13`).
   - A stopped job is a match like any other.
4. **Report.** Every rule pattern that matched nothing is shown in the review sheet as "expected a background item <pattern>, none found". It is not skipped silently.
5. Teardown (bootout, then trash the plist) follows F-0023.

- `LaunchJobResolver.candidates() -> [Job(label, plistURL?, domain, program, associatedBundleIDs, state)]` has one pure matcher, `matches(pattern:, job:)`. Unit-test the matcher with the probe's rows:

  - `com.paragon-software.ntfs*` must match `com.paragon-software.ntfs.notification-agent` (stopped).
- Integration: `research/bench/uninstall-oracle/launchd_probe.sh` (from F-0023) with the fixture agent *not loaded*. The resolver must still list its plist.
- Reproduce brew's behaviour with `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew ruby research/bench/homebrew-homebrew-cask/wildcard_probe.rb`. Note that `brew ruby` turns on Homebrew developer mode; run `brew developer off` afterwards. Pattern counts come from `analyze_zap.py` (key `wildcard_launchctl`).

findings.title: Zap paths freeze one version: 630 zap lines in 179 casks interpolate #{version...}, the feed resolves them (PyCharm2026.2), so every earlier version's settings/caches/logs stay behind (Homebrew cask, measured)
findings.where: homebrew-cask Casks/*/*.rb zap stanzas (e.g. Casks/p/pycharm.rb:36-45); brew Library/Homebrew/cask/cask.rb:612-660 to_hash_with_variations
findings.problem:
Many cask `zap` stanzas build a folder name from the cask's current version. The API feed evaluates the DSL, so each such path is frozen to the single version the feed was generated for. Data that earlier majors or minors left behind never matches: `brew uninstall --zap`, or any tool that reuses the feed literally, leaves it on disk. IDEs and pro apps keep a separate settings, cache, index and log tree per version, so these are often the largest leftovers an app has.

- **Source:** `Casks/p/pycharm.rb:36-45` (Homebrew/homebrew-cask@0e47c3a) has `"~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/PyCharm#{version.major_minor}"`, and the same pattern for `Caches/JetBrains`, `Logs/JetBrains` and `Preferences`.
- **Feed:** `pycharm` → `"~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/PyCharm2026.2"` (cask.json, Last-Modified 2026-09-23 07:42:02 GMT). Nothing in the feed marks that `2026.2` was a version. A user who used 2025.3 and upgraded keeps `.../JetBrains/PyCharm2025.3`, `Caches/JetBrains/PyCharm2025.3` and `Logs/JetBrains/PyCharm2025.3`.
- **The evaluation step:** `Cask#to_hash_with_variations` (`Library/Homebrew/cask/cask.rb:612-660`, brew@570982948a) serializes the evaluated artifacts. `api_hashable.rb:5-19` swaps only HOME and HOMEBREW_PREFIX for placeholders, and version strings are not touched.
- **Scale (measured over all 7,755 `Casks/**/*.rb` at 0e47c3a):** 630 zap path lines in 179 casks interpolate a version:
  - `#{version.major}`: 478
  - `#{version.major_minor}`: 89
  - `#{version.csv.first.major}`: 20
  - `#{version}`: 10
  - others: the rest

  In the feed, 111 zap paths in 40 casks contain the current major.minor literally (android-studio `Google/AndroidStudio2026.1`, rider, pycharm, affinity-*, ...).
- On this Mac, none of the 40 casks' older-version folders exist, so the size impact was not measured here. JetBrains per-version caches reaching multiple GB is common, but unverified.
